title: Piero Cipollone: Interview with Milano Finanza
body:
Interview with Milano Finanza Skip to: Skip to navigation Skip to content Skip to footer EN Български Čeština Dansk Deutsch Eλληνικά English Español Eesti keel Suomi Français Gaeilge Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Lietuvių Latviešu Malti Nederlands Polski Português Română Slovenčina Slovenščina Svenska Menu Search Menu ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Search Options Image Preview Sort by ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Suggestions Home Media Explainers Research & Publications Statistics Monetary Policy The €uro Payments & Markets Careers Suggestions Sort by Relevance Date Piero Cipollone Member of the ECB's Executive Board INTERVIEW Interview with Milano Finanza Interview with Piero Cipollone, Member of the Executive Board of the ECB, conducted by Roberto Sommella on 21 October 2026 24 October 2026 Mr Cipollone, you have just attended a meeting of the Executive Committee of the Italian Banking Association. Was the digital euro one of the topics discussed? We mainly talked about tokenisation. On the subject of the digital euro, I provided an update on the status of the debates on the legislation in Brussels and on the progress of our internal preparations within the Eurosystem. Since you joined the ECB, payments have become one of the main focus areas of your work. Why are they so important for Europe’s future? Because payments constitute a strategic infrastructure for Europe and, as a central bank, ensuring the smooth functioning of payment systems falls within our mandate. Whenever we buy something online or pay for a coffee, we think about the price of what we’re buying. But we hardly ever think about how the payment is made. Yet if the payment system stops working, the economy stops working. Will the introduction of the digital euro help with this? Yes. Today we can use money issued by the central bank only in the form of cash. But a growing share of our economic life takes place online, where banknotes can’t be used. The digital euro fills this gap. It gives people the freedom to make payments using an instrument that is equivalent to cash in terms of its nature and characteristics, such as privacy and covering all payment needs, but which also works where cash can’t be used. Why has this now become necessary? Ever more purchases are being made online. In Italy, for example, according to the latest available data, online payments grew from 6% of the total in 2019 to 24% in 2024. And I expect they’ve grown even more since then. These online purchases are normally made via card payments and two thirds of these payments are made using non-European card schemes. For most euro area countries, this dependence on non-European operators is not limited to online payments but also extends to physical shops, because they don’t even have anything like Italy’s Bancomat that would enable payments to be made in local shops. In short, for an essential service like payments, we are heavily dependent on an infrastructure over which we have no direct control. So can the digital euro be described as a European digital sovereignty project? The Eurosystem focuses on matters that are closely related to its mandate. And, as I said at the start, the smooth functioning of payment systems is one of our responsibilities. If we are critically dependent on third parties, it’s not easy to ensure this smooth functioning. In recent years Europe has learned that, for some essential services, we cannot rely only on third parties. We saw this with energy and we’re seeing it today with defence. And the same is true for payments. The digital euro will give Europe an alternative of its own, bringing to the digital world what cash has always ensured: a secure form of public money that protects privacy and is accepted throughout the euro area. Sovereignty doesn’t mean shutting third parties out. It means having the power to choose and knowing that, for an essential service like payments, Europe can also rely on its own strength. Does this dependency bring any specific consequences for merchants too? Yes, particularly for small merchants. Today the fees that a small shop pays can be up to four times higher than those paid by large operators. The digital euro will introduce a European alternative that will increase competition and, thanks to the caps on costs laid down by law, will help to reduce fees for those with less bargaining power. From this perspective, it seems that there’s no time to waste. Absolutely. In 2027 we will already launch a pilot based on real transactions carried out by the staff of the ECB and the other national central banks. It will serve to test the technology in real conditions and to build the digital euro hand-in-hand with the market. 36 market operators, of which seven are Italian, are already collaborating in the preparatory works. And we are now calling for e-commerce and mobile commerce operators to take part. If the regulation is approved this year, the digital euro could be rolled out as early as 2029. When will the final decision be taken? The decision can only be taken once the legislative negotiations that are under way in Brussels have been concluded. We hope that the regulation will be adopted by the end of the year, enabling the ECB’s Governing Council to issue a formal decision on issuance. The adoption of the regulation will make it possible to complete the rulebook with the technical rules necessary for the market to prepare ahead of time. The ECB can get the infrastructure ready, but banks, payment system operators and merchants will also need time to adapt their systems and processes. Will there be a limit on holdings of digital euro? Yes, but there won’t be limits on payments. The limit applies to how much digital euro I can hold in a digital wallet, not how much I can spend. If a payment exceeds the available balance – when buying a car, for example – it will be possible to take the remainder automatically from the linked current account. The limit on the amount of digital euro that can be held will safeguard financial stability, particularly in crisis situations. Our analyses show that with a properly calibrated limit, there will be no negative effects on the banking system. Is it true that it will also work offline? Yes. It will be possible to make payments in shops during a power cut or in remote and isolated areas where there’s no internet connection or where the connection is weak and sporadic. It will suffice to bring two devices together, as when using a contactless card today. The payment will be made directly between the payor and payee, without going via the internet. It means merchants can keep receiving payments even when other digital payment methods are not available. This will make the digital euro more resilient and will also better protect privacy. With offline payments, details of the transaction remain exclusively between the payor and the payee, very much like cash payments today. How exactly will we be able to use the digital euro? Will a new app be available? There will be two options. Banks will be able to integrate the digital euro into the apps their clients already use, while the Eurosystem will offer an easy-to-use, standardised, reliable app with the basic functions. Even if you use the latter option, your relationship will nevertheless still be with your own bank; the ECB will not open accounts for people. But what will this European app be used for? Just as banknotes are the same throughout the euro area, the digital euro app will also offer a common point of access. The digital euro must be accessible to everyone, regardless of their country, their age or their digital skills. We have incorporated accessibility from the design stage onwards, and have been working with organisations representing those with disabilities. We are implementing a clear principle set out in the European Commission's legislative proposal, i.e. the choice of how to access and use the digital euro should remain in users’ hands and not be controlled by payment service providers. Will the ECB decide how much digital euro will be issued, based on a limit set each year, just like it does for banknotes and coins? No. As is the case for cash, it will be up to citizens and firms to determine the digital euro’s use based on demand. On which technological platform will the digital euro run? It will run on a common European infrastructure developed exclusively by European providers, on which banks and private operators will be able to build new services. We’ve already seen this in our innovation programmes: more than 70 operators worked with the ECB to explore the options the digital euro offers to provide new services to their customers. Some firms have already put forward solutions, such as automatic digital receipts or automatic payment upon delivery for online purchases. These are tangible innovations that will make life easier for people and firms. We have just launched a second call for new ideas and projects, with the aim of speeding up innovation and creating new growth opportunities for the European payments industry. Banks have complained because they are afraid of being left out of the digital euro loop. Are their fears justified? Dialogue with the banking sector has been, and continues to be, an essential component of the project. The digital euro has not been devised as a replacement for banks, but to integrate and strengthen their own payment services. It will in fact be the banks and other authorised intermediaries that will distribute the digital euro, manage customer relationships and develop new services. The digital euro’s common standards will enable payment solutions developed in Europe to reach customers and merchants throughout the euro area. Is it conceivable that one day there will only be the digital euro? I don’t think so, and I don’t think that’s what anyone is aiming for. The goal is to create a payment system in which cash, the digital euro and the services already offered by banks coexist in such a way that resilience will be guaranteed and consumers will have freedom of choice. How can cyberattacks be prevented? The digital euro’s security will be built on multiple layers: advanced encryption, data segregation and regular testing for simulated attacks. The infrastructure will also be distributed across several European regions to ensure continuity of service even if part of the system were to become temporarily unavailable Security is not an afterthought, but an integral requirement built into the project from the very start. We can draw on the Eurosystem’s wealth of experience in managing critical infrastructure such as TARGET. Will we be able to buy everything with the digital euro, such as a coffee, a government bond or even a share? The digital euro will be a means of payment, not a tool that the ECB will be able to use to tell people how to spend their own money. People will be able to use it to buy a coffee, shop online, pay a bill or even transfer money to somebody else. In short, the digital euro will be available for in-store, online and person-to-person payments. The ECB is a federal institution. What is still missing from the European Union for it to become truly complete and stronger from a financial perspective? Europe already has a single currency and a single central bank. Now we must complete the process through the creation of a genuine European capital market, a more integrated banking system and common infrastructure in strategic sectors. Today, Europeans' savings far exceed the financing needs of our firms, but a significant portion of those savings ends up outside Europe, while many European firms struggle to find the capital they need to grow, innovate and compete. We need to find a way of ensuring European savings do more to finance the European economy. A start-up or an innovative small business should be able to access not just capital from its own country but available capital from anywhere in Europe with ease. To achieve this, there is work to be done on several fronts, including legal, regulatory and technological. On the technological front, we have a real opportunity: new technologies such as distributed ledger technologies (DLTs) allow us to overcome the fragmentation of market infrastructures. The Eurosystem is making a concerted effort towards this through the Pontes project, which went live on 21 September 2026. It enables the settlement of financial transactions carried out on DLT platforms using central bank money. Its complementary project, Appia, aims to create a fully integrated European financial ecosystem. The common theme is the same as for the digital euro: we have a single currency, but in many sectors we still have fragmented national markets and infrastructures. Completing the European capital market would mean that citizens and firms could truly take advantage of the opportunities offered by a market operating on a continental scale. title: See what 5 builders are making with Gemini 4 Argon
body: See what 5 builders are making with Gemini 4 Argon Oct 23, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Our newest model is ready to handle your most ambitious projects. See how the community's putting it to work — and get inspired for your next build. Kimberly Fusaro Contributor Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Read AI-generated summary Google just released a powerful new AI model called Gemini 4 Argon. It’s great at handling complicated tasks like coding, math, and building 3D worlds. People are already using it to create everything from interactive globes to multiplayer video games. It’s a huge step up for anyone who wants to build complex projects quickly. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Gemini 4 Argon , our new frontier model, excels at tackling complex projects. Argon excels at deep work in complex, real-world tasks to help across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Its depth and precision across multi-step tasks leads Argon to outperform other frontier models on benchmarks across domains. Since we rolled out Argon broadly last week, we've seen builders tap into its expanded abilities to create interactive tools, engineer 3D worlds, and more. These five builds from the community — including a globe that maps tectonic shockwaves in real time and a 3D multiplayer game — are some of our favorites so far. Simulate a seaplane on water. With major upgrades in spatial reasoning, mathematical precision, and visual coding, Gemini 4 Argon can generate complex 3D environments. In this test by Lumina (@LuminaBench on X) , Argon rendered a 3D simulation of a seaplane with realistic lighting, reflections, and water movement. Because Argon can maintain depth and precision across multi-step tasks, it was able to coordinate the motions of different elements simultaneously. Map wildfires and tectonic shockwaves on a 3D globe. Gemini 4 Argon excels at turning dense, unstructured data into clear visuals. Using Gemini 4 Argon in Antigravity, Alex Patrascu (@maxescu on X) combined NASA's live feed of global wildfires and seismic data from the U.S. Geological Survey to create an interactive 3D globe. Argon's frontier reasoning across domains like coding allowed it to parse data, map coordinates, and render animated shockwaves and hotspots. Engineer an interactive jet engine. Using Gemini 4 Argon with Blender and Three.js, Ashutosh Shrivastava (@ai_for_success on X) generated a detailed simulation of a high-bypass turbofan jet engine with live measurements and data and part-by-part specs. With enhanced capabilities across coding and the ability to sustain long, multi-step tasks, Argon was able to model individual elements before rendering them together in a 3D environment. Build a 3D carriage from a single image. Gemini 4 Argon has the ability to bring flat image files to life. The Bugged Dev (@thebuggeddev on X) gave Argon a single image of a Gothic Victorian carriage and asked it to build the whole thing as an interactive 3D experience. Argon translated the image into a complex rendering with functioning doors and windows, flickering oil lamps, and an undercarriage that reacts to bumps in the road. Create a multiplayer capture-the-flag game. Chong-U (@chongdashu on X) used Gemini 4 Argon to build “Backyard Rascals,” a multiplayer browser game where cartoon animals race to capture the other team’s flag. Argon's ability to maintain depth and precision across complex workflows helped this creator build a game with complex features allowing the characters to run, collide, whack each other, and cheer as multiple players engage in real time. Gemini 4 Argon is now globally available for developers and enterprises via the API in AI Studio and Gemini platform , for Google AI Ultra and paid Pro subscribers in Google Antigravity , and Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search . title: Convicted Felon Sentenced to Twelve Years in Federal Prison for Drug Trafficking and Firearm Offenses
body: Press Release Convicted Felon Sentenced to Twelve Years in Federal Prison for Drug Trafficking and Firearm Offenses Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Pensacola, Florida – Scott Oranje, 52, of Mary Esther, Florida, has been sentenced to 12 years in federal prison after pleading guilty to possession with intent to distribute more than 40 grams of fentanyl, possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking offense, and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida announced the sentence. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “I am proud that my office has delivered yet another successful prosecution in our fight to eliminate the operations of armed drug traffickers in this district.  President Donald J. Trump rightly designated fentanyl as a weapon of mass destruction because of the devastation it can wreak, especially in the quantities possessed by this trafficker. Our citizens deserve to live in safe, drug-free communities, and my office will continue to aggressively prosecute these cases until we deliver on that promise.” Court documents reflect that on November 10, 2025, law enforcement officers intercepted a package addressed to the defendant’s residence that contained over 300 grams of fentanyl. Law enforcement thereafter conducted a controlled delivery at the defendant’s residence, and the defendant took possession of the package and entered his condominium. Shortly thereafter, law enforcement officers executed a search warrant on the residence. The defendant did not answer the door requiring officers to breach the door, after which the defendant fled through the back patio with the fentanyl. The defendant was caught and taken into custody, and a subsequent search of his residence located a digital scale, various narcotics paraphernalia, owe sheets documenting transaction records, and multiple firearms. The defendant had previously been convicted of First-Degree Residential Robbery and sentenced to state prison in California on or about July 30, 2018, and was therefore legally prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition as a felon. “This career criminal possessed enough potential deadly doses of fentanyl to decimate the population of a mid-sized city,” said DEA Special Agent in Charge Daniel Escobar, Tampa Field Division. “Our agents and law enforcement partners did a great job bringing this case to a successful conclusion.” “The United States Postal Inspection Service is committed to ensuring that the mail system is not used to deliver fentanyl and other poisons into our communities,” said Bladismir Rojo, Inspector in Charge, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Miami Division. “The stiff sentence handed down in this case should serve as a warning to others that you will be prosecuted.” The case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Okaloosa County Sheriff’s Office, and the United States Postal Inspection Service. Assistant United States Attorneys Christopher C. Patterson and Thomas S.P. Geeker prosecuted the case. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General.  To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl . title: HAM Crazy Gang Member Sentenced to 168 Months’ Imprisonment for Being a Felon in Possession of a Firearm
body: Press Release HAM Crazy Gang Member Sentenced to 168 Months’ Imprisonment for Being a Felon in Possession of a Firearm Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Minnesota MINNEAPOLIS – United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen announced that Casey Jemar Davis, 32, was sentenced to 168 months in prison for being a felon in possession of a firearm. Davis was sentenced before Chief U.S. District Judge Eric C. Tostrud on October 22, 2026. Chief Judge Tostrud also imposed 24 months’ imprisonment consecutive to the 168-month sentence for Davis violating his terms of federal supervised release from a 2018 federal firearms-related conviction. (The 168-month sentence included a 12-month credit from the statutory maximum of 180 months to account for the time Davis had already served in custody.) According to court documents, on July 28, 2022, at approximately 1:30 a.m., Davis was involved in a verbal altercation with Person 1 and several other men. Davis and the men were standing next to an SUV in the parking lot of a sports bar near the corner of North 4th Street and North 1st Avenue in downtown Minneapolis, after a fight that occurred inside the bar. Davis possessed a .40-caliber Glock firearm equipped with a switch and an inserted high-capacity magazine. The switch on Davis’s firearm is a machinegun conversion device that enabled the firearm to fire in fully automatic mode with a single trigger pull. Davis’s firearm with a high-capacity magazine Davis’s firearm with a switch convertor Person 1, co-defendant Cleveland Longmire, and another person with Person 1, were also in possession of firearms. Surveillance video showed that Person 1 held a firearm in his right hand that was pointed to the ground. Longmire raised his firearm and discharged it towards the ground near Person 1. As Person 1 turned and began to run away, Davis shot Person 1 with Davis’s firearm in the back, legs, and arms multiple times, killing Person 1. Two innocent bystanders in the parking lot were also hit by Davis’s gunfire. Davis and Longmire then placed their firearms under the driver’s seat of the SUV. Davis got in another vehicle and drove away from the scene as police arrived, while Longmire walked away from the scene. During a warrant-authorized search of the SUV, police located the two firearms under the driver’s seat and Longmire’s ID on the driver’s seat. Law enforcement recovered over twenty .40-caliber casings from the parking lot that were forensically determined to have been fired from Davis’s firearm, and three 9mm casings that were determined to have been fired from Longmire’s firearm. Person 1’s firearm was not fired. Davis’s and Longmire’s firearms under the seat of the SUV Davis was on fugitive warrant status for nearly two-and-one-half years. On or about February 20, 2025, police located and arrested Davis in St. Paul, Minnesota, on state and federal charges related to the July 28, 2022, shooting. At the time of his arrest, Davis possessed another firearm also equipped with a switch and an extended magazine. Davis’s additional firearm that was found during his February 2025 arrest Davis has multiple prior felony convictions, including the June 2018 federal conviction for a firearms-related offense, for which he was previously sentenced to 50 months’ imprisonment, and for which he was on federal supervised release for about six months at the time of the July 2022 shooting. In January 2026, Davis was sentenced to 294 months’ imprisonment in Hennepin County District Court after pleading guilty to second-degree unintentional murder for the July 2022 killing of Person 1, and to two counts of second-degree assault with a dangerous weapon. Davis’s co-defendant, Cleveland Longmire, was previously sentenced to 90 months in prison on January 9, 2024. Both Davis and Longmire are known members of the HAM Crazy criminal street gang, which has a long history of endangering the lives and safety of innocent bystanders and the community because many of the shootings they were involved in occurred in public venues. During the sentencing hearing, Chief Judge Tostrud noted that Davis’s conduct was “brutal, inhumane, and sadistic,” and found that Davis represents a “great threat to public safety” and acted with “total disregard for the law and the safety of the community.” “This defendant had no regard for life and killed a man while shooting his firearm in a crowded place. This case reflects the strong partnership between federal and local law enforcement to protect public safety,” said United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen. “The Minneapolis Police Department is grateful to U.S. Attorney Daniel N. Rosen and his office and to Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty and her office for their partnership in bringing Davis to justice. Davis fired a machine gun into a crowd, killing one person and injuring two others. His utter disregard for the sanctity of human life warrants the highest federal sentence allowed by law in addition to the sentence already given in Hennepin County,” said Minneapolis Police Department Interim Chief Bill Peterson. “Today’s sentencing holds the defendant accountable for firing more than 20 rounds from a firearm equipped with a machinegun conversion device in a crowded parking lot, killing one person and putting many others at significant risk,” said ATF Special Agent in Charge Joseph Persails, of the St. Paul Field Division. “I am proud of the diligent work of ATF agents who built a thorough investigation that helped bring justice to the victim and the community. This sentence reinforces a clear message that individuals who commit violent acts with illegal firearms will face serious consequences.” This case was the result of an investigation by ATF and the Minneapolis Police Department, with assistance from other law enforcement partners, including the United States Marshals Service Fugitive Task Force. Assistant United States Attorney Benjamin Bejar prosecuted the case. title: Tax Preparer Sentenced in $5 Million Tax Fraud
body: Press Release Tax Preparer Sentenced in $5 Million Tax Fraud Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of California kelly.Thornton@usdoj.gov SAN DIEGO – San Diego CPA Oladapo Olagbemi was sentenced in federal court today to 18 months in prison for preparing false tax returns containing $5 million in improper deductions and credits that resulted in $1.5 million in losses to the public fisc. Olagbemi, who managed San Diego-based D.A.O. Accounting, Consulting, and Taxation, pleaded guilty in June to four counts of aiding and assisting the preparation of false tax returns, admitting to multiple schemes between tax years 2019 and 2023 to help clients get illegitimate refunds by claiming business expenses, charitable gifts, and energy credits to which the taxpayers were not entitled. See this link for further information on the plea . Olagbemi’s tax practice generated almost $1.2 million in gross revenue in 2025 alone.  “He betrayed the trust of his clients,” Judge Montenegro observed at today’s hearing. Olagbemi continued filing false returns even after he was investigated by the California Board of Accountancy, interviewed about his questionable practices by civil and criminal IRS agents, and his office was searched by federal agents as part of the investigation that led to charges in this case. He even filed at least one false tax return after pleading guilty in this case, while awaiting sentencing. “Tax fraud may hide the truth for a moment, but justice always comes to collect,” said U.S. Attorney Adam Gordon. “For years, Olagbemi abused his position as a trusted tax preparer by filing fraudulent returns designed to generate refunds to which his clients were not entitled, causing more than $1.5 million in tax losses. Even after being confronted by authorities and pleading guilty, he continued engaging in the same conduct,” said Darren Lian, Special Agent in Charge, IRS Criminal Investigation's Los Angeles Field Office. “Today’s sentence demonstrates that individuals who undermine the integrity of our tax system for personal gain will be held accountable.” This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Nicholas W. Pilchak. DEFENDANT Case Number 26-CR-1982-RBM Oladapo Olagbemi                            Age: 72                                   San Diego, CA CHARGES Aiding and Assisting in the Preparation of False Tax Returns, in violation of 26 U.S.C. § 7206(2) Maximum Penalties: Three years in prison (per count); $250,000 fine or twice the gross gain or loss INVESTIGATING AGENCY Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation Contact Kelly Thornton, Director of Media Relations Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Tax Component USAO - California, Southern Press Release Number: CAS26-1023-Olagbemi

title: Michigan Man Sentenced to 70 Months for Pandemic Relief Fraud
body: Press Release Michigan Man Sentenced to 70 Months for Pandemic Relief Fraud Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Delaware Nick.Young@usdoj.gov WILMINGTON, Del. – A Michigan man was sentenced on October 20, 2026, to 70 months in federal prison for his role in a scheme to defraud the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP). U.S. District Judge Jennifer L. Hall imposed the sentence. According to court documents, Carl Lawrence, 50, of Kentwood, Michigan, ran a business-consulting firm. Over the internet, Lawrence met Jady Solano, a Wilmington tax preparer, and the two conspired to defraud the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP), a COVID-19 relief program designed to safeguard jobs during the pandemic. Lawrence referred his consulting clients to Solano, who prepared fraudulent applications on their behalf. Lawrence also personally falsified documents for inclusion in the applications. In total, Lawrence assisted with 29 fraudulent applications, resulting in more than $4.7 million in wrongful loan disbursements. Lawrence personally made nearly $450,000 through the scheme, all of which he has been ordered to forfeit to the government. The total scheme led by Lawrence and Solano obtained approximately $9.1 million in pandemic relief funds. Across two charging instruments, eight members of the scheme have been charged: Defendant Case Number Stage of Case Jady Solano 24-cr-91-1 (JLH) Sentenced to 80 months in prison and restitution of $9,181,830.99 Shatoya Moss 24-cr-91-2 (JLH) Sentenced to 18 months in prison and restitution of $578,133.09 Carl Lawrence 24-cr-109-1 (JLH) Sentenced to 70 months in prison and restitution of $4,736,088.37 Brigette Miller-Levy 24-cr-109-2 (JLH) Sentenced to 24 months in prison and restitution of $882,777.70 Amber Baldwin 24-cr-109-3 (JLH) Convicted at trial; awaiting sentencing Marvin Edwards 24-cr-109-4 (JLH) Sentenced to 16 months in prison and restitution of $365,214.57 Anthony McKinzy 24-cr-109-5 (JLH) Indicted; remains at large after absconding Devlon Porter 24-cr-109-6 (JLH) Convicted at trial; awaiting sentencing “Stealing taxpayer money is always a serious crime,” said U.S. Attorney Benjamin L. Wallace. “But it is particularly serious when that money was meant to keep hardworking Americans employed during a pandemic. Carl Lawrence stole, and helped others steal, millions in disaster-relief funds. He’ll now spend years in federal prison, and, upon release, he’ll be forced to pay back every cent of his ill-gotten gains. I extend my thanks to our law-enforcement partners at IRS-CI and FBI. Together, we will tirelessly pursue anyone who seeks to plunder the public till.” “Carl Lawrence thought he could dupe the federal government and swindle American taxpayers. Instead, every dollar he stole will be forfeited and federal prison will be his home for the next six years,” said FBI Baltimore Special Agent in Charge Jimmy Paul. “The FBI and our partners are committed to finding fraudsters and ensuring they are held accountable for their crimes.” “Carl Lawrence and others deliberately carried out a scheme to defraud a program that was implemented to assist people during a pandemic,” said Philadelphia Field Office Special Agent in Charge Yury Kruty. “This sentencing holds Mr. Lawrence accountable for his criminal actions and shows that our office is committed to working with our law enforcement partners to investigate and prosecute individuals who commit these crimes.” Upon Lawrence’s release from prison, he will be required to serve three years of supervised release. The Court also ordered restitution in the amount of $4,736,088.37 and a forfeiture money judgement of $447,061.77. Agents of the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation and the FBI Baltimore Field Office’s Wilmington Resident Agency investigated the case. U.S. Attorney Wallace and Assistant U.S. Attorney Bryan C. Williamson prosecuted the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. A copy of this press release is located on the website of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Delaware.  Related court documents and information are located on the website of the District Court for the District of Delaware or on PACER by searching for Case No. 1:24-cr-109-JLH. For any defendant who has been indicted and not adjudicated guilty, his or her involvement in the fraud scheme described above is merely an allegation, and he or she is presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. ### Updated October 23, 2026 Topic COVID-Related Fraud Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Delaware

title: Justice Department Defends Army Corps’ Thorough Review for CWA Permit, Paving the Way for Much Needed Housing Development in Charleston, South Carolina
body: Press Release Justice Department Defends Army Corps’ Thorough Review for CWA Permit, Paving the Way for Much Needed Housing Development in Charleston, South Carolina Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit today affirmed the issuance by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (Corps) of a Clean Water Act Section 404 permit for the Cainhoy Plantation development in Charleston, South Carolina. The published decision paves the way for a major, long‑term housing initiative designed to meet the needs of one of the country’s fastest‑growing metropolitan areas. “Charleston’s rapid growth has created a real need for responsibly planned housing,” said Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General Adam Gustafson of ENRD. “This ruling confirms that the Corps followed the law, thoroughly evaluated alternatives, and approved a plan that supplies homes and community infrastructure while protecting the region’s most valuable wetlands.” The Corps’ permit authorizes carefully planned residential and mixed‑use development on portions of a 9,076‑acre property — an area the City of Charleston has long identified as essential to meeting regional growth and housing demand. The project will provide new housing, schools, medical facilities, and community services, all while permanently conserving thousands of acres of land. In affirming the permit, the court recognized that the Corps conducted a thorough, data‑driven review of numerous alternatives before concluding that none offered a practicable path to delivering needed housing with fewer environmental impacts. The court emphasized that the Corps worked with the developers to reduce projected wetlands impacts by nearly 90%, from 1,820 acres to just 181.5 acres, after years of analysis and refinement. Attorneys from ENRD’s Environmental Defense, Natural Resources, Wildlife and Marine Resources, and Appellate Sections handled the litigation. title: Las Vegas Man Sentenced to Eight Years in Prison for Child Sexual Abuse Material Crimes
body: Press Release Las Vegas Man Sentenced to Eight Years in Prison for Child Sexual Abuse Material Crimes Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada LAS VEGAS – A Las Vegas man was sentenced today by United States District Judge Gloria M. Navarro to 96 months in prison followed by 10 years of supervised release for distributing and transporting child sexual abuse material over social media networks and applications, and for maintaining a large collection of CSAM. The government recommended a sentence of 96 months in prison. “The distribution and possession of child sexual abuse material is an unforgivable, savage violation of human dignity that inflicts lifelong trauma on our most vulnerable,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “Let this lengthy sentence serve as a definitive baseline for anyone who participates in this toxic marketplace: we will exhaust every technical and legal resource to track you down, strip away your digital anonymity, and permanently remove you from civilized society. There will be no leniency, no compromises, and no mercy.” “Today’s sentencing delivers justice for victims of a predator who targeted children,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher S. Delzotto for the FBI Las Vegas Field Office. “While it cannot erase the harm he caused, we hope it brings some measure of peace and closure. Donovan’s systematic collection and distribution of child abuse material reflects profound depravity. The exploitation of children is an unforgivable crime, and we remain committed to holding offenders accountable.” According to court documents, James Donovan distributed CSAM at least 11 times with other users and channels of the social media application Discord. He also transported CSAM to an Amazon Cloud account using the internet. He also possessed about 70 printed images and over 50,000 digital images and videos of CSAM depicting sadistic or masochistic conduct or other depictions of violence, infants and toddlers, and prepubescent minors under the age of 12. Donovan pleaded guilty to one count of distribution of child pornography, one count of transportation of child pornography, and one count of possession of child pornography. In addition to his sentence of imprisonment, Donovan will be required to pay restitution to his victims and to register as a sex offender in the place where he resides, where he is an employee, and where he is a student, under the Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act (SORNA). The FBI investigated the case. Assistant United States Attorney Afroza Yeasmin prosecuted the case. These cases are a part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc . The public is urged to remain vigilant and report suspected exploitation of a child through the FBI’s tipline at 1-800-CALL-FBI (225-5324), tips.fbi.gov , or by calling your local FBI field office. ### Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Nevada

title: Former Texas Tech professor sentenced to 480 months in federal prison for “pink flamingo” fentanyl trafficking conspiracy
body: Press Release Former Texas Tech professor sentenced to 480 months in federal prison for “pink flamingo” fentanyl trafficking conspiracy Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas LUBBOCK, Texas – United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould today announced that a former Texas Tech University professor who manufactured and distributed fentanyl — including a branded mixture known as “pink flamingo” — was sentenced to 40 years in federal prison. Daniel Taylor, 51, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute 40 grams or more of fentanyl on July 1. U.S. District Judge James Wesley Hendrix imposed the 480‑month sentence today. “Daniel Taylor earned every year of his 40-year sentence,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “Taylor targeted and preyed on vulnerable women, enlisted some of them to help his drug supply chain, branded his poison as if it were a product sold off a shelf and showed a shocking disregard for human life. Thank you to the agents and our AUSAs who removed him from our communities for the rest of his life so he can’t hurt or manipulate anyone else ever again.” “Daniel Taylor exploited his position of trust and education to engage in the distribution of one of the deadliest drugs threatening our communities,” said DEA Special Agent in Charge Joseph B. Tucker. “While he should have been helping shape the futures of young Americans, he was instead distributing a deadly poison that has devastated families across this country.” According to court documents, Taylor was an assistant professor of supply chain management at Texas Tech’s Rawls College of Business when he began distributing fentanyl powder throughout the Lubbock area. He produced two fentanyl products: a potent white powder known as “ghost,” and “pink flamingo,” a fentanyl–bromazolam mixture that he dyed pink and packaged with flamingo‑branded stickers and envelopes. Law enforcement began investigating Taylor in 2025. In January, agents observed Taylor meet with one of his distributors in a convenience‑store parking lot shortly before a passenger in the same vehicle overdosed and required emergency hospitalization. During subsequent operations, agents executed search warrants and recovered fentanyl, bromazolam, methamphetamine, cocaine base, ketamine, and MDMA. They also found a heat‑sealing and packaging station, pink envelopes, flamingo stickers, and a handwritten recipe outlining the formula for “pink flamingo.” Court documents show that Taylor provided fentanyl to multiple women in exchange for sex. Several women overdosed after consuming Taylor’s fentanyl products, including at least one who required multiple doses of Narcan administered in Taylor’s home. Messages obtained from Taylor’s phone showed him instructing associates to move drug discussions to encrypted applications and delete messages. Taylor referred to the women collectively as his “flamingos.” Taylor is a previously federally convicted felon and had earlier been court‑martialed after using fraudulent documents and attempting to fake his own death. This investigation was a joint operation of the Texas Anti-Gang Center and the Caprock Hi-Intensity Drug Trafficking Area. This group is composed of agents with the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, the Texas Department of Public Safety, the Lubbock County Sheriff’s Office and the Lubbock Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Stephen J. Rancourt from the Lubbock Division prosecuted the case. ### Documents daniel_taylor_factual_resume.pdf Contact Public Affairs Division U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of Texas USATXN.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Components Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) USAO - Texas, Northern

title: Kansas man sentenced for sending and receiving child pornography online
body: Press Release Kansas man sentenced for sending and receiving child pornography online Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Kansas WICHITA, KAN. – A Kansas man was sentenced to 155 months in prison for distributing child sexual abuse material (CSAM). According to court documents, Zachery Leslie, 25, of Wichita pleaded guilty to one count of distribution of child pornography. Leslie used an online file sharing platform to send and receive CSAM including nine files which included prepubescent children subjected to sex acts. “There is a misconception that distributing child sexual abuse material found online is a lesser offense because the perpetrator never directly encounters a victim,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “In reality, each time these images are circulated, the abuse is compounded and the victims are harmed again. This conduct is serious, and it must end.” The Kansas Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) investigated the case. Project Safe Childhood This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. title: Indian foreign national arrested on child pornography charges
body: Press Release Indian foreign national arrested on child pornography charges Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Ohio CINCINNATI – A foreign national currently in the United States on an H-1B work visa was arrested by federal agents on charges alleging he accessed and downloaded child pornography. Vimalesh Prem Kumar, 39, of Blue Ash, appeared in federal court on Oct. 21. According to charging documents, cyber tips led agents to Kumar’s online accounts. Kumar allegedly viewed child pornography via Instagram, Twitter and Telegram and downloaded and shared the child sexual abuse material on Telegram. The uploaded child sexual abuse material allegedly included explicit images of a young girl next to a teddy bear and a young girl wearing sheer lingerie. “HSI special agents continue to leverage every tool at our disposal and our national footprint to identify and investigate predators who share horrendous and obscene images of children being abused,” said HSI Detroit acting Special Agent in Charge Jeremy Pierczynski. “Working in the U.S. as a foreign national is a privilege and violators that target the most vulnerable members of our community will be held fully accountable under the law.” Kumar is charged with possessing or accessing with the intent to view child pornography, a federal crime punishable by up to 10 years in prison. Dominick S. Gerace II, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Ohio; Jeremy Pierczynski, Acting Special Agent in Charge, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Detroit; and officials with the Ohio Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force announced the charges. Assistant United States Attorney Kyle J. Healey is representing the United States in this case. A criminal complaint merely contains allegations, and defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law. title: Deadly Arson Spree in Northeast Yields 25 Years in Prison for D.C. Man
body: Press Release Deadly Arson Spree in Northeast Yields 25 Years in Prison for D.C. Man Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia USADC.Media@usdoj.gov WASHINGTON – D’Aundrey Scott, 32, of Washington, D.C., was sentenced today to 25 years in prison for charges related to a spree of arsons, one of which killed of 62-year-old Darryl Finney, in May 2020, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. “D’Aundrey Scott deliberately set two men on fire in the middle of the night, killing Darryl Finney in an act of horrific violence," said U.S. Attorney Pirro. "His actions were cruel, calculated, and utterly unconscionable. Now, he will spend the next 25 years behind prison walls, answering for his crimes.” Scott pleaded guilty to one count of second-degree murder and one count each of assault with a dangerous weapon, arson, and felony destruction of property, on August 14, 2026, before D.C. Superior Court Judge Todd Edelman. In addition to the 25-year prison sentence, Judge Edelman ordered Scott to serve five years of supervised release. According to court documents, at approximately 12:23 a.m., on May 13, 2020, Scott went on an arson spree. He first approached an adult male who was lying on the sidewalk in the 1300 block of H Street Northeast, Washington, D.C. The defendant ignited a small, flammable object and threw that burning object onto the man who kicked the object off, avoiding injury. Then at approximately 1:04 a.m., Scott approached a second male, Darryl Finney, who was sleeping on the sidewalk in the 900 block of H Street Northeast, Washington, D.C. The defendant ignited a small, flammable object and tossed it onto Mr. Finney. The defendant then splashed an ignitable liquid onto Mr. Finney, causing Mr. Finney and his personal effects to catch fire. Mr. Finney, who was engulfed in flames, managed to get up and walk toward H Street, where the Metropolitan Police Department and D.C. Fire and EMS responded to assist. The victim suffered second and third degree burns to multiple parts of his body and despite treatment at a local hospital, he died due to his injuries on May 15, 2020. Scott was arrested on May 19, 2020, and has been in custody since. Joining the announcement was Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll of the Metropolitan Police Department. In announcing the sentence, U.S. Attorney Pirro and Interim Chief Carroll commended the work of those who investigated the case from the Metropolitan Police Department. They also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Brian Ganjei, who prosecuted the case. 2020 CF1 004775 Contact USADC.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Component USAO - District of Columbia

title: Illegal Alien from Dominican Republic Sentenced for Trafficking Methamphetamine, Fentanyl, and Cocaine
body: Press Release Illegal Alien from Dominican Republic Sentenced for Trafficking Methamphetamine, Fentanyl, and Cocaine Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Maine Lenin Nova-Nova identified himself using a false name BANGOR, Maine: A Dominican Republic national was sentenced today in U.S. District Court in Bangor for possessing controlled substances with intent to distribute. U.S. District Judge John A. Woodcock, Jr. sentenced Lenin Nova-Nova , 45, to 10 years in prison to be followed by five years of supervised release. Nova-Nova pleaded guilty on June 17, 2024. According to court records, in November 2023, Nova-Nova was a passenger in a vehicle that East Millinocket police officers stopped due to a headlight issue. An officer observed an unnatural bulge under Nova-Nova’s clothing. Nova-Nova identified himself using a false name and a warrant check of that alias revealed an outstanding arrest warrant. A search of Nova-Nova’s person revealed $1,305 in cash, four cell phones, and suspected controlled substances wrapped in cellophane. The substances were analyzed and identified as approximately 113 grams of 100% pure methamphetamine, approximately 19 grams of a substance containing fentanyl, and 57.8 grams of a substance containing cocaine base. Homeland Security Investigations was able to determine Nova-Nova’s real identity and that he was in the country illegally. The East Millinocket Police Department and Homeland Security Investigations investigated the case. ### Contact Joel Casey, Assistant United States Attorney (Tel: 207-945-0373) Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Maine

title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Filed 114 Border-Related Cases This Week
body: Press Release U.S. Attorney’s Office Filed 114 Border-Related Cases This Week Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of California SAN DIEGO – Federal prosecutors in the Southern District of California filed 114 border-related cases this week, including charges of bringing in aliens for financial gain, reentering the U.S. after deportation, and importation of controlled substances. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California is the fourth-busiest federal district, largely due to a high volume of border-related crimes. This district, encompassing San Diego and Imperial counties, shares a 140-mile border with Mexico. It includes the San Ysidro Port of Entry, the world’s busiest land border crossing, connecting San Diego (America’s eighth largest city) and Tijuana (Mexico’s second largest city). In addition to reactive border-related crimes, the Southern District of California also prosecutes a significant number of proactive cases related to terrorism, organized crime, drugs, white-collar fraud, violent crime, cybercrime, human trafficking and national security. Recent developments in those and other significant areas of prosecution can be found here . A sample of border-related arrests this week: On October 19, 2026, Cristian Jonathan Cortes, a United States citizen, was arrested and charged with Importation of Controlled Substance. According to a complaint, Customs and Border Protection officers discovered 49 pounds of cocaine concealed in the doors of the 2010 Toyota Tundra the defendant was driving as he applied for entry to the U.S. at the San Ysidro Port of Entry. On October 20, 2026, Marina Viviana Gary, a Mexican citizen and Permanent Resident of the United States, was arrested and charged with Bringing in Aliens for Financial Gain. According to a complaint, Customs and Border Protection officers discovered an individual concealed under a plastic panel covering a non-factory sheet-metal compartment towards the rear of the vehicle. Further inspection revealed a second individual concealed in a modified spare tire well compartment. In order to remove the second individual from the spare well compartment, Customs and Border Protection officers had to unlatch and fold back the sheet metal. The two individuals were concealed in the Hyundai Santa Fe the defendant was driving as she applied for entry to the U.S. at the San Ysidro Port of Entry. On October 21, 2026, Benjamin Galindo, a United States citizen, was arrested and charged with Importation of a Controlled Substance. According to a complaint, Customs and Border Protection officers discovered 37 pounds of fentanyl concealed in the rear seats, center console, and roof of the vehicle of his 2005 Toyota Camry the defendant was driving as he applied for entry to the U.S. at the Tecate Port of Entry. The immigration cases were referred or supported by federal law enforcement partners, including Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ICE ERO), Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Border Patrol, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), with the support and assistance of state and local law enforcement partners. Indictments and criminal complaints are merely allegations and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Contact Kelly Thornton Director of Media Relations U.S. Attorney’s Office Southern District of California 619.546.9726 Follow us on Twitter @SDCAnews Updated October 23, 2026 Component USAO - California, Southern Press Release Number: CAS26-1023-Border Cases

title: Convicted felon sentenced to two and a half years in prison for firearms crime in addition to a six-year sentence for fraud
body: Press Release Convicted felon sentenced to two and a half years in prison for firearms crime in addition to a six-year sentence for fraud Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Virginia NORFOLK, Va. – A Chesapeake man was sentenced yesterday to two years and six months in prison for possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. This sentence will run consecutively to a six-year sentence for a separate fraud conviction . According to court documents, on Dec. 1, 2025, Chesapeake Police responded to a 911 emergency response call for a domestic assault incident at a residence in Chesapeake involving Adrian Thomas Knight Jr., 42. Reports indicated Knight was cocking a firearm while battering an individual. Even though he knew he had two firearms, when questioned, Knight stated, “I’m on federal probation, why would I have a gun?” Knight was arrested and an officer obtained a no-contact Emergency Protective Order against Knight that prohibited him from returning to the residence. Around 3:30 a.m., despite being served with a no-contact emergency protective order, Knight returned to the residence and was again arrested. At the time of the incident, Knight had been convicted of conspiracy to commit mail, bank, and wire fraud; wire fraud; and bank fraud, and sentencing in that case was pending. As a convicted felon, Knight was prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition. Theophani K. Stamos, First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia, and Anthony A. Spotswood, Special Agent in Charge of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives Washington Field Division, made the announcement after sentencing by U.S. District Judge Jamar K. Walker. Assistant U.S. Attorney Clayton D. LaForge prosecuted the case. Related court documents and information are located on the website of the District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia or on PACER by searching for Case No. 2:26-cr-23. Contact USAVAE.Press@usdoj.gov Updated October 23, 2026 Topics Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Virginia, Eastern

title: Suburban Chicago Man Sentenced to Two Years in Federal Prison for Staging Robberies To Help Others Fraudulently Apply for Immigration Visas
body: Press Release Suburban Chicago Man Sentenced to Two Years in Federal Prison for Staging Robberies To Help Others Fraudulently Apply for Immigration Visas Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Illinois CHICAGO — A suburban Chicago man has been sentenced to two years in federal prison for conspiring to stage armed robberies so that the purported victims could apply for U.S. immigration visas reserved for crime victims. From 2022 to 2024, PARTH NAYI organized and participated in hundreds of staged armed robberies at coffee shops, restaurants, liquor stores, and gas stations throughout the country, including in Chicago and the suburbs of Lombard, Elmwood Park, St. Charles, Hickory Hills, River Grove, Lake Villa, and South Holland.  Nayi worked with others to recruit fake victims, pay off store owners to use their locations, coordinate and pay fake robbers, and coach the bogus victims through the plan.  Thousands of individuals who posed as victims each paid Nayi $5,000 to $30,000 to participate in the scam so that they could later apply for Nonimmigrant U-Visas, which are set aside for foreign nationals who are victims of certain crimes and are helpful to law enforcement in the investigation. During the staged robberies, individuals acting as robbers brandished what appeared to be firearms, approached the purported victims, and demanded money.  Afterwards, the purported victims submitted forms to local law enforcement to obtain certification that they were victims of a qualifying crime and were helpful in the investigation. Upon receiving the certification, the purported victims then submitted fraudulent U-Visa applications to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services predicated upon their alleged status as robbery victims. Nayi, 29, of Woodridge, Ill., pleaded guilty earlier this year to conspiracy to commit visa fraud.  On Thursday, U.S. District Judge Mary M. Rowland sentenced Nayi to two years in federal prison and fined him $50,000. The sentence was announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois; Ryan Whalen, Special Agent-in-Charge of the Chicago Field Office of the FBI; and Matthew Scarpino, Special Agent-in-Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in Chicago. “Defendant was the main organizer and at the center of almost every single one of the hundreds of staged robberies that were perpetrated,” Assistant U.S. Attorney Saqib Mohammad Hussain argued in the government’s sentencing memorandum.  “Defendant significantly corrupted the federal U Visa program, designed to provide a benefit to a particularly vulnerable group—foreign nationals who are victims of serious crimes while visiting the United States.” Five other individuals have also been convicted as part of the federal investigation. Updated October 23, 2026 Topics Fraud Immigration Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Illinois, Northern

title: U.S. Government Contractor Arrested for Allegedly Leaking National Defense Information
body: Press Release U.S. Government Contractor Arrested for Allegedly Leaking National Defense Information Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs A U.S. government contractor was arrested by the FBI this morning for allegedly leaking national defense information to another individual who repeatedly posted classified information to an online publication. “National defense information is classified to protect the American people from bad actors around the world who wish to do us harm,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “The details alleged in this affidavit reflect the behavior of a government contractor who exempted himself from a federal law governing the protection of classified information. The Department of Justice will continue prosecuting individuals who leak classified information and put our national security at risk.” “The FBI arrested the subject after he was caught allegedly betraying his oath and leaking classified defense information,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Protecting America’s secrets is a top counterintelligence priority of this FBI - and anyone caught abusing their position of trust within the government by jeopardizing national security and putting our brave warriors at risk will be met with the full weight of justice.” “Following a referral from the Agency, on Friday, October 23rd, the FBI arrested a contractor who provided services to CIA for alleged unauthorized disclosures of classified information,” said CIA Director John Ratcliffe. “The unauthorized release of classified material poses grave risks to our national security, intelligence sources, ongoing operations, and our officers. There is absolutely zero tolerance for leaking, and anyone who violates their oath will be held accountable and prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law.” “As alleged, Brinksman reached far outside his own duties to obtain some of our Nation’s most closely held secrets and handed them to a romantic partner he knew intended to publish them,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “That is not carelessness. It is a betrayal of his oath and the American people who entrusted him to fulfill his duties honorably. Those cleared to hold our Nation's secrets undertake a solemn obligation to protect that information. If proven at trial, this conduct is a grave violation of the Espionage Act, and the National Security Division will prosecute it as such.” Ian A. Brinksman, 42, of the District of Columbia was arrested following a search of his residence and charged by criminal complaint with unlawfully transmitting national defense information. According to the criminal complaint, beginning in 2020, the defendant worked as an employee of a U.S. government agency based in the Eastern District of Virginia and later in 2022 began working as a developer for systems integration for “Company 1,” a contractor to the same U.S. government agency. During all times relevant to the complaint, Brinksman held a Top Secret security clearance with Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access. As further detailed in the complaint, Brinksman had an ongoing personal relationship with an individual who maintains an online publication on Substack (Individual 1). A fundraising article reportedly published by Individual 1 in September 2026 claimed Individual 1 had “published reporting based on classified [relevant U.S. government agency] assessments.” Individual 1 posted on her social media profile, “I also accept leaks.” The FBI Chicago Field Office is investigating the case with substantial assistance from the Washington Field Office. Trial Attorneys Eli Ross and Kathryn DeMarco of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Vito Iaia for the Eastern District of Virginia are prosecuting the case, with valuable assistance from Assistant U.S. Attorneys Tejpal Chawla and Stuart Allen for the District of Columbia. Charges in a complaint are merely allegations, and every defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Note: Please see the affidavit here . Updated October 23, 2026 Topic National Security Components Office of the Attorney General Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) National Security Division (NSD) USAO - Virginia, Eastern Press Release Number: 26-1256

title: Vidalia man sentenced to 24 years in prison for firearms-related charge
body: Press Release Vidalia man sentenced to 24 years in prison for firearms-related charge Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Georgia STATESBORO, Georgia: A Toombs County man has been sentenced to federal prison after pleading guilty to a firearms-related charge. The sentence was imposed by U.S. District Court Judge J. Randal Hall and announced by Margaret E. “Meg” Heap, U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Georgia. Iran Darna Harris , 30, of Vidalia, was sentenced to 288 months in prison followed by five years of supervised release after pleading guilty to Use of a Firearm During and in Relation to a Crime of Violence. The firearm was also equipped with a machinegun conversion device converting it to a fully automatic machinegun. There is no parole in the federal system. According to court documents and testimony, in May 2025, Harris entered a restaurant located on East 1 st St. in Vidalia. While inside the establishment, Harris produced a firearm, a Glock 22, .40 caliber pistol, and demanded money from employees. After committing the robbery, Harris attempted to flee the restaurant and discard the weapon and stolen money but was apprehended by a Toombs County Sheriff’s deputy. A search of the area where Harris had fled revealed the firearm and cash stolen from the establishment. "This lengthy sentence sends a clear message that individuals who bring violence and fear into our community businesses will be held fully accountable," said U.S. Attorney Heap. "The quick actions of our local law enforcement partners prevented further danger and ensured this armed robber was brought to justice. We will continue to aggressively prosecute violent offenders to keep our neighborhoods safe." This case was investigated by the FBI, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and the Toombs County Sheriff’s Office. “Armed robberies that place innocent people in harm’s way have no place in our society and will not be tolerated,” said Brian Ozden, Assistant Special Agent in Charge of FBI Atlanta. “The FBI remains committed to protecting our communities and working alongside our law enforcement partners to keep every neighborhood safe.” “Bringing a firearm into a place of business and threatening employees is a serious act of violence. This sentence underscores that those who put our community at risk will be held accountable,” said ATF Assistant Special Agent in Charge Brian Graves. “We thank our local and state law enforcement partners for their swift response and coordination in bringing this case to justice.” This case was prosecuted for the United States by Southern District of Georgia Assistant U.S. Attorney Makeia R. Jonese. Contact For any questions, please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Office at (912) 652-4422. Updated October 23, 2026 Topics Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Georgia, Southern Press Release Number: 110-26

title: Alien Charged for Illegal Voting
body: Press Release Alien Charged for Illegal Voting Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada LAS VEGAS – An alien was charged today for illegally voting in a federal election in Nevada. “Let me be absolutely clear: if you are a noncitizen and you cast a ballot in our elections, you are committing a federal crime,” said Sigal Chattah, First Assistant United States Attorney for the District of Nevada. “We will not hesitate to use the full weight of federal law enforcement to investigate, indict, and prosecute anyone who attempts to compromise the integrity of our elections. I commend our partners at FBI and HSI for their diligence, assistance and unwavering commitment to ensuring our elections remain fair and free from unlawful interference.” “Protecting the integrity of the electoral process is essential to maintaining public confidence in our democratic institutions,” said Erin Burke, Special Agent in Charge for HSI Los Angeles. “HSI will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to investigate allegations of violations of federal election laws and hold individuals accountable through the judicial process.” “Safeguarding the integrity of our elections for American citizens stands as a paramount mission for the FBI,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher S. Delzotto for the FBI Las Vegas Office. “The FBI will aggressively deploy every resource at our disposal to investigate any credible claim of voter fraud or illegal voting. Fidelity, Bravery, and Integrity—Justice will find you.” According to information in the criminal information, on or about November 2, 2024, Jullie Ann Sumalinog Moore voted in an election held in part for the purpose of electing a candidate for the office of President, Vice President, Member of the Senate, and Member of the House of Representatives. Moore is charged with one count of voting by an alien. The maximum statutory penalty is one year of imprisonment, a fine of up to $100,000, or both. An initial appearance date has not yet been scheduled. The FBI and HSI investigated this case. An information is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. ### Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - Nevada

title: Federal Correctional Officer Indicted for Receiving a Bribe and Providing Contraband to A Federal Prisoner
body: Press Release Federal Correctional Officer Indicted for Receiving a Bribe and Providing Contraband to A Federal Prisoner Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Ocala, Florida – Weston Burney (34, Webster) has been charged by federal indictment with one count of receipt of a bribe by a public official and one count of providing contraband to a federal prisoner. If convicted, Burney faces a maximum penalty of 15 years’ imprisonment for the bribery offense and up to 10 years for the contraband offense. The indictment also notifies Burney that the United States intends to forfeit any property, real or personal, which constitutes or is derived from proceeds traceable to proceeds to the alleged offense. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to the indictment, between February and June 2025, Burney, a public official, employed by the U.S. Department of Justice Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) accepted monies in return for smuggling contraband into the Coleman Federal Correctional Complex in violation of his official duties as a correctional officer. During this time, Burney provided contraband, namely tobacco and Methyl 3,3-dimethyl-2-(1-(pent-4-en-1-yl)-1H-indazole-3-carboxamido) butanoate (MDMB-4en-PINACA), a Schedule I controlled substance, to an inmate at the federal prison in return for monetary payments. An indictment is merely a formal charge that a defendant has committed one or more violations of federal criminal law, and every defendant is presumed innocent unless, and until, proven guilty. This case is being investigated by the Department of Justice Office of the Inspector General and the Federal Bureau of Prisons. It will be prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Angela Moon Palacios. Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Public Corruption Component USAO - Florida, Middle

title: Forest City Township Man Pleads Guilty to Making False Statements
body: Press Release Forest City Township Man Pleads Guilty to Making False Statements Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Maine Gregory P. Heimann Jr. falsely stated that he was unable to walk in order to receive disability benefits BANGOR, Maine: A Forest City Township man pleaded guilty today in U.S. District Court in Bangor to making false statements to a federal official. According to court records, Gregory P. Heimann Jr. , 52, falsely represented to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) in May 2023 that he had been using a wheelchair since 2004 and was unable to walk or stand. Heimann was documented and recorded walking and standing without the assistance of any mobility devices on numerous occasions. Heimann faces up to five years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000, and up to three years of supervised release.  He will be sentenced after the completion of a presentence investigative report by the U.S. Probation Office. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. The VA Office of Inspector General and the Social Security Administration Office of Inspector General investigated the case with assistance from the Maine Warden Service. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. ### Contact Alisa Ross, Assistant United States Attorney (Tel: 207-945-0373) Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Benefit Fraud Component USAO - Maine
