title: Federal jury convicts Richmond area man for armed robbery of delivery driver
body: Press Release Federal jury convicts Richmond area man for armed robbery of delivery driver Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Virginia NEWPORT NEWS, Va. – A federal jury convicted Jayveon Christopher McCloud yesterday on charges of conspiracy to interfere with interstate commerce by robbery, threats, and violence; interference with interstate commerce by robbery, threats, and violence; carjacking; and brandishing a firearm during of a crime of violence. According to court records and evidence presented at trial, on Oct. 22, 2025, McCloud and Takaree Alexander Fields, 22, of Roanoke Rapids, North Carolina, each wearing a mask and armed with a handgun, approached a food delivery driver in Newport News. McCloud and Fields pointed their firearms at the victim and ordered him to drop everything, empty his pockets, and remove his shoes. McCloud and Fields took the food the victim was attempting to deliver and the victim’s shoes, money, and car key fob. McCloud took the victim’s car while Fields fled in a vehicle he had stolen from his mother. After the victim reported the crime, Newport News Police observed the victim’s vehicle and attempted a traffic stop. McCloud attempted to flee but crashed the victim’s vehicle. McCloud was arrested after a brief foot pursuit. Fields was not apprehended that night. The following day, Henrico County Police located Fields, who fled at a high rate of speed. He eventually crashed in a convenience store parking lot and attempted to flee on foot into a wooded area. Officers apprehended Fields nearby. Fields pled guilty on Oct. 5 to interference with interstate commerce by robbery, threats, and violence and brandishing a firearm during of a crime of violence. He faces a mandatory minimum of seven years and up to life in prison when sentenced on Jan. 7, 2027. McCloud faces a mandatory minimum of seven years and up to life in prison when sentenced on Jan. 20, 2027. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. Theophani K. Stamos, First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia; Anthony A. Spotswood, Special Agent in Charge of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives Washington Field Division; and Steve R. Drew, Chief of Newport News Police, made the announcement after the verdict was accepted by U.S. District Judge Elizabeth W. Hanes. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Alyson C. Yates and Mack Coleman are prosecuting the case. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. Related court documents and information are located on the website of the District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia or on PACER by searching for Case No. 4:26-cr-34. Contact USAVAE.Press@usdoj.gov Updated October 23, 2026 Topics Project Safe Neighborhoods Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Virginia, Eastern

title: Three More Defendants Sentenced to Lengthy Terms of Imprisonment for Federal Crimes Related to the Murder of Puerto Rico Police Sergeant Eliezer Ramos Vélez in Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Prosecution
body: Press Release Three More Defendants Sentenced to Lengthy Terms of Imprisonment for Federal Crimes Related to the Murder of Puerto Rico Police Sergeant Eliezer Ramos Vélez in Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Prosecution Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Puerto Rico SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – Today, United States District Court Judge Judge María Antongiorgi-Jordán sentenced three more defendants for drug trafficking and firearm violations, related to the murder of Puerto Rico Police Sergeant Eliezer Ramos Vélez, announced Héctor Ramírez-Carbó, Acting United States Attorney for the District of Puerto Rico.  The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated the case. Olvin O’Neill Concepción-Tapia, a/k/a “Sinfo” – sentenced to 480 months (40 years) in prison, followed by a supervised release term of 10 years. Daniel J. López-Vega, a/k/a “Dany” - sentenced to 480 months (40 years) in prison, followed by a supervised release term of 10 years. Andyel González-Sáez, a/k/a “Martino” - sentenced to 336 months (28 years)  in prison, followed by a supervised release term of 10 years. The other defendant, Luis N. Isaac-Sánchez, a/k/a “Chimbo”, “CDobleta”, “Dobleta” was rescheduled to be sentenced on Thursday, October 29, 2026. All defendants accepted responsibility for their role and participation in the drug trafficking conspiracy (Count One) in violation of Title 21, U.S.C., Sections 841(a)(1), 846, and 860. The drug conspiracy charged that the defendants conspired with others to distribute and to possess with intent to distribute significant quantities of drugs, including heroin, cocaine, crack cocaine, marijuana, and other drugs in the Sabana Abajo Public Housing Project (PHP), Luis Llorens Torres PHP, Los Mirtos PHP, Lagos de Blasina PHP, La Esmeralda PHP, El Coral PHP, Jardines de Monte Hatillo PHP and other nearby areas, and also pleaded guilty to possession of a firearm in furtherance of drug trafficking (Count Seven), in violation of Title 18, U.S.C., Section 924(c). All defendants admitted to their participation in the murder of Sgt. Ramos-Vélez and all plea agreements include a provision that the murder sentencing guidelines provision (U.S. Sentencing Guidelines Section 2A1.1), applies to their cases. The murder guidelines provision applies whether a defendant pleaded guilty to the drug trafficking conspiracy (Count One) or to the substantive firearms-related murder (Count Nine). Assistant United States Attorney (AUSA) and Chief of the Gang Section Alberto López-Rocafort; Deputy Chief of the Gang Section, AUSA Teresa Zapata-Valladares; and AUSAs Laura Díaz-González, and Joseph Russell are prosecuting the case. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF San Juan comprises agents and officers from the following federal partners: FBI, ICE-HSI, CBP (OFO, AMO and Border Patrol), the U.S. Marshals Service for Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, DEA, ATF, IRS, U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the Department of State, and the U.S. Secret Service, the Puerto Rico/U.S. Virgin Islands HIDTA, TSA, FAA, and the U.S. Attorney’s Offices for the Districts of Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The HSTF also has the following state and local law enforcement partners as participating agencies: the Puerto Rico Police Department; the San Juan, Carolina, Guaynabo, Barceloneta, and Ponce Municipal Police Departments, the Puerto Rico National Guard – Counter Drug Program; the Puerto Rico Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation; the Puerto Rico Internal Revenue Service (Hacienda); the Puerto Rico Port Authority; and the Virgin Islands Police Department. ### Updated October 23, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Puerto Rico U.S. Marshals Service Press Release Number: 2026-114

title: Leader of FARC Dissident Group Extradited to South Florida to Face Federal Cocaine Trafficking and Money Laundering Charges
body: Press Release Leader of FARC Dissident Group Extradited to South Florida to Face Federal Cocaine Trafficking and Money Laundering Charges Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Florida MIAMI – The leader of Frente 33, part of the FARC dissident group Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia – People’s Army (FARC-EP), a designated foreign terrorist organization, was extradited from Colombia to the Southern District of Florida on Thursday to face federal charges stemming from an alleged international cocaine trafficking and money laundering conspiracy. According to court records, from September 2021 through August 2022, Willinton Henao Gutierrez, also known as “El Mocho Olmedo,” 45, and his co-conspirators participated in an international drug trafficking operation involving five kilograms or more of cocaine. The conspiracy allegedly operated in Colombia and in South Florida, including Miami-Dade and Broward Counties. Henao Gutierrez and his co-conspirators allegedly agreed to transfer funds from the U.S. to and through locations outside the country to promote the manufacture, importation, sale, and distribution of controlled substances. Henao Gutierrez is charged with conspiring to import cocaine into the United States, conspiring to distribute cocaine known or having reasonable cause to believe it would be unlawfully imported into the United States, conspiring to commit money laundering, and attempted money laundering. He is charged alongside Jennifer Tapiero, Heyner Raul Sandoval Salazar, and Wilder Antonio Sanchez Duarte. If convicted, Henao Gutierrez faces a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years and up to life in federal prison on each of the two drug trafficking conspiracy charges. He also faces up to 20 years in prison on each of the money laundering charges. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. The Justice Department’s Judicial Attaché in Bogotá and Office of International Affairs secured the arrest and extradition of Henao Gutierrez. The Justice Department thanks the Cuerpo Técnico de Investigación of the Colombian Attorney General’s Office for its assistance and coordinated efforts. U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida and Special Agent in Charge Miles Aley of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Miami Field Division made the announcement. DEA Miami and the DEA Bogotá Country Office are investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Yara Dodin is prosecuting the case. Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.flsd.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.flsd.uscourts.gov , under case numbers 23-cr-20070. ### Contact Public Affairs Unit U.S. Attorney’s Office Southern District of Florida USAFLS.News@usdoj.gov Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Florida, Southern

title: Glenvil Man Convicted for Conspiracy to Distribute Cocaine
body: Press Release Glenvil Man Convicted for Conspiracy to Distribute Cocaine Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nebraska United States Attorney Lesley A. Woods announced that Luis Molina, 33, of Glenvil, Nebraska, was sentenced on October 22, 2026, in federal court in Lincoln, Nebraska, for conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing cocaine and possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing cocaine. United States District Judge Susan M. Bazis sentenced Molina to a total of 72 months’ imprisonment. There is no parole in the federal system. After Molina’s release from prison, he will begin a 5-year term of supervised release. On June 9, 2025, Molina and his co-defendants, Kenneth Palenzuela, Chanda Schroyer, and another individual, drove from Nebraska to Chicago in Schroyer’s vehicle.  Upon their arrival, Molina met with an individual to pick up a kilogram of cocaine.  On June 10, 2025, the group began their drive back to Nebraska.  After they entered the state, a Nebraska State Patrol trooper observed their vehicle speeding and conducted a traffic stop.  Molina was the driver, Palenzuela was in the passenger seat, and Schroyer and the other individual were in the backseat. The trooper smelled marijuana when he approached the vehicle and a search of the vehicle was conducted.  A small amount of marijuana was found in a purse in the front passenger area.  A black backpack was found under the seat at the back.  The backpack contained a clear cellophane bundle of suspected cocaine. The state crime laboratory confirmed that the bundle contained over one kilogram of cocaine.  A drug ledger was also found in the vehicle. Palenzuela pleaded guilty to possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing cocaine on July 8, 2026. He was sentenced to 24 months’ imprisonment followed by 5 years of supervised release on October 15, 2026. Schroyer pleaded guilty to possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing cocaine on January 14, 2026. She is set for sentencing on November 5, 2026. This case was investigated by the Nebraska State Patrol Commercial Interdiction Unit in Omaha Nebraska and the TRIDENT and CODE Task Forces which are made up of law enforcement agencies throughout a 22-county area in west-central/southwest Nebraska and includes the North Platte Police Department, Lexington Police Department, Dawson County Sheriff’s Office, Ogallala Police Department, Nebraska State Patrol, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI). Contact Amy Donato 402-661-3700 Updated October 23, 2026 Component USAO - Nebraska

title: Registered Sex Offender from Rhode Island Indicted for Transportation of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Registered Sex Offender from Rhode Island Indicted for Transportation of Child Pornography Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts BOSTON – A Rhode Island man has been indicted by a federal grand jury for possession of child sexual abuse material (CSAM). Frank DeCaro, 47, of Westerly, R.I., was indicted on one count of transportation of child pornography. DeCaro was previously arrested and charged in August 2026 . According to the charging documents, DeCaro is a registered sex offender following a 2014 conviction for possession of CSAM in Rhode Island state court, for which he received a probationary sentence. In November 2025, DeCaro was stopped at Boston Logan Airport attempting to enter the country from an international trip to Italy.  During a subsequent search, multiple images and videos depicting CSAM were allegedly discovered on DeCaro’s phone. The charge of transporting child pornography after a previous similar offense provides for a minimum mandatory sentence of 15 years in prison and a maximum sentence of up to 40 years in prison, a minimum of five years of supervised release, and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England; and Jennifer B. De La O, Director of Field Operations, U.S. Customs and Border Protection made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Rhode Island State Police and the Westerly (R.I.) Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Eric L. Hawkins of the Major Crimes Unit is prosecuting the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the DOJ’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . The details contained in the charging documents are allegations. The defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: United States Attorneys Available to Receive Election Complaints
body: Press Release United States Attorneys Available to Receive Election Complaints Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of New York United States Attorneys Joseph Nocella and Jamie McDonald announced today that Assistant United States Attorneys (AUSAs) will lead the efforts of their Offices in connection with the Justice Department’s nationwide Election Day Program for the upcoming November 3, 2026 general election, including the early voting period that in New York lasts from October 24, 2026 through November 1, 2026.  AUSAs Erik Paulsen and Andrew Grubin have been appointed to serve as the District Election Officers (DEO) for the Eastern District of New York, and AUSA David J. Kennedy has been appointed to serve as the DEO for the Southern District of New York.  In their capacity as DEOs, these AUSAs are responsible for overseeing the Districts’ handling of Election Day complaints of voting rights concerns, threats of violence to election officials or staff, and election fraud, in consultation with Justice Department Headquarters in Washington. “When citizens of the Eastern District of New York exercise the fundamental constitutional right to vote, the process must be legally safeguarded,” stated United States Attorney Nocella.  “Anyone seeking to corrupt the process will be brought to justice.  Our Office is ready to vigorously defend this sacred right.” United States Attorney McDonald stated, “Democracy depends upon elections that are free, fair, and accessible. The Southern District of New York is proud to continue its longstanding practice of maintaining an opportunity for voters to promptly report any issues that they may face at the polls that could diminish or impede their fundamental right to vote.” The Department of Justice plays an important role in deterring and combating discrimination and intimidation at the polls, threats of violence directed at election officials and poll workers, and election fraud.  The Department will address these violations wherever they occur.  The Department’s longstanding Election Day Program furthers these goals and also seeks to ensure public confidence in the electoral process by providing local points of contact within the Department for the public to report possible federal election law violations. Federal law protects against such crimes as threatening violence against election officials or staff, intimidating or bribing voters, buying and selling votes, impersonating voters, altering vote tallies, stuffing ballot boxes and marking ballots for voters against their wishes or without their input. It also contains special protections for the rights of voters, and provides that they can vote free from interference, including intimidation, and other acts designed to prevent or discourage people from voting or voting for the candidate of their choice.  The Voting Rights Act and the Americans with Disabilities Act protect the right of voters to mark their own ballot or to be assisted by a person of their choice (where voters need assistance because of disability or individuals who are limited English proficient). AUSAs will be on duty in this District while the polls are open. To respond to complaints of election fraud or voting rights concerns during the voting period that ends on November 3, 2026, and to ensure that such complaints are directed to the appropriate authorities, the United States Attorneys said that their Offices will be available to receive complaints at the following numbers through Tuesday, November 3, 2026: (646) 369-4739 for Manhattan, Bronx, Dutchess, Orange, Putnam, Rockland, Sullivan, and Westchester counties and and (718) 208-1182 for Brooklyn, Queens, Staten Island, Nassau, and Suffolk counties. Complaints about possible violations of the federal voting rights laws can also be made directly to the Civil Rights Division in Washington, DC by phone at 800-253-3931 or by complaint form at https://civilrights.justice.gov/. In addition, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) will have special agents available in each field office and resident agency throughout the country to receive allegations of election fraud and other election abuses on Election Day.  The FBI’s New York Field Office can be reached by the public at (212) 384-1000. In the case of a crime of violence or intimidation, please call 911 immediately and before contacting federal authorities.  State and local police have primary jurisdiction over polling places, and almost always have faster reaction capacity in an emergency. The United States Attorneys also noted that the following additional telephone numbers are available on Election Day for citizens to call for routine inquiries, such as where to vote or how late the polls are open, or to register complaints that may concern violations of New York State election laws: IN NEW YORK CITY New York City Board of Elections Main Office                            (866) 868-3692 TTY #: 212-487-5496 IN COUNTIES OUTSIDE NEW YORK CITY: County Boards of Elections Dutchess                                  (845) 486-2473 Nassau                                      (516) 571-8683 Orange                                      (845) 360-6500 Orange (Spanish language)      (855) 331-2444 Putnam                                     (845) 808-1300 Rockland                                  (845) 638-5172 Suffolk                                      (631) 852-4500 Sullivan                                    (845) 807-0400 Westchester                             (914) 995-5700 Contact John Marzulli Denise Taylor United States Attorney’s Office (718) 254-6323 Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - New York, Eastern

title: Over 250 New Immigration Cases Filed This Week in Western District of Texas
body: Press Release Over 250 New Immigration Cases Filed This Week in Western District of Texas Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Texas SAN ANTONIO – Federal prosecutors in the Western District of Texas filed 255 new immigration and immigration-related criminal cases from October 16 through October 22, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons. Charges were brought against alien smugglers and illegal aliens with past convictions for violent crimes, thefts, and multiple prior removals. Among the new cases, a U.S. citizen was arrested and charged with alien smuggling after she allegedly attempted to bring two undocumented minors into the U.S. via the Paso Del Norte Port of Entry. A criminal complaint alleges that Hilary Freyre presented her Texas identification card to a Customs and Border Protection officer (CBPO), along with two birth certificates—one from Texas and one from New Mexico—on behalf of two minors sitting in the backseat of her vehicle. The complaint alleges that while the CBPO was questioning the minors, Freyre repeatedly interrupted. A photo on her phone allegedly showed Freyre with two children but the officer noticed facial discrepancies between the children in the photo and the children in the vehicle. After Freyre was referred to secondary inspection, she allegedly stated the minors in the vehicle were not her children and that the birth certificates she presented actually belonged to her two biological children. Additionally, the complaint alleges, Freyre possessed $1,123 U.S. Dollars and $5400 Mexican pesos, despite claiming she had only $400 when she was initially asked. Oscar David Hernandez-Gonzalez aka Juan Higera-Medrano was arrested after he allegedly jumped out of a rail car during a Customs and Border Protection inspection on a train at the BNSF railyard in El Paso. Hernandez-Gonzalez, an illegal alien from Mexico, has been previously removed from the U.S. seven times, the last being in 2015. He’s been previously convicted of prostitution, sex battery, and burglary of a building, and now faces an illegal re-entry charge. Raul Azahel Zubia-Alvidrez , an illegal alien from Mexico, was found and arrested by U.S. Border Patrol agents just under 13 miles west of the Fort Hancock Port of Entry. Zubia-Alvidrez was deported for the first time in July 2025 but has multiple felony convictions dating back to 2012, including aggravated robbery, robbery, and aggravated assault. Juan Jose Aguilar-Gonzalez , an illegal alien from Mexico, was pulled over on Oct. 17 in Balcones Heights for driving without lights when required. According to a criminal complaint, Aguilar-Gonzalez provided the officer with a Mexican driver’s license and was positively identified as a Mexican national unlawfully in the United States. Aguilar-Gonzalez was arrested and turned over to Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Enforcement Removal Operations (ERO). Aguilar-Gonzalez is a convicted felon who, in May 2006, was convicted under the name Juan Carlos Turrubiartes-Cruz for illegal re-entry.  He was convicted again in 2008 under the same name for alien smuggling. Aguilar-Gonzalez has been removed from the U.S. at least three times and now faces his second illegal re-entry charge. Also an illegal alien from Mexico, Fermin Gonzalez-Sanchez was encountered by ICE ERO at the Bexar County Adult Detention Center following his arrest for criminal mischief. Gonzalez-Sanchez was transferred to ICE custody on Oct. 17. He has four prior convictions for illegal re-entry and now faces the same charge for the fifth time. He was most recently removed from the U.S. in July 2023. Ruben Salazar-Lopez , an illegal alien from Mexico, was arrested by U.S. Border Patrol agents on Oct. 17, near Eagle Pass. Salazar-Lopez is a convicted felon with two prior convictions for illegal re-entry. He was also convicted in 2017 for assault causing bodily injury to a family member. He’s been removed from the U.S. four times and now faces his third illegal re-entry charge. Anacleto Silva-Herrera is also an illegal alien from Mexico. He faces an illegal re-entry charge after being arrested near Del Rio on Oct. 16. In Dec. 2023, Silva-Herrera was convicted of possession with intent to distribute cocaine. He was sentenced to 37 months in prison. Silva-Herrera has been deported three times, the last being in July through Harlingen. In Austin, Galdino Cortes-Cortes was arrested in Manor on Oct. 18. Cortes-Cortes is an illegal alien from Mexico who was previously removed for the second time in March 2021, following a conviction for alien smuggling. Cortes-Cortes has also been previously convicted of a DWI and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. He’s currently charged with illegal re-entry. These cases were referred or supported by federal law enforcement partners, including ICE, U.S. Border Patrol, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the FBI, the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), with additional assistance from state and local law enforcement partners. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Texas comprises 68 counties located in the central and western areas of Texas, encompasses nearly 93,000 square miles and an estimated population of 7.6 million people. The district includes three of the five largest cities in Texas—San Antonio, Austin and El Paso—and shares 660 miles of common border with the Republic of Mexico. Indictments and criminal complaints are merely allegations and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. These cases are part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. ### Contact USATXW.MediaInquiry@usdoj.gov Updated October 23, 2026 Topics Operation Take Back America Human Smuggling Immigration Component USAO - Texas, Western

title: California Couple Sentenced for Trafficking Protected Wildlife
body: Press Release California Couple Sentenced for Trafficking Protected Wildlife Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Linh Luu and Kevin Le, a husband and wife of Anaheim, California, pleaded guilty today in federal court in Eugene, Oregon, to violating the Lacey Act. The court sentenced them to three years’ probation and a $10,000 fine each for their roles in trafficking wildlife between Oregon and Vietnam. Photo of tiger pelt trafficked by defendants, from sentencing memo in case number 26-cr-00297 in U.S. District Court for the District of Oregon. According to court documents and statements made in court, Luu and Le admitted that from September 2019 through May 2021, they processed $51,100 in payments to aid an individual in Vietnam to illegally move wildlife items to and from Oregon. The wildlife parts included American black bear gallbladders and cougar bones, all shipped to Vietnam; and lion teeth, segments from black rhinoceros and white rhinoceros horns, and a tiger pelt, all imported to Oregon. According to a sentencing submission filed by the government, Luu and Le met an undercover federal agent in December 2020 in a parking lot. They accepted $12,000 in cash as a down payment for part of a rhino horn and discussed ways to avoid U.S. banking regulations that could detect illicit transactions. They later each received nearly $5,000 in electronic payments for the horn segment, which was then shipped to Oregon disguised as a household decoration. The sale was discussed as a way to build trust for future, larger deals. Lion teeth trafficked by the defendants to Oregon, from sentencing memo in case number 26-cr-00297 in U.S. District Court for the District of Oregon. All of the wildlife that had parts trafficked in this case are listed under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), a treaty that the United States, Vietnam, and 183 other governments have signed to regulate commercial trade in species that are or may become extinct. Trade in listed species is prohibited without a permit, which the defendants did not receive. Black bears and cougars are native to Oregon and are prized by some for use in traditional Asian medicine. Lions, tigers, and black and white rhinoceroses are also protected under the Endangered Species Act. The Lacey Act is the country’s oldest wildlife trafficking statute and prohibits, among other things, buying or selling wildlife that was illegally imported or exported. Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General Adam Gustafson of the Justice Department’s Energy and Natural Resources Division (ENRD), U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford for the District of Oregon, and Assistant Director Douglas Ault of the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) made the announcement. Photo of a part of a rhino horn (left) and the same rhino horn part disguised as a house good to thwart customs (right), from sentencing memo in case number 26-cr-00297 in U.S. District Court for the District of Oregon. The USFWS’s Office of Law Enforcement investigated the case with assistance from Homeland Security Investigations and the Oregon State Police. Senior Trial Attorney Ryan Connors of ENRD’s Environmental Crimes Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney William McLaren for the District of Oregon prosecuted the case. Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Wildlife Components Energy and Natural Resources Division USAO - Oregon Press Release Number: 26-1254

title: Madison Man Sentenced to 140 Years in Prison for Child-Exploitation Crimes
body: Press Release Madison Man Sentenced to 140 Years in Prison for Child-Exploitation Crimes Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Alabama PROJECT SAFE CHILDHOOD HUNTSVILLE, Ala., A Madison man has been sentenced for child exploitation crimes, announced U.S. Attorney Phillip W. Williams Jr. U.S. District Court Judge Corey L. Maze sentenced Jason Brian Seay, 55, to 1,680 months (140 years) in prison. In February, Seay pleaded guilty to four counts of sexual exploitation of children and one count of possession of child pornography. According to the plea agreement, on March 6, 2025, FBI agents obtained a search warrant for Seay’s residence in Madison, Alabama. As a result of the search of Seay’s residence, agents seized more than 20 electronic devices. Examination of those devices revealed more than 500,000 images and videos of child pornography. Agents also discovered images and videos of child pornography that Seay produced. “This significant 140-year prison sentence demonstrates the seriousness of these crimes and shows unequivocally that there are real consequences for criminal conduct,” said U.S. Attorney Williams. “It is a just result that this defendant will spend the rest of his natural days in prison. The sentence cannot undo the harm that he inflicted on the victims, but it sends a clear message that my office and our law enforcement partners will tirelessly pursue justice and make our communities safe.” “The depravity and scale of Seay’s crimes are staggering, and today’s sentence ensures he will never again have the opportunity to harm a child,” said David R. Fitzgibbons, Special Agent in Charge, FBI Birmingham. “The FBI will relentlessly pursue anyone who exploits the most vulnerable among us. If you commit these offenses, we will find you, we will uncover the evidence, and you will be brought to justice.” This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC . If you suspect or become aware of the possible sexual exploitation of a child, please contact law enforcement.  Reports can also be filed with the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) or online at www.cybertipline.org . The FBI investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney R. Leann White prosecuted the case. Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Alabama, Northern

title: Fresno man arrested with more than 4 kilograms of fentanyl
body: Press Release Fresno man arrested with more than 4 kilograms of fentanyl Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of California FRESNO, Calif. — Isaac Benito Lopez, 39, of Fresno, was arrested and charged by complaint with possession with intent to distribute fentanyl, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced. According to court documents, on Oct. 21, 2026, Lopez drove to a Fresno restaurant to sell 4 kilograms of fentanyl. Investigators arrested Lopez. Later, investigators executed a search warrant at his residence, where they discovered nearly an additional 400 grams of fentanyl. Investigators also discovered at the residence an AR-style rifle with a drum-style magazine containing in excess of 70 rounds of ammunition for the firearm. “This arrest reflects our Office’s commitment to disrupting high‑volume narcotics pipelines and targeting individuals engaged in trafficking fentanyl into the community,” said U.S. Attorney Grant. “Coordinated enforcement efforts with federal, state, and local partners remain central to identifying distribution networks, executing intelligence‑driven interdictions, and removing lethal substances from circulation. This arrest demonstrates how collaborative investigative work can neutralize immediate threats to public safety.” “DEA will not stop targeting fentanyl dealers who peddle poison in our communities,” said Drug Enforcement Administration Special Agent In Charge Bob P. Beris. “DEA will work shoulder to shoulder with our partners to bring these drug dealers to justice.” “The Fresno Police Department works closely with our federal partners to maximize our impact on eradicating narcotic sales, including sales of fentanyl, in our community. Our officers are proud to be a part of the team that brought the sales of fentanyl to an end by the suspect in this case. We look forward to working with our local, state and federal partners to continue the effort to remove this deadly drug from our streets and arrest those who dare to sell it within our city,” said Fresno Police Department Chief of Police Mindy Casto. This case is the product of an investigation by the Drug Enforcement Administration and Fresno Police Department. Assistant United States Attorney Chan Hee Chu is prosecuting the case. If convicted, Lopez faces a mandatory minimum statutory sentence of 10 years in prison with a maximum statutory sentence of life in prison, and up to a $10,000,000 fine. Any sentence, however, is at the discretion of the sentencing court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the Federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables. The charges are only allegations; the defendant is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. Updated October 23, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Opioids Component USAO - California, Eastern

title: Nine Pennsylvania Non-Citizens Charged with Illegally Voting
body: Press Release Nine Pennsylvania Non-Citizens Charged with Illegally Voting Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Pennsylvania PHILADELPHIA/HARRISBURG – Nine Pennsylvania residents have been charged separately with illegally voting, despite knowing that they were not U.S. citizens, announced David Metcalf, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania, and Brian Miller, United States Attorney for the Middle District of Pennsylvania. Under both federal and state law, only United States citizens may vote in Pennsylvania. The cases were investigated by Homeland Security Investigations (“HSI”). “Upholding the integrity of our elections, and the right of American citizens to determine the outcome, is non-negotiable,” said U.S. Attorney Metcalf.  “Our democracy depends on it.” “These cases are important because the crime of illegal voting undermines the integrity of our elections and harms citizens by stealing the power of our votes,” said U.S. Attorney Miller. “Illegal voting is not a victimless crime but a serious affront to the principles of our democratic republic.” “Illegally casting a ballot in a federal election corrupts the electoral process and diminishes the voice of every lawful voter,” said HSI Philadelphia Special Agent in Charge Nathan Abel. “These alleged violations undermine public confidence in our democratic institutions and harm the citizens whose votes are entitled to determine our nation’s future. HSI will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to investigate election-related crimes and hold accountable those who violate federal law. In the Eastern District of Pennsylvania: Artur Kopacz , 50, of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, was charged by information with two counts of voting by an alien. The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Poland and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2022 and 2024 general elections. If convicted, Kopacz faces a maximum possible sentence of a fine, two years in prison, or both. Osmal Loy , 70, of Fountain Hill, Pa., was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Cuba and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2024 general election. Yehuda Peer , 30, of Merion Station, Pa., was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Israel and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2024 general election. Alfredo Santiesteban , 73, also of Philadelphia, was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Cuba, illegally voted in the 2024 general election. If convicted, Loy, Peer, and Santiesteban each face a maximum possible sentence of a fine, one year in prison, or both. In the Middle District of Pennsylvania: Joyce Donovan , 38, of Selinsgrove, Pa., was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Kenya and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2024 general election. Inna Henry , 52, of Harrisburg, Pa., was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien.The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Russia and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2022 and 2024 general elections. Nourten Kuruju , 64, of Luzerne, Pa., was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Greece and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2022 general election. Nina Nyawara , 21, of Selinsgrove, Pa., was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien.The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Kenya and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2024 general election. Joyce Pitts , 80, of Effort, Pa., was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of the Netherlands and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2024 general election. If convicted, these defendants each face a maximum possible sentence of a fine, one year in prison, or both. The charges and allegations contained in the informations are merely accusations. Every defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty in court. # # # Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - Pennsylvania, Middle

body: Press Release Two Men Charged with Conspiracy to Produce and Production of Child Sexual Abuse Material Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Pennsylvania WILLIAMSPORT - The United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Pennsylvania announced that Morris W. Reese, 65, and Michael H. Woomer, 67, both of Tyrone, Pennsylvania, were indicted by a federal grand jury on a four-count indictment charging conspiracy to produce and production of child sexual abuse material. According to United States Attorney Brian D. Miller, the indictment alleges that Reese and Woomer conspired with others to produce child pornography from November 2024 to November of 2025. The indictment alleges that Reese produced child pornography with two minor victims and Woomer produced child pornography with one minor victim. The FBI Philadelphia’s Capital Area Resident Agency, the Pennsylvania State Police, and the Centre County District Attorney’s Office investigated the matter. Assistant U.S. Attorney Alisan V. Martin is prosecuting the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC. The maximum penalty under federal law is up to thirty years of imprisonment, a term of supervised release following imprisonment, and a fine. A sentence following the finding of guilt is imposed by the Judge after consideration of the applicable federal sentencing statutes and the Federal Sentencing Guidelines. Indictments are only allegations. All persons charged are presumed to be innocent unless and until found guilty in court. # # # Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Pennsylvania, Middle

title: Auglaize County Man Sentenced to 17 Years in Prison for Child Pornography Charges
body: Press Release Auglaize County Man Sentenced to 17 Years in Prison for Child Pornography Charges Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Ohio TOLEDO, Ohio – A 33-year-old man has been sentenced to federal prison for Child Sexual Abuse Materials charges. Seth Jacob Schwerin, of Wapakoneta, Ohio, was sentenced to 204 months (17 years) in prison by U.S. District Judge James R. Knepp, after pleading guilty to: •    Receipt and Distribution of Child Pornography •    Transportation of Child Pornography Schwerin was also ordered to serve 15 years of supervised release after imprisonment and pay $5,000 toward the Justice for Victims of Trafficking Act, which was established in 2015 to provide justice for victims of trafficking. According to court documents, federal agents were investigating a cybertip about Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) files uploaded to an online platform, as well as distributed to an undercover agent, and Schwerin was subsequently identified.  During a search warrant executed at his residence, Schwerin’s electronic devices were seized and forensically examined. Investigators found that on several occasions, from approximately August 2021 to January 2025, Schwerin received, possessed, distributed, and transported images and videos of minors engaged in sexually explicit conduct. Additionally, investigators learned that he committed some of his CSAM activity during work hours. The investigation was led by the Homeland Security Investigations Cleveland Office, the Ohio Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force, the Wapakoneta Police Department, and the Auglaize County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant United States Attorney Tracey Ballard Tangeman led the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. The initiative is led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices throughout the country and marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, visit justice.gov/PSC. To report child exploitation, please visit cybertipline.org, or call 1-800-843-5678, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Contact Jessica Salas Novak Jessica.Salas.Novak@usdoj.gov Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Ohio, Northern

title: New Orleans Woman Sentenced for $1.3 Million Covid Fraud and Tax Evasion
body: Press Release New Orleans Woman Sentenced for $1.3 Million Covid Fraud and Tax Evasion Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – AMANDA CLAYBORNE-WILLIAMS (“CLAYBORNE-WILLIAMS”) , age 45, was sentenced on October 20, 2026 by U.S. District Judge Jay C. Zainey, after previously pleading guilty to wire fraud, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Section 1343, and tax evasion, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Section 7201, announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle. According to court documents, between April 2020 and January 2021, CLAYBORNE-WILLIAMS submitted twelve false and misleading applications for loans through the Paycheck Protection Program (“PPP”) and the Economic Injury Disaster Loan (“EIDL”) program, seeking approximately $1.3 million on behalf of four entities. Each application contained materially false information regarding the number of employees, average monthly payroll, gross receipts, and/or gross revenue for the relevant entity.  As a result of these applications, CLAYBORNE-WILLIAMS received approximately $447,305.98 through fraud. CLAYBORNE-WILLIAMS then used the PPP and EIDL funds for personal and unauthorized expenses, including for a mortgage payment on her personal residence. CLAYBORNE-WILLIAMS did not repay the EIDLs as required, and the loans went into default.  Moreover, the defendant submitted a forgiveness application to the Small Business Administration (“SBA”) for each PPP loan, in which she falsely certified that she had spent the loan proceeds on permissible items and payroll expenses. As a result, the SBA forgave eight PPP loans that CLAYBORNE-WILLIAMS had obtained. In addition, CLAYBORNE-WILLIAMS attempted to evade paying income tax for tax years 2011-2014 and 2016-2020.  In 2022, IRS Collections opened an investigation because CLAYBORNE-WILLIAMS owed significant overdue taxes.  Even though CLAYBORNE-WILLIAMS had sufficient income to make payments on her back taxes in 2022, she sought and obtained “Currently Not Collectible/Unable to Pay” account status.  In November of 2022, CLAYBORNE-WILLIAMS submitted a false form to the Internal Revenue Service (“IRS”), on which she failed to report bank accounts, credit cards, loans, and business information.  Due to her evasive conduct, CLAYBORNE-WILLIAMS caused a loss of $360,466.24 to the IRS. Judge Zainey sentenced CLAYBORNE-WILLIAMS to five (5) years of probation, to include one (1) year of home detention and one-hundred and fifty (150) hours of community service.  A mandatory $200 special assessment fee was also imposed.  Judge Zainey also ordered CLAYBORNE-WILLIAMS to pay restitution in the amount of $447,305.98 to the SBA and $360,466.24 to the IRS. For more information on the Department of Justice’s response to the pandemic, please visit https://www.justice.gov/coronavirus . Anyone with information about allegations of attempted fraud involving COVID-19 can report it by calling the Department of Justice’s National Center for Disaster Fraud (NCDF) Hotline at 866-720-5721 or via the NCDF Web Complaint Form at https://www.justice.gov/disaster-fraud/ncdf-disaster-complaint-form . U.S. Attorney Courcelle praised the work of the Internal Revenue Service on this investigation. Assistant United States Attorney Maria M. Carboni of the Public Integrity Unit is in charge of the prosecution. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The core mission of the Fraud Division is to zealously investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars.  Department of Justice efforts to combat fraud support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. *       *       * Contact Shane M. Jones Public Information Officer United States Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of Louisiana United States Department of Justice Updated October 23, 2026 Topics COVID-Related Fraud Tax Component USAO - Louisiana, Eastern

title: Dyersburg Man Sentenced to 31 Years in Federal Prison for Drug Trafficking - Again
body: Press Release Dyersburg Man Sentenced to 31 Years in Federal Prison for Drug Trafficking - Again Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Tennessee Jackson, TN – A federal judge has sentenced Vinson Brent Taylor , 46 , of Dyersburg, Tennessee, to a total term of 31 years in federal prison for drug trafficking offenses. D. Michael Dunavant, United States Attorney for the Western District of Tennessee, announced the sentence today. According to evidence presented in court, in August of 2024, an officer with the Dyersburg Police Department was on patrol duty when he witnessed two men fighting in front of a residence. Both men fled the scene upon the officer’s arrival. While investigating the scene, the officer came across a rental vehicle that was left running and had its driver-side door wide open. The vehicle contained a large quantity of crack cocaine and over 250 fentanyl pills, as well as marijuana, ecstasy, and an unknown substance later tested and identified to be methamphetamine. Near the center console of the vehicle were Taylor’s cellphone and a car rental agreement in his name. A hat with distinctive embroidery was found near the vehicle; and a forensic analysis conducted by the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation determined that the hat contained Taylor's DNA. Taylor's criminal history includes at least three other convictions for selling cocaine, three convictions for evading law enforcement, six convictions for possessing and trafficking marijuana, a conviction for retaliating against a law enforcement officer, two convictions for assaults, and over 46 prior arrests. On May 5, 2026, a federal jury found Taylor guilty on two counts of trafficking crack cocaine and fentanyl. At a sentencing hearing on October 20, 2026, United States District Court Judge S. Thomas Anderson noted the serious nature of the crime as well as Taylor’s extensive criminal history, and sentenced Taylor to 30 years’ imprisonment. Taylor previously served a 151-month sentence in federal prison for trafficking crack cocaine and was on federal supervised release at the time he committed this crime. The government presented additional evidence that Taylor had engaged in other criminal conduct while on supervised release, including possessing over 800 grams of marijuana in April 2024 and evading police in October 2024, which resulted in Taylor being sentenced to an additional year of imprisonment. There is no parole in the federal system. U.S. Attorney D. Michael Dunavant said, “Taylor is a hard-headed recidivist drug dealer who was brazenly distributing deadly fentanyl into our rural communities while on supervised release for the same conduct. He clearly did not learn his lesson from his prior 12 ½-year prison sentence, so he will now be removed from West Tennessee until he is 77 years old.” “Our agency, as well as our law enforcement partners, will continue to vigorously pursue those who fuel this deadly epidemic by illegally distributing these deadly substances,” said TBI Director David Rausch. This case was investigated by the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, Dyersburg Police Department, United States Secret Service, and the Federal Bureau of Prisons. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Immanuel Chioco and Adam Davis prosecuted this case on behalf of the government. ### For more information, please contact our Media Relations Team at USATNW.Media@usdoj.gov . Follow the U.S. Attorney’s Office on Facebook or on X at @WDTNNews for office news and updates. Updated October 23, 2026 Component USAO - Tennessee, Western

title: Convicted sex offender sent to prison after 911 call
body: Press Release Convicted sex offender sent to prison after 911 call Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Kansas WICHITA, KAN. – A convicted child sex offender was sentenced to 151 months in prison for having child sexual abuse material (CSAM). According to court documents, Michael Eugene Watley, 59, of Wichita pleaded guilty to one count of possession of child pornography. In July 2025, Watley allowed someone to use his cellphone.  While using Watley's phone, the person discovered CSAM images on the device. After the person confronted Watley, they saw Watley move the images into a secure folder protected with a pin code. The witness then called 911, and law enforcement responded. A forensic review of Watley's phone and laptop revealed CSAM including images of prepubescent children under the age of 12 subjected to sex acts. In 2006, Watley was convicted in Sedgwick County District Court of Attempted Aggravated Indecent Liberties with a Child and sentenced to 44 months in prison. “While law enforcement works tirelessly to apprehend child predators, they can’t be everywhere. In this case, a witness saw that Mr. Watley was engaged in sexually deviant behavior that victimizes children and made the brave decision to contact the police,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “Please, if you see something, say something.” The Kansas Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) investigated the case. Project Safe Childhood This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. title: Former Partner at Broker-Dealer Firm Pleads Guilty to Securities Fraud Conspiracy
body: Press Release Former Partner at Broker-Dealer Firm Pleads Guilty to Securities Fraud Conspiracy Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Jersey Unlawfully Made Millions of Dollars in Illicit Profits from Insider Trading TRENTON, N.J. – A former partner at a New Jersey broker-dealer firm admitted to conspiring to commit securities fraud involving insider trading in a special purpose acquisition company that netted millions of dollars in illegal profits, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced. Christopher Matthaei, 48, of Brielle, New Jersey, pleaded guilty yesterday before U.S. District Judge Georgette Castner in Trenton federal court to a Superseding Information charging him with conspiracy to commit securities fraud. According to documents filed in the cases and statements made in court: Matthaei worked as a partner and senior salesperson at a broker-dealer with offices in Red Bank, New Jersey.  Matthaei conspired with his then-client and close personal friend, Sean Wygovsky, to engage in an insider trading scheme involving material nonpublic information regarding a special purpose acquisition company (“SPAC-1”).  Like other SPACs, SPAC-1 was a publicly traded shell company that existed solely for the purpose of merging with another company.  After Wygovsky learned through his role as a trader at a Canada-based asset management company that SPAC-1 was engaged in confidential merger discussions with a target company, Wygovsky shared that material nonpublic information with Matthaei on or about May 28, 2020 using an encrypted messaging platform, with the intention that Matthaei would trade on and profit from that nonpublic information.  Wygovsky previously pleaded guilty on or about May 25, 2023, to securities fraud related to this scheme. Based on that tip and other tips of material nonpublic information from Wygovsky concerning SPAC-1’s merger discussions, Matthaei repeatedly purchased SPAC-1 securities between May 29, 2020 and June 18, 2020, despite knowing that Wygovsky was prohibited from sharing that information with him and that Matthaei was prohibited from trading on it.  After SPAC-1 publicly announced on June 19, 2020 that it had entered into a merger agreement with the target company, Matthaei’s positions in SPAC-1 substantially increased in value.  That same day, Matthaei began selling his SPAC-1 securities, ultimately generating illicit profits in the total amount of nearly $1.5 million.  Overall, as part of his plea agreement, Matthaei agreed that he earned profits in a total amount of between $2 million and $3.5 million after factoring in other relevant conduct. The charge of conspiracy to commit securities fraud carries a maximum potential penalty of 5 years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000, or twice the gross gain to the defendant or loss to the victim, whichever is greatest.  Sentencing for Matthaei is scheduled for February 25, 2027. U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents of the FBI, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy in Newark, with the investigation leading to the charges and guilty plea.  U.S. Attorney Frazer also thanked the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and the Criminal Prosecution Assistance Group at the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority for assistance throughout the investigation. The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jennifer S. Kozar, Rachelle M. Navarro, and Casey S. Smith of the Criminal Division in Newark. ### Defense counsel: Michael Critchley, Esq. Amy Luria, Esq. Armando Suarez, Esq. matthaei.information.pdf Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Securities, Commodities, & Investment Fraud Component USAO - New Jersey Press Release Number: 26-234

title: Project Safe Schools: Former Carrollton-Farmers Branch ISD teacher indicted for making false statements to the FBI
body: Press Release Project Safe Schools: Former Carrollton-Farmers Branch ISD teacher indicted for making false statements to the FBI Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas DALLAS — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a former Carrollton Farmers Branch Independent School District teacher was indicted for making false statements to federal agents during an investigation into his alleged inappropriate conversations with students using the school’s internal messaging platforms. Landon Beck, 32, was originally charged by criminal complaint for allegedly making materially false statements to the FBI during interviews conducted on July 9 and July 30. A grand jury returned an indictment on Oct. 7. “When federal agents investigate allegations involving the safety of students, they expect truthful answers, rather than obfuscation and outright lies,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “By allegedly lying to the FBI, Mr. Beck chose to obstruct that investigation and blame his inappropriate conduct on special needs students instead of accepting accountability for his actions. This indictment makes clear that Project Safe Schools will utilize every tool in the toolchest to hold offenders accountable.” “Providing false information to the FBI or otherwise obstructing a federal investigation is a serious offense. These actions undermine our ability to uncover the facts and enforce the law,” said FBI Dallas Special Agent in Charge R. Joseph Rothrock. “The FBI remains committed to protecting the most vulnerable in our community and ensuring that anyone who obstructs investigations to conceal criminal conduct is held fully accountable.” According to the indictment, Beck was employed by CFB-ISD in March 2023. Around that time, an internal school district inquiry identified concerns about Beck’s communications with students through the school’s messaging system. The FBI’s investigation included reviewing reports provided by the district and other relevant materials. The indictment alleges that Beck sent inappropriate content to students, including the following: photos of an adult male defecating outdoors; webpage photos of a digital rectal exam; photos of adult men kissing; and cartoon or “meme” photos of male genitals. The conversation also included discussing a pornography website with a special needs student and calling a special needs student “wee ta did. During two separate interviews, Beck allegedly denied sending inappropriate digital content to students and claimed that any such messages originated from special needs students rather than himself. If convicted, Beck faces up to five years federal prison in prison. The FBI’s Dallas Field Office conducted the investigation with assistance from the Carrollton Police Department and the Texas Education Agency. Assistant U.S. Attorney Theodore V. Parran, III is prosecuting the case. Project Safe Schools is a federal initiative aimed at protecting students, enforcing accountability and restoring transparency in public schools across North Texas. Project Safe Schools directly targets failures in mandatory reporting of educator misconduct and combats the practice known as “passing the trash,” where educators with known misconduct issues move between schools without disclosure of their prior wrongdoing. Project Safe Schools’ goals are to: Enforce mandatory reporting requirements tied to federal education programs. Hold school districts, administrators and teachers accountable through civil and criminal enforcement. Increase transparency in educator misconduct investigations. Strengthen student safety across schools in North Texas. An indictment is merely an allegation, and a defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in a court of law. ### Documents landon_beck_indictment.pdf Contact Public Affairs Division U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of Texas USATXN.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 23, 2026 Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Texas, Northern

title: Illegal Alien Sentenced for Unlawful Reentry
body: Press Release Illegal Alien Sentenced for Unlawful Reentry Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Defendant arrested several times for operating under the influence BOSTON – An Ecuadorian national unlawfully residing in Milford, Mass. has been sentenced in federal court in Worcester for illegally reentering the United States after deportation. The defendant was previously deported from the United States and arrested several times for driving under the influence in Massachusetts. Luis Rolando Clavijo Tacuri, 32, was sentenced on Oct. 20, 2026 by U.S. District Court Judge Margaret R. Guzman to time served (85 days). The defendant is now subject to deportation proceedings. The government recommended a sentence of seven months in prison. In September 2026 , Tacuri pleaded guilty to one count of unlawful reentry of a deported alien.  Tacuri was charged in August 2026 . Tacuri was first encountered by immigration officials in October 2015, while he was incarcerated on charges of operating under the influence in Holliston, Mass. At the time, it was Tacuri’s third operating under the influence offense. Tacuri was subsequently placed into removal proceedings and deported to Ecuador in December 2016. Sometime after his removal, Tacuri illegally reentered the United States. On May 27, 2024, Tacuri was encountered by law enforcement in Milford, Mass. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England; and David T. Wesling, Acting Field Office Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Enforcement and Removal Operations in Boston made the announcement. Assistant U.S. Attorney Brendan O’Shea of the Worcester Branch Office prosecuted the case. Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Immigration Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: Man Sentenced to 260 Months in Prison for Sexual Exploitation of a 2-year-old Female Minor
body: Press Release Man Sentenced to 260 Months in Prison for Sexual Exploitation of a 2-year-old Female Minor Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Puerto Rico SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – On October 21, 2026, United States District Court Judge Aida Delgado Colón sentenced Ángel Javier Santos-Méndez to 260 months (21 years and 8 months) in prison followed by 20 years of supervised release for child exploitation charges against a female minor victim. Santos-Méndez, 34, from Caguas, PR, was indicted on October 30, 2025, arrested on November 5, 2025, and pleaded guilty on April 16, 2026. According to court documents, on September 22, 2025, Ángel Javier Santos-Méndez knowingly employed, used, and coerced his 2-year-old female minor daughter to engage in sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing visual depictions of such conduct, that is images of lascivious exhibition of the minor’s genital area. The visual depictions were produced using his cellular device. Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Puerto Rico Crimes Against Children Task Force received information from the Police of Puerto Rico regarding the allegations that Defendant had sexually abused and recorded sexually explicit images of the minor female. The investigation led to the arrest and prosecution of Santos-Méndez. “Child sexual abuse is a depraved criminal act that harms the most innocent among us,” said Héctor Ramírez-Carbó, Acting United States Attorney for the District of Puerto Rico. “While prosecuting a predator like Santos-Méndez can’t undo that damage, his prison sentence prevents him from causing further harm and provides his victim justice. I thank our dedicated team of prosecutors, victim witness coordinator, support personnel, as well as our dedicated law enforcement partners and their relentless efforts against child exploitation and to bring offenders to justice.” “Defenseless children may not have a voice, but they are not helpless. This individual abused his own 2-year-old daughter to produce child sexual abuse material, a heinous act that demands accountability,” said Yariel Ramos, Acting Special Agent in Charge, HSI San Juan. “HSI is vigilant and will protect children who were not protected by the very people responsible for their care. This sentence sends a clear message: HSI and our law enforcement partners will relentlessly pursue offenders and hold them accountable so they won’t hurt one more victim.” The Department of Homeland Security Investigations investigated the case with the collaboration of the Puerto Rico Police Department. Assistant United States Attorney (AUSA) Elba Gorbea of the Child Exploitation and Immigration Unit, prosecuted the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc. ### Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Puerto Rico Press Release Number: 2026-113

title: Indictment Charges Bridgeport Man with Offense Stemming from New Year’s Shooting
body: Press Release Indictment Charges Bridgeport Man with Offense Stemming from New Year’s Shooting Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, P.J. O’Brien, Special Agent in Charge of the New Haven Division of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and Bridgeport Police Chief Roderick Porter today announced that a federal grand jury in Bridgeport has returned an indictment charging JONATHAN BOHANNON, 38, of Bridgeport, with an offense stemming from a shooting incident earlier this year. As alleged in court documents and statements made in court, in the early morning hours of January 1, 2026, Bohannon shot an employee of the Mystique Gentleman’s Club, located on Main Street in Bridgeport.  Bohannon and the shooting victim had been involved in an altercation of the club earlier that night.  Investigators recovered a single shell casing at the spot of shooting.  The bullet remains inside the shooting victim. The indictment alleges that Bohannon’s criminal history includes a felony drug conviction in state court, and federal convictions for narcotics trafficking and firearm possession offenses for which Bohannon was sentenced to 160 months of imprisonment. He was released from federal prison in September 2025. The indictment charges Bohannon with unlawful possession of ammunition by a felon, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of 15 years.  Bohannon, who is on federal supervised release, faces additional penalties if he is found to have violated the conditions of his supervised release. The indictment was returned on October 8, 2026.  On October 21, 2026, Bohannon, who had been detained in state custody since May 2026, appeared before U.S. Magistrate Judge Thomas O. Farrish in Hartford and pleaded not guilty to the charge. U.S. Attorney Sullivan stressed that an indictment is not evidence of guilt.  Charges are only allegations, and a defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. This investigation is being conducted by the FBI Bridgeport Safe Streets Task Force and the Bridgeport Police Department.  The Task Force is composed of personnel from the FBI, Connecticut State Police, and the Bridgeport, Fairfield, Norwalk, Trumbull, and Westport Police Departments.  The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Rahul Kale. Updated October 23, 2026 Topics Project Safe Neighborhoods Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Component USAO - Connecticut

title: Duxbury Man Sentenced to Over Five Years in Prison for Distributing Child Pornography
body: Press Release Duxbury Man Sentenced to Over Five Years in Prison for Distributing Child Pornography Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts BOSTON - A Duxbury man was sentenced yesterday in federal court in Boston for distribution of child sexual abuse material (CSAM). Daniel Debreczeni, 35, was sentenced by U.S. District Court Chief Judge Denise J. Casper to 63 months in prison, to be followed by five years of supervised release. Debreczeni pleaded guilty in April 2026 after being arrested and charged in August 2025 . Between Nov. 29, 2023 and Dec. 12, 2023, Debreczeni distributed three videos containing CSAM in a private chat room dedicated to child sexual abuse on the Kik Messenger platform. The children in the three videos appeared to be between approximately two, three and eight years old. During a subsequent search of Debreczeni’s residence, five images and 19 videos depicting CSAM were located on Debreczeni’s Kik account. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Massachusetts State Police and the Duxbury and Quincy Police Departments. Assistant U.S. Attorney David Tobin of the Major Crimes Unit prosecuted the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the DOJ’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identify and rescue victims.
