title: Boston Man Pleads Guilty to Being a Felon in Possession of a Firearm and Ammunition
body: Press Release Boston Man Pleads Guilty to Being a Felon in Possession of a Firearm and Ammunition Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts BOSTON – A Boston man pleaded guilty on Oct. 21, 2026 in federal court in Boston to being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition after being found in possession of a semi-automatic rifle and assorted ammunition. Elydes Zorrilla, 22, pleaded guilty to one count of being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition. U.S. District Court Judge Nathaniel M. Gorton scheduled sentencing for Jan. 20, 2026. Zorrilla was indicted by a federal grand jury in May 2026. On Dec. 30, 2025, the Zorrilla possessed a semi-automatic rifle and assorted ammunition. The defendant possessed this firearm and ammunition in the course of selling the firearm and ammunition to an undercover agent. Zorrilla is prohibited from possessing a firearm and ammunition due to his prior state court convictions, including a prior conviction in Boston Municipal Court for assault and battery with a dangerous weapon. The charge of being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition provides for a sentence of up to 15 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Thomas Greco, Special Agent in Charge of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by Boston Police Department, Boston Housing Authority, and Massachusetts State Police. Assistant U.S. Attorney Allegra K. Flamm of the Major Crimes Unit is prosecuting the case. Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: Three Defendants Charged with Offenses for Voting as Non-Citizens
body: Press Release Three Defendants Charged with Offenses for Voting as Non-Citizens Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of New York BROOKLYN, NY – Three defendants were presented in federal court in Brooklyn this week following charges of various offenses related to illegal voting in federal elections. Eoin Cranney, a citizen of Ireland and a lawful permanent resident of the United States, was charged by indictment with making a false claim of citizenship in order to vote and voting by an alien in a federal election.  Ronald Sheldon Baird, a citizen of Guyana and a lawful permanent resident of the United States, was charged by misdemeanor complaint with voting by an alien in a federal election. Karlene Daniels Samuels, a citizen of Jamaica and a lawful permanent resident of the United States, was charged by misdemeanor complaint with voting by an alien in a federal election. Cranney was arraigned on October 20, 2026, before United States Magistrate Judge James R. Cho.  Baird and Samuels were presented on October 22, 2026, before Judge Cho. Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, and Pete Gizas, Acting Special Agent in Charge, Homeland Security Investigations, New York (HSI New York), announced the charges. “It is illegal for non-citizens to knowingly vote in federal elections,” stated United States Attorney Nocella.  “Our Office will prosecute those who illegally vote in order to preserve the integrity of our electoral process.” As alleged in the indictment against him, Cranney, who was not a citizen of the United States, submitted a fraudulent voter registration application to the Board of Elections in the City of New York (the “NYC BOE”) in which he falsely asserted that he was a United States citizen.  Cranney then voted in the federal general election held on November 5, 2024.  In a voluntary interview with federal agents, Cranney admitted, in substance and in part, that he was not a United States citizen, that he had registered to vote in 2024, and that he had voted in the November 5, 2024 federal general election knowing that he was not a United States citizen. As alleged in the complaint against him, Baird, who is not a citizen of the United States, submitted a fraudulent voter registration application to the NYC BOE, in which he falsely asserted that he was a United States citizen.  Baird voted in the federal general election held on November 5, 2024.  In a voluntary interview with federal agents, Baird admitted, in substance and in part, that he was not a United States citizen and that he had voted in the November 5, 2024 federal general election knowing that he was not a United States citizen. As alleged in the complaint against her, Samuels, who is not a citizen of the United States, submitted a fraudulent voter registration application to the NYC BOE, in which she falsely asserted that she was a United States citizen.  Baird voted in the federal general election held on November 5, 2024.  In a voluntary interview with federal agents, Baird admitted, in substance and in part, that she was not a United States citizen and that she had voted in the November 5, 2024 federal general election knowing that she was not a United States citizen. The charges in the indictment and complaints are allegations, and the defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. If convicted, Cranney faces a maximum sentence of up to six years in prison, and Baird and Samuels face a sentence of up to one year in prison. The Defendants : EOIN CRANNEY Age: 35 Oakland Gardens, New York E.D.N.Y. Docket No. 26-CR-293 (NGG) RONALD SHELDON BAIRD Age: 47 Laurelton, New York E.D.N.Y. Docket No. 26-MJ-191 KARLENE DANIELS SAMUELS Age: 55 Saint Albans, New York E.D.N.Y. title: Boyfriend Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison for Killing His Romantic Partner
body: Press Release Boyfriend Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison for Killing His Romantic Partner Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia USADC.Media@usdoj.gov WASHINGTON – Tyjuan Bazemore, 35, of Washington, D.C., was sentenced to 20 years in prison today for the shooting death of his girlfriend, 27-year-old Nyesha Tranae Walden-Hatcher, on February 2, 2026, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. Bazemore pleaded guilty to one count of second-degree murder while armed on July 10, 2026. Superior Court Judge Todd Edelman sentenced Bazemore to 20 years in prison to be followed by five years of supervised release. According to the government’s evidence, Bazemore and Walden-Hatcher were inside 3120 16 th Street Apartment #13 after going to the liquor store.  While inside the apartment, Bazemore shot Walden-Hatcher in the head, causing her death. After he shot Walden-Hatcher, Bazemore proceeded to run upstairs and then returned downstairs several times.  Bazemore put on shoes and a hoodie, attempted to knock down the camera at the foot of the staircase on the first floor, and eventually left the apartment complex. At approximately 2:57 a.m., members of the Metropolitan Police Department were dispatched to 3120 16 th Street Apartment #13. After no response at the door, MPD pushed open the door and located Walden-Hatcher, unresponsive on the floor, suffering from a single gunshot wound to the head. Despite all life-saving efforts, she was pronounced dead at the scene. After the murder, Bazemore fled to Connecticut where he was located and extradited back to D.C. At the time of this killing, Bazemore had two open domestic violence assault cases concerning the victim. Bazemore was ordered, as a condition of his release, to stay away from her and not to possess firearms. This case is being investigated by the Metropolitan Police Department and prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Stephanie Dinan. Tyjuan Bazemore running towards the staircase with a black handgun. 2026 CF1 003647 Contact USADC.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 23, 2026 Topics Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Component USAO - District of Columbia

title: Harlingen couple sentenced in multimillion-dollar Medicare fraud scheme
body: Press Release Harlingen couple sentenced in multimillion-dollar Medicare fraud scheme Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Texas DOJ’s National Fraud Enforcement Division investigates and prosecutes those who commit fraud against the American People BROWNSVILLE, Texas – The operators of a durable medical equipment company have been sentenced for defrauding Medicare. Jeremiah Yzaguirre, 47, and his wife, Maria Luisa Yzaguirre, 47, both of Harlingen, pleaded guilty April 22, 2025. U.S. District Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr. imposed a 110-month-term of imprisonment for Jeremiah Yzaguirre, while Maria Luisa Yzaguirre received 80 months. Both must also serve three years of supervised release following their sentences. They were both further ordered to pay $9,248,976 in restitution to Medicare and a $25,000 fine. The Yzaguirres operated a business called Southwest Medical Homepatient in Harlingen. The business was enrolled in the Medicare program as a provider of DME and services. Among other things, the business purported to provide parts and repairs for power wheelchairs. Between 2019 and 2023, the Yzaguirres caused Medicare to be billed approximately $14 million for power wheelchairs, parts, and repairs for only 37 individual Medicare beneficiaries. There were multiple instances in which they billed Medicare for hundreds of parts and repairs for a single beneficiary’s wheelchair. As part of their pleas, both admitted they were paid millions of dollars for parts and repairs that were never actually performed or provided. They also admitted that, for one specific Medicare beneficiary, they billed approximately $736,072 for parts and repairs by falsely claiming to have replaced certain expensive parts hundreds of times. As part of their pleas, the couple admitted they received millions of dollars for parts and repairs that were never performed or provided. They both acknowledged billing Medicare approximately $736,072 for parts and repairs for one specific beneficiary, falsely claiming to have replaced expensive parts hundreds of times. The investigation revealed the Yzaguirres used proceeds of the fraud to purchase cryptocurrency, a vehicle, electronics, miscellaneous collectibles, and purses. Both will remain in custody pending transfer to a Federal Bureau of Prisons facility to be determined in the near future. The FBI, Department of Health and Human Services - Office of Inspector General, Texas Health and Human Services - OIG, Texas Attorney General - Medicaid Fraud Control Unit, and Texas Department of Insurance conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Andrew Swartz and Ana Cano prosecuted the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division which is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste and abuse within federal benefit programs. Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Healthcare Fraud Components National Fraud Enforcement Division USAO - Texas, Southern

title: Former Hillsborough Township School District Worker Admits to Paying Approximately $70,000 in Kickbacks to Former School District Business Administrator as part of a Fraudulent Overtime Scheme
body: Press Release Former Hillsborough Township School District Worker Admits to Paying Approximately $70,000 in Kickbacks to Former School District Business Administrator as part of a Fraudulent Overtime Scheme Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Jersey TRENTON, N.J. – A Pennsylvania man admitted to paying approximately $70,000 in cash kickbacks to former Hillsborough Township School District (HTSD) Business Administrator Aiman Mahmoud as part of a fraudulent overtime scheme undertaken by the two men in relation to a large-scale project involving the construction and upgrade of HTSD facilities, United States Attorney Robert Frazer announced today. Kenneth Gratto, 55, of Dingman’s Ferry, Pennsylvania, pleaded guilty yesterday before U.S. District Judge Robert Kirsch to embezzling, stealing, and obtaining by fraud more than $156,000 of funds belonging to and under the care, custody and control of the HTSD, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Section 666(a)(1)(A). According to the documents filed in this case and statements made in Court: Aiman Mahmoud, who served as the Business Administrator for the HTSD from 2008 through the end of 2021, helped oversee a multi-million dollar project involving the upgrade of existing school facilities as well as the construction of a new school building that had been greenlighted by a 2019 referendum.  Mahmoud arranged for Gratto to be appointed as the site supervisor/owner’s representative to oversee aspects of the project including safety monitoring, and to assist two companies involved in implementing the goals set forth in the 2019 referendum. Gratto admitted that shortly after he was hired, he agreed to provide substantial cash kickbacks to Mahmoud in exchange for which Mahmoud approved Gratto’s time sheets which substantially exaggerated the number of overtime hours Gratto worked and for which Gratto billed at a rate of $150 per hour.  Specifically, Gratto admitted that he regularly submitted time sheets claiming that he had worked more than 12 hours of overtime work on both Saturdays and Sundays throughout the latter half of 2021 even though he had not performed any work on those weekend days.  After receiving his paychecks from the companies involved – who were in turn reimbursed by the HTSD for those amounts – Gratto would deposit the checks, withdraw cash in the amount of the intended kickback, and deliver that cash in an envelope at a location of Mahmoud’s choosing, typically, within Mahmoud’s unlocked school vehicle.  Gratto admitted to paying Mahmoud approximately $70,000 in kickbacks generated from the fraudulently billed overtime hours. In total, Gratto admitted to embezzling approximately $156,150.00 from the HTSD with Mahmoud via the overtime billing scheme.  As part of his plea agreement with the Government, Gratto agreed to forfeit this amount. The embezzlement charge is punishable by a maximum potential penalty of 10 years in prison and a maximum $250,000 fine.  Sentencing is scheduled for March 4, 2027. U.S. Attorney Frazer credited agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy in Newark; Homeland Security Investigations, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Michael McCarthy; and the Somerset County Prosecutor’s Office, under the direction of Prosecutor John P. McDonald, with the investigation. The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark J. McCarren of the Office’s Special Prosecutions Division in Newark. The charges and allegations contained in the Indictment remain pending as to defendant Mahmoud and are merely accusations, and defendant Mahmoud is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. ### Defense counsel: Timothy Donahue, AFPD, Newark  (for defendant Gratto) Stephen G. McCarthy, Esq., New York, NY (for defendant Mahmoud) mahmoudgratto.indictment.pdf Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Public Corruption Component USAO - New Jersey Press Release Number: 26-232

title: Chinese National Extradited for Alleged Role in  Multimillion-Dollar Cryptocurrency Scam Targeting U.S. Citizens
body: Press Release Chinese National Extradited for Alleged Role in  Multimillion-Dollar Cryptocurrency Scam Targeting U.S. Citizens Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Case is Part of Cyber-Enabled Scam Initiative Zheng Zhao, 44, a Chinese national, was arraigned today in the Central District of California after being extradited from the Netherlands for his alleged role in an international cryptocurrency investment conspiracy carried out from scam centers in the Kingdom of Cambodia that targeted U.S. citizens. Ultimately, the government was able to identify 174 U.S. victims. “This extradition should be a lesson to all those who seek to exploit vulnerable Americans from overseas,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “We will pursue charged defendants anywhere in the world, especially those who are alleged to have stolen money, converted it to cryptocurrency, and used foreign financial institutions in the process to try to hide and obfuscate their crimes. Wherever you are, we have the reach to find you.” “As crime has globalized, so has law enforcement’s ability to locate and catch criminals,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli for the Central District of California. “When innocent Americans are harmed by cybercriminals and their enablers, we and our partners around the globe will relentlessly ensure they face justice in a U.S. courtroom.” “Today’s arraignment demonstrates our collective commitment to pursuing transnational criminal networks that exploit the American people,” said Special Agent in Charge Todd Bratz of the U.S. Secret Service (USSS) Criminal Investigative Division. “This case should serve as a warning to scammers in every corner of the world: there is nowhere to hide. Secret Service investigators and our law enforcement partners remain unwavering in their commitment to identify those who operate scam centers, disrupt their financial infrastructure, and bring them to justice.” According to court documents, Zhao was allegedly part of an international criminal network that induced U.S. victims to transfer funds to accounts controlled by co-conspirators, who then laundered victim money through U.S. shell companies, international bank accounts, and digital asset wallets. The cycle of the scheme began when overseas co-conspirators contacted U.S. victims via unsolicited social media interactions, telephone calls, text messages, and online dating services to gain the victims’ trust. The co-conspirators promoted fraudulent digital asset investments to the victims. The co-conspirators created fake websites that resembled real cryptocurrency trading platforms and convinced victims to send funds through the fake websites for investments. The scammers would then tell the victims that their investments were appreciating in value when, in fact, the scammers had stolen the victims’ money. More than $36.9 million in victim funds were transferred from U.S. bank accounts controlled by the co-conspirators to a single account at Deltec Bank in the Bahamas. Zhao and other co-conspirators arranged for Deltec Bank to convert victim funds to the stablecoin Tether (USDT) and to transfer the converted funds to a digital asset wallet controlled in Cambodia. From there, co-conspirators in Cambodia transferred the USDT to the leaders of scam centers throughout the region. In August 2025, Zhao was charged with conspiracy to commit money laundering. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. Eight co-conspirators have pleaded guilty so far, including ShengSheng He and Jingliang Su. He and Su each pleaded guilty to conspiracy to operate an unlicensed money transmitting business and were sentenced to 51 months and 46 months in prison, respectively. USSS’s Global Investigative Operations Center is investigating the case. The Homeland Security Investigations’ El Camino Real Financial Crimes Task Force, Customs and Border Protection’s National Targeting Center, U.S. Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service, and U.S. Marshals Service provided valuable assistance. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs worked closely with Dutch authorities to secure the arrest and extradition of Zhao and provided significant assistance throughout the investigation.  The United States sincerely thank Dutch authorities for their assistance. Trial Attorney Tamara Livshiz of the Criminal Division’s White Collar and Corporate Enforcement Section, Acting Assistant Deputy Chief James S. Yoon of the Criminal Division’s Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section (CCIPS), and Assistant U.S. Attorneys Nisha Chandran and Alexander Gorin for the Central District of California are prosecuting the case. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs worked closely with Dutch authorities to secure the arrest and extradition of Zhao and provided significant assistance throughout the investigation. The United States sincerely thanks Dutch authorities for their assistance. CCIPS investigates and prosecutes cybercrime in coordination with domestic and international law enforcement agencies, often with assistance from the private sector. Since 2020, CCIPS has secured the conviction of over 180 cybercriminals and court orders for the return of over $350 million in victim funds. This case is part of efforts being undertaken by the Criminal Division’s Cyber-Enabled Scam Initiative (CSI). The CSI is a dedicated team of prosecutors built to find scammers who prey on Americans, disrupt their networks, and hold them accountable. CSI coordinates across the Criminal Division’s Sections, bringing together prosecutors and subject matter experts in complex frauds and investment schemes, cybercrimes and dismantling cyber infrastructure, online child exploitation, international evidence gathering and extradition, overseas prosecutorial development and assistance, and financial tracing and asset forfeiture. If you or someone you know is a victim of a digital asset investment fraud, report it to IC3.gov . A criminal complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. title: United States Attorneys Available To Receive Election Complaints
body: Press Release United States Attorneys Available To Receive Election Complaints Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of New York United States Attorneys Joseph Nocella and Jamie McDonald announced today that Assistant United States Attorneys (AUSAs) will lead the efforts of their Offices in connection with the Justice Department’s nationwide Election Day Program for the upcoming November 3, 2026 general election, including the early voting period that in New York lasts from October 24, 2026 through November 1, 2026.  AUSAs Erik Paulsen and Andrew Grubin have been appointed to serve as the District Election Officers (DEO) for the Eastern District of New York, and AUSA David J. Kennedy has been appointed to serve as the DEO for the Southern District of New York.  In their capacity as DEOs, these AUSAs are responsible for overseeing the Districts’ handling of Election Day complaints of voting rights concerns, threats of violence to election officials or staff, and election fraud, in consultation with Justice Department Headquarters in Washington. “When citizens of the Eastern District of New York exercise the fundamental constitutional right to vote, the process must be legally safeguarded,” stated United States Attorney Nocella.  “Anyone seeking to corrupt the process will be brought to justice.  Our Office is ready to vigorously defend this sacred right.” United States Attorney McDonald stated, “Democracy depends upon elections that are free, fair, and accessible.  The Southern District of New York is proud to continue its longstanding practice of maintaining an opportunity for voters to promptly report any issues that they may face at the polls that could diminish or impede their fundamental right to vote.” The Department of Justice plays an important role in deterring and combating discrimination and intimidation at the polls, threats of violence directed at election officials and poll workers, and election fraud.  The Department will address these violations wherever they occur.  The Department’s longstanding Election Day Program furthers these goals and also seeks to ensure public confidence in the electoral process by providing local points of contact within the Department for the public to report possible federal election law violations. Federal law protects against such crimes as threatening violence against election officials or staff, intimidating or bribing voters, buying and selling votes, impersonating voters, altering vote tallies, stuffing ballot boxes and marking ballots for voters against their wishes or without their input.  It also contains special protections for the rights of voters, and provides that they can vote free from interference, including intimidation, and other acts designed to prevent or discourage people from voting or voting for the candidate of their choice.  The Voting Rights Act and the Americans with Disabilities Act protect the right of voters to mark their own ballot or to be assisted by a person of their choice (where voters need assistance because of disability or individuals who are limited English proficient). AUSAs will be on duty in this District while the polls are open. To respond to complaints of election fraud or voting rights concerns during the voting period that ends on November 3, 2026, and to ensure that such complaints are directed to the appropriate authorities, the United States Attorneys said that their Offices will be available to receive complaints at the following numbers through Tuesday, November 3, 2026: (646) 369-4739 for Manhattan, Bronx, Dutchess, Orange, Putnam, Rockland, Sullivan, and Westchester counties and (718) 208-1182 for Brooklyn, Queens, Staten Island, Nassau, and Suffolk counties. Complaints about possible violations of the federal voting rights laws can also be made directly to the Civil Rights Division in Washington, DC by phone at 800-253-3931 or by complaint form at https://civilrights.justice.gov/. In addition, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) will have special agents available in each field office and resident agency throughout the country to receive allegations of election fraud and other election abuses on Election Day.  The FBI’s New York Field Office can be reached by the public at (212) 384-1000. In the case of a crime of violence or intimidation, please call 911 immediately and before contacting federal authorities.  State and local police have primary jurisdiction over polling places, and almost always have faster reaction capacity in an emergency. The United States Attorneys also noted that the following additional telephone numbers are available on Election Day for citizens to call for routine inquiries, such as where to vote or how late the polls are open, or to register complaints that may concern violations of New York State election laws: IN NEW YORK CITY New York City Board of Elections Main Office                            (866) 868-3692 TTY #: 212-487-5496 IN COUNTIES OUTSIDE NEW YORK CITY: County Boards of Elections Dutchess                                  (845) 486-2473 Nassau                                      (516) 571-8683 Orange                                      (845) 360-6500 Orange (Spanish language)      (855) 331-2444 Putnam                                     (845) 808-1300 Rockland                                  (845) 638-5172 Suffolk                                      (631) 852-4500 Sullivan                                    (845) 807-0400 Westchester                             (914) 995-5700 Contact U.S. ATTORNEY’S OFFICE-EDNY John Marzulli, Denise Taylor (718) 254-6323 U.S. ATTORNEY’S OFFICE-SDNY Nicholas Biase, Shelby Wratchford (212) 637-2600 Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - New York, Southern Press Release Number: 26-302

title: DEA Hosts the 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day on Saturday,  October 24th
body: Press Release DEA Hosts the 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day on Saturday, October 24th Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Tennessee Memphis, TN – The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, in collaboration with more than 4,300 law enforcement partners, will host the 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day on Saturday, October 24 th , from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. More than 4,400 collection sites will be set up across the country to dispose of unneeded, expired, and unused prescription medications. This is a simple step that prevents diversion, reduces the risk of accidental poisonings, and helps protect communities. “Since 2010, Take Back Day has helped Americans remove more than twenty million pounds of unneeded medications from their homes,” said DEA Administrator Terry Cole. “By participating in Take Back Day, you are preventing potentially addictive medications from falling into the wrong hands – a small step that can save lives. I am grateful to the thousands of law enforcement and community partners who make these events possible, and I urge everyone to take a few minutes on Saturday, October 24, to clean out your medicine cabinets.” “I’m encouraging everyone to take just a few minutes to gather any medications they no longer need,” said Special Agent in Charge Jim Scott, head of DEA’s Louisville Field Division.  “By dropping off your unneeded or expired medications at an authorized collection site, you’re making our community safer by keeping those drugs out of the hands of anyone who might otherwise abuse them.” What will be collected: Tablets, capsules, patches, and other forms of prescription medications Liquid medications securely sealed in their original containers What won’t be collected Syringes, sharps, and illicit drugs Why it matters Prescription opioids, such as oxycodone, hydrocodone, codeine, and morphine, are among the most frequently misused prescription pain medications, according to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA). Removing unneeded medications from the home reduces the risk of misuse or accidental ingestion. Visit www.DEATakeBack.com to find a registered Take Back location near you. If you are unable to participate in this fall’s National Prescription Drug Take Back Day, there are more than 15,300 pharmacies, hospitals, and businesses that offer safe medication disposal year-round. In addition, many police departments also provide permanent drop boxes to ensure Every Day is Take Back Day . ### Updated October 23, 2026 Component USAO - Tennessee, Western

title: Manchester Resident Charged with Smuggling Machine Gun Conversion Devices from China
body: Press Release Manchester Resident Charged with Smuggling Machine Gun Conversion Devices from China Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, and Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), New England, today announced that DAVID WILLIAMS, JR., also known as “Lavish David,” 23, of Manchester, has been charged by indictment with offenses related to the importation and trafficking of machine gun conversion devices. As alleged in court documents and statements made in court, on June 16, 2026, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (“CBP”) officers at Chicago O’Hare International Airport examined a package en route from China to “Lavish David” at an address in Bloomfield, Connecticut, that contained a machine gun conversion device concealed within portable camping stove components.  Commonly referred to as a “Glock switch,” a conversion device allows certain firearms to fire fully automatically.  On July 10, 2024, CBP officers at New York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport examined a package en route from China to “Lavish David” at the same Bloomfield address that contained multiple machine gun conversion device components concealed within portable camping stove components.  On July 21, 2026, HSI conducted a controlled delivery of the two packages to the Bloomfield address and confirmed that Williams had ordered the items for delivery to the residence. It is further alleged that a court-authorized search of Williams’ Apple account revealed photos, videos, and messages involving the possession of firearms and trafficking of machine gun conversion devices. Williams was arrested on a federal criminal complaint on October 2, 2026.  On October 14, 2026, a grand jury in Hartford returned an indictment charging Williams with firearms trafficking conspiracy, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of 15 years; unlawful possession of a machinegun, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of 10 years; possession of an unregistered machinegun, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of 10 years; and smuggling goods into the United States, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of 20 years. Williams appeared today in Hartford federal court and pleaded not guilty to the charges.  He is released on a $100,000 bond pending trial. U.S. Attorney Sullivan stressed that an indictment is not evidence of guilt.  Charges are only allegations, and a defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. This investigation is being conducted by Homeland Security Investigations, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection, with the assistance of the Manchester Police Department.  The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Geoffrey M. Stone. Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Connecticut

title: Nine Pennsylvania Non-Citizens Charged with Illegally Voting
body: Press Release Nine Pennsylvania Non-Citizens Charged with Illegally Voting Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Pennsylvania PHILADELPHIA/HARRISBURG – Nine non-citizens have been charged separately with illegally voting, despite knowing that they were not U.S. citizens, announced David Metcalf, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania, and Brian Miller, United States Attorney for the Middle District of Pennsylvania. Under both federal and state law, only United States citizens may vote in Pennsylvania. The cases were investigated by Homeland Security Investigations (“HSI”). “Upholding the integrity of our elections, and the right of American citizens to determine the outcome, is non-negotiable,” said U.S. Attorney Metcalf.  “Our democracy depends on it.” “These cases are important because the crime of illegal voting undermines the integrity of our elections and harms citizens by stealing the power of our votes,” said U.S. Attorney Miller. “Illegal voting is not a victimless crime but a serious affront to the principles of our democratic republic.” “Illegally casting a ballot in a federal election corrupts the electoral process and diminishes the voice of every lawful voter,” said HSI Philadelphia Special Agent in Charge Nathan Abel. “These alleged violations undermine public confidence in our democratic institutions and harm the citizens whose votes are entitled to determine our nation’s future. HSI will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to investigate election-related crimes and hold accountable those who violate federal law. In the Eastern District of Pennsylvania: Artur Kopacz , 50, of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, was charged by information with two counts of voting by an alien. The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Poland and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2022 and 2024 general elections. If convicted, Kopacz faces a maximum possible sentence of a fine, two years in prison, or both. Osmal Loy , 70, of Fountain Hill, Pa., was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Cuba and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2024 general election. Yehuda Peer , 30, of Merion Station, Pa., was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Israel and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2024 general election. Alfredo Santiesteban , 73, also of Philadelphia, was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Cuba, illegally voted in the 2024 general election. If convicted, Loy, Peer, and Santiesteban each face a maximum possible sentence of a fine, one year in prison, or both. In the Middle District of Pennsylvania: Joyce Donovan , 38, of Selinsgrove, Pa., was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Kenya and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2024 general election. Inna Henry , 52, of Harrisburg, Pa., was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien.The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Russia and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2022 and 2024 general elections. Nourten Kuruju , 64, of Luzerne, Pa., was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Greece and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2022 general election. Nina Nyawara , 21, of Selinsgrove, Pa., was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien.The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of Kenya and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2024 general election. Joyce Pitts , 80, of Effort, Pa., was charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. The information alleges that the defendant, a citizen of the Netherlands and lawful permanent U.S. resident, illegally voted in the 2024 general election. If convicted, these defendants each face a maximum possible sentence of a fine, one year in prison, or both. The charges and allegations contained in the informations are merely accusations. Every defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty in court. Contact USAPAE.PressBox@usdoj.gov 215-861-8300 Updated October 23, 2026 Topics Immigration Voting and Elections Components USAO - Pennsylvania, Eastern USAO - Pennsylvania, Middle

title: Two defendants charged in superseding indictment alleging $19 million health care fraud scheme targeting federal workers’ compensation program
body: Press Release Two defendants charged in superseding indictment alleging $19 million health care fraud scheme targeting federal workers’ compensation program Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas DALLAS — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a federal grand jury returned a superseding indictment Oct. 7 charging Dr. Javaria Jabeen and Allendor Kenyon Brown with participating in a years‑long scheme to defraud the Federal Employees’ Compensation Act program of approximately $19 million in fraudulent medical claims. In connection with the July 2025 National Health Care Fraud Takedown , prosecutors in the Northern District of Texas charged Demitrious Gilmore with conspiracy to commit health care fraud. His indictment referenced two unindicted coconspirators: a physician and a former U.S. Postal Service employee and union official. Gilmore later pleaded guilty. This superseding indictment now charges those previously unidentified individuals — physician Javaria Jabeen and postal employee Allendor Kenyon Brown — with conspiracy to commit health care fraud. “Those who exploit federal programs designed to protect injured workers undermine both the integrity of our system and the trust of the public,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “As alleged, these defendants orchestrated a years‑long scheme that siphoned millions of dollars from a program meant to help dedicated federal employees recover from on‑the‑job injuries. Anyone who attempts to enrich themselves at the expense of hard-working American taxpayers will not escape justice in the Northern District of Texas. “This indictment alleges a calculated, years-long conspiracy to conceal payments and to steal millions of dollars in taxpayer funds through fabricated medical claims for unnecessary services that were not performed. Every dollar lost to healthcare fraud threatens the system designed to protect injured federal workers,” said U.S. Department of Labor Inspector General Anthony P. D’Esposito. “The Department of Labor, Office of Inspector General will not tolerate this theft. We remain committed to working alongside our law enforcement partners and the U.S. Attorney’s Office to aggressively combat these criminal enterprises and hold accountable those who seek to enrich themselves through fraud.” “These charges are a reminder that some in the healthcare industry continue to place greed over patient care,” said US Postal Service Office of Inspector General Special Agent in Charge Jonathan Ulrich. “The investigative and legal teams tirelessly working these cases will ensure that the individuals who knowingly engage in these schemes will be held accountable for their actions.” According to the indictment, from 2017 to 2023, the defendants engaged in a scheme to submit false and fraudulent claims to the U.S. Department of Labor’s Office of Workers’ Compensation Programs (OWCP). FECA provides medical and wage benefits to federal employees injured on the job. Dr. Javaria Jabeen, a licensed Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine, owned and operated multiple clinics in Flower Mound and Grand Prairie, Texas. The indictment alleges that Dr. Jabeen, along with chiropractor Demitrious Gilmore and with assistance from Allendor Kenyon Brown, billed FECA for medical equipment and services that were ineligible for reimbursement, medically unnecessary or never provided. These included: Expensive knee braces that claimants did not need or receive Physical therapy sessions that did not occur Platelet‑rich plasma (PRP) infusions and at‑home ultrasonic devices allegedly never performed or provided Brown, a retired U.S. Postal Service employee and former union official, is accused of recruiting federal employees to the clinics and assisting in efforts to secure FECA claim approvals. The indictment alleges that Brown was compensated through an entity registered in his control to conceal the payments. In total, the conspirators submitted roughly $19 million in fraudulent claims, resulting in at least $17 million in payments from the FECA program. The indictment alleges that the defendants and their coconspirators each received a share of the proceeds. Jabeen and Brown were both arrested and had their initial appearances on Oct. 14. If convicted, the defendants each face a maximum sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment. The U.S Department of Labor Office of Inspector General and U.S. Postal Service Office of Inspector General conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Douglas Brasher from the Fraud Section is prosecuting the case. An indictment is merely an allegation of criminal conduct and defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law. ### Documents superseding_indictment_-_jabeen_brown.pdf Contact Public Affairs Division U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of Texas USATXN.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Healthcare Fraud Component USAO - Texas, Northern

title: Firearms dealer sentenced to prison for having unregistered firearms
body: Press Release Firearms dealer sentenced to prison for having unregistered firearms Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Kansas TOPEKA, KAN. – A Kansas firearms dealer was sentenced to 18 months in prison for having dozens of unregistered firearms devices. According to court documents, Travis Lee Ray, 37, of Smith Center pleaded guilty to one count of illegal possession of a machine gun. In October 2024, the Smith County Sheriff’s Office responded to a domestic dispute call from a property that served both as Ray’s home and his business “Ray’s Armageddon Arsenal.”  A witness told deputies that in the basement Ray had cocaine, parts to convert semi-automatic firearms into fully automatic firearms, and silencers. Deputies contacted the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF). ATF agents obtained and executed a search warrant where they found 38 Glock conversion devices and seven silencers, none of which were registered. “The Second Amendment protects lawful gun ownership, but those rights come with responsibilities. Firearms are powerful tools that must be used responsibly and in accordance with the law,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “As a firearms dealer, the defendant was well acquainted with federal gun laws. Now, along with going to prison, he has to relinquish his Federal Firearms License.” The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF) and Smith County Sheriff’s Office investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Greg Hough prosecuted the case. ### Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Kansas

title: North Carolina man pleads guilty for his role in gun trafficking conspiracy
body: Press Release North Carolina man pleads guilty for his role in gun trafficking conspiracy Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of New York BUFFALO, N.Y.-U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Jerry Antonio Baine a/k/a Bank 3x, 23, of Durham, NC, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to engage in the firearms business without a license, which carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison. Between March 2023, and June 23, 2025, Baine conspired with Hassain Humphrey, Keishawn Turner, Jylin Woods, and Benjamin Martin, to illegally sell firearms. During this time, Baine sent Humphrey photographs of approximately 19 firearms, several were privately manufactured firearms, bearing no serial number. On multiple occasions, he indicated that the firearms were for sale, and he and Humphrey would often discuss a potential sale price. On one occasion, Baine indicated that a sale price proposed by Humphrey would not leave him with enough “profit.” When discussing certain firearms via text message, Baine and/or Humphrey used the terms “ghost” and “p80,” terms commonly used to refer to privately manufactured firearms bearing no serial number. During the conspiracy, Baine purchased multiple firearms from retail establishments in North Carolina, one of which was recovered in a separate criminal investigation in Buffalo, on July 4, 2024. Another firearm was recovered in a separate criminal investigation in Buffalo on June 19, 2026. In October 2024, Baine was interviewed by members of the ATF, during which he stated that he purchased multiple firearms for Humphrey in North Carolina. He also confirmed that he had knowledge that Humphrey and another individual were reselling the firearms in New York. Baine that he sold the firearms to Humphrey because he was unemployed and needed the money. Baine admits that neither he or Humphrey were licensed importers, manufacturers, dealers, and collectors of firearms. Humphrey and Turner were previously convicted and are awaiting sentencing. Charges remain pending against Jylin Woods and Benjamin Martin. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Louis A. Testani and Monica Benjovsky. The plea is the result of an investigation by the Buffalo Police Department, under the direction of Police Commissioner Erika Shields and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Bryan DiGirolamo. Sentencing is scheduled for March 5, 2027, before U.S. District Judge Lawrence J. Vilardo. # # # # Contact Barbara Burns 716-843-5817 Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Component USAO - New York, Western

title: Kansas man receives prison sentence for distributing child pornography
body: Press Release Kansas man receives prison sentence for distributing child pornography Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Kansas WICHITA, KAN. – A Kansas man was sentenced to 210 months in prison for distributing child sexual abuse material (CSAM). According to court documents, Jordan Mark Morrison, 21, of Wichita pleaded guilty to one count of distribution of child pornography. In 2025, the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) received a cybertip about an email account that was being used to distribute CSAM.  Law enforcement obtained a search warrant for the account and discovered it belonged to Morrison and included personal information like his date of birth and phone number.  The defendant later admitted to using that email account to send CSAM which included a video of an adult sexually assaulting a screaming toddler. “No punishment can fully repair the profound harm caused to victims. However, this sentence underscores the Department of Justice’s enduring commitment to aggressively investigating and prosecuting those who prey on children,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “We remain dedicated to delivering justice for victims and preventing further exploitation.” The Kansas Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) investigated the case. Project Safe Childhood This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . ### Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Kansas

title: Four Individuals Plead Guilty to Conspiracy to Make and Distribute Animal Crush Videos Involving Monkeys
body: Press Release Four Individuals Plead Guilty to Conspiracy to Make and Distribute Animal Crush Videos Involving Monkeys Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs The Justice Department today announced that four additional individuals have pleaded guilty in connection with a conspiracy to create and distribute videos depicting extreme violence and sexual abuse against monkeys. According to court documents, Ernest Chavez, of Arizona, pleaded guilty today to conspiring to create and distribute so-called “animal crush” videos. In addition, the following individuals pleaded guilty for their role in the conspiracy: Mary Longoria, of North Carolina, pleaded guilty on July 16 and is scheduled to be sentenced on Dec. 2. Kimberly Anglin, of Connecticut, pleaded guilty on Aug. 12 and is scheduled to be sentenced on Dec. 2. Patrick Naylor, of North Carolina, pleaded guilty on Aug. 14 and is scheduled to be sentenced on Dec. 17. Chavez, Longoria, Anglin, and Naylor were among 11 individuals indicted in 2025 based on their involvement with various online groups dedicated to the creation and proliferation of monkey torture videos. According to court documents, the defendants and their co-conspirators used Telegram, an online messaging application to gather online and discuss topics for upcoming torture videos. The conspirators would then funnel money to individuals in Indonesia willing to carry out requested acts of torture on camera using various online payment applications. Nicholas Dryden, of Cincinnati, Ohio, was one of the sources of videos at the time and was previously sentenced to 108 months in prison for his role in the conspiracy. Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General Adam Gustafson of the Justice Department’s  Energy and Natural Resources Division (ENRD), U.S. Attorney Dominick S. Gerace II for the Southern District of Ohio, Special Agent in Charge Jason Cromartie of the FBI’s Cincinnati Field Office, and Assistant Director Doug Ault of the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS)’s Office of Law Enforcement made the announcement. The USFWS’ Office of Law Enforcement and the FBI investigated the cases. Senior Trial Attorney Adam Cullman of ENRD is prosecuting the cases. title: Rochester man going to prison for conspiring to defraud victims, including taxpayers, of more than $2,000,000 and money laundering
body: Press Release Rochester man going to prison for conspiring to defraud victims, including taxpayers, of more than $2,000,000 and money laundering Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of New York ROCHESTER, N.Y.-U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Timothy Wadsworth, 35, of Rochester, NY, who was convicted of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and money laundering, was sentenced to serve 51 months in prison and pay $810,965.19 in restitution by U.S. District Judge Frank P. Geraci, Jr. In addition, Wadsworth was ordered to forfeit $810,956.19, which represents the wire fraud proceeds he received. This case is part of the Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud. Between March 2020, and September 2021, Wadsworth conspired with others to fraudulently obtain money. To execute the scheme, he obtained credit card account numbers from coconspirators and processed unauthorized credit card transactions from those accounts, transferring the money to his bank accounts, transferring a portion of the money to his Coinbase account to purchase Bitcoin, and transferring Bitcoin to his coconspirators. Between March 10, 2020, and May 15, 2020, Wadsworth, using a Stripe, Inc. account, which allows merchants to receive funds from consumers as payments for goods and services, attempted to process 310 payments totaling $1,673,578. Of the 310 attempted transactions, 116 were initially successful totaling $730,728.22. These transactions were fraudulent. The account holders did not authorize the transactions, and their account information was used to make the payments without authorization. Once credit card payments were successfully processed, Wadsworth transferred the funds from his Stripe account to bank accounts he owned with HSBC and Evolve Federal Credit Union. He then transferred funds from those bank accounts to his Coinbase account, purchased Bitcoin with the money, and transferred the Bitcoin to various external addresses. These transactions were often in excess of $10,000 each. For example, between April 22 and April 28, 2020, Wadsworth transferred fraudulently obtained proceeds from his Stripe account to his HSBC account on three separate occasions, in the amounts of $49,419.99, $45,501.85, and $53,496.75. In addition, between May 13, 2020, through May 5, 2021, Wadsworth and others submitted nine false Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) applications in an attempt to obtain money they were not entitled to. The applications contained misrepresentations about the businesses’ revenue and operation, which was material in assessing the businesses’ eligibility for the EIDL funds. Three of the EIDL applications were approved, and a total of $161,200 was paid to Wadsworth’s bank accounts as a result of the fraud. Between March 7 and April 26, 2021, Wadsworth applied for six Payroll Protection Program (PPP) loans totaling $91,219. Two of the loans were funded for $20,833 and $20,416, respectively, which was paid to Wadsworth’s bank account. Once again, the applications contained misrepresentations about the businesses they were submitted for. From May 2020 through September 2021, Wadsworth fraudulently received approximately $65,896 in unemployment benefits from New York State, the State of Washington, and the Department of Labor. He was not eligible to receive any unemployment funds from any source during that time. Wadsworth also participated in a romance fraud scheme in 2020. The victim, recently widowed, met an individual on Facebook that represented himself as an oil rig worker, and requested $42,000 from her to pay for travel expenses to return to the United States. The victim was directed to wire the money to Wadsworth’s bank account, which she did on March 20, 2020. Wadsworth also defrauded six other victims out of $26,000 as a result of his schemes. Wadsworth’s actions, including the credit card fraud, the PPP and EIDL fraud, the unemployment fraud, and the other frauds, resulted in actual and intended losses of approximately $2,059,893.00. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Katelyn M. Hartford. The sentencing is the result of an investigation by Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Allen D. Davis, II, the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Harry T. Chavis, Jr., New York Field Office, the New York State Department of Financial Services, under the direction of Acting Superintendent Kaitlin Asrow, and the New York State Department of Labor, under the direction of Commissioner Roberta Reardon. # # # # Contact Barbara Burns 716-843-5817 Updated October 23, 2026 Topics Benefit Fraud COVID-Related Fraud Financial Fraud Component USAO - New York, Western

Geraci, Jr. In addition, Wadsworth was ordered to forfeit $810,956.19, which represents the wire fraud proceeds he received. title: Telemedicine Company Owner Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison for $46M Medicare Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Telemedicine Company Owner Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison for $46M Medicare Fraud Scheme Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs The owner of a telemedicine company was sentenced today to 20 years in prison for organizing and leading a $46.2 million Medicare fraud conspiracy that spanned more than six years. In addition to the prison term, the defendant was ordered to pay $17,942,402 in restitution to Medicare and $10,431,463 in forfeiture. According to court documents, Christopher Harwood, 44, of Fort Lauderdale, Florida, owned and operated a telemedicine company called TelevisitMD. Harwood and his co-conspirators targeted Medicare patients through aggressive telemarketing campaigns, inducing them to accept orthotic braces and genetic tests that they did not need. Harwood paid doctors to approve orders for orthotic braces and genetic tests. These doctors did not follow Medicare’s rules for telemedicine visits, did not have real medical relationships with the Medicare patients, and often signed orders for orthotic braces and genetic tests without any meaningful interaction with the Medicare patients. Harwood then sold the signed doctors’ orders to durable medical equipment (DME) supply companies, laboratories, and marketers who were part of the scheme. Harwood also owned and operated multiple DME supply companies based in Florida that he used to bill Medicare millions of dollars for orthotic braces that Medicare patients did not want or need. In total, Harwood caused $46.2 million in false and fraudulent claims to Medicare, and Medicare paid $17.9 million based on those claims. Harwood personally profited more than $10.4 million from the fraud scheme. In March 2026, Harwood pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit health care fraud and wire fraud. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division; U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida; Special Agent in Charge Brett Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office; and Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG) made the announcement. FBI and HHS-OIG investigated the case. Trial Attorney Owen Dunn of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section is prosecuting the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit . Updated October 23, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1253

title: Sanostee Man Charged Federally for Violent Attack
body: Press Release Sanostee Man Charged Federally for Violent Attack Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – A Sanostee man is facing federal charges after an alleged assault left a man with a fractured facial bone and other injuries. According to court documents, on October 18, 2026, Cordell Washburn , 37, an enrolled member of the Navajo Nation, repeatedly struck the victim with an axe handle and kicked him while he was on the ground outside a residence in Sanostee, New Mexico. When a witness intervened, Washburn allegedly raised the axe handle toward her, causing her to retreat. Other witnesses reported hearing Washburn threaten to kill the victim. They also reported seeing him throw large rocks at a woman and break a truck window with a rock. Navajo Nation Police officers responding to the scene found the victim bleeding from his head and face and appearing disoriented. Officers located Washburn approximately half a mile from the residence and took him into custody. Investigators recovered an axe handle from the scene. The victim later told investigators that the assault began when he approached Washburn to retrieve his truck keys. He reported being knocked to the ground, beaten and kicked. Medical records confirmed that the victim suffered a facial fracture and abrasions to both knees. Washburn is charged with assault with a dangerous weapon and assault resulting in serious bodily injury. He will remain in third party custody pending trial, which has not been scheduled. If convicted of the current charge, Washburn faces up to 10 years in prison. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and Special Agent in Charge Justin A. Garris of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office made the announcement today. The Farmington Resident Agency of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office investigated this case with assistance from the Navajo Nation Police Department and Navajo Nation Department of Criminal Investigations. Assistant U.S. Attorney Aaron O. Jordan is prosecuting the case. A criminal complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. title: Tallahassee Felon Sentenced to Federal Prison for Firearm Possession While Shoplifting
body: Press Release Tallahassee Felon Sentenced to Federal Prison for Firearm Possession While Shoplifting Friday, October 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Tallahassee, Florida – Lamar Bunch, 35, of Tallahassee, Florida, was sentenced by U.S. District Judge Mark E. Walker to two years and four months in federal prison for possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. The sentence was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “Our brave law enforcement partners confront dangerous, armed criminals like this defendant every day in their fight to keep our communities safe, and I am proud to deliver this successful prosecution and prison sentence to make clear that we will not tolerate criminality in my district. Armed serial offenders like this defendant belong behind bars, and my office will continue to aggressively prosecute these cases to deliver the safe, crime-free streets our citizens deserve.” Court documents reflect that on February 18, 2026, an off-duty Leon County Sheriff’s Office deputy was working a security detail at Dillards when he observed the defendant shoplifting. The deputy made contact with the defendant outside of the store, and, while talking with him, the defendant opened his backpack where the deputy could see a pair of jeans inside the bag with the tags still on them. When the deputy attempted to detain the defendant, he fled on foot. The defendant was caught, arrested and a search of the defendant’s backpack yielded the stolen pair of pants with the size and price tags still attached and a 9-millimeter pistol. The defendant was prohibited from possessing firearms due to prior felony convictions for burglary, robbery, and attempted burglary. Evidence at sentencing showed that the day prior, specifically after midnight on February 17, 2026, the defendant threatened his ex-girlfriend with a silver and black pistol. The ex-girlfriend had a gas station store clerk call 911 and then locked herself inside the store’s bathroom until law enforcement arrived. The defendant left the store before law enforcement was able to talk to the ex-girlfriend and was not found that night. The case involved an investigation by the Leon County Sheriff’s Office, the Tallahassee Police Department, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney James A. McCain. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities . The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General.  To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl . title: ECB Consumer Expectations Survey results – September 2026
body:
ECB Consumer Expectations Survey results – September 2026 Skip to: Skip to navigation Skip to content Skip to footer EN Български Čeština Dansk Deutsch Eλληνικά English Español Eesti keel Suomi Français Gaeilge Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Lietuvių Latviešu Malti Nederlands Polski Português Română Slovenčina Slovenščina Svenska Menu Search Menu ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Search Options Image Preview Sort by ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Suggestions Home Media Explainers Research & Publications Statistics Monetary Policy The €uro Payments & Markets Careers Suggestions Sort by Relevance Date PRESS RELEASE ECB Consumer Expectations Survey results – September 2026 23 October 2026 Compared with August 2026: median consumer perceptions of inflation over the past 12 months and expectations for inflation over the next 12 months increased slightly, while median expectations for inflation three years and five years ahead were unchanged; expectations for nominal income growth over the next 12 months increased, as did expectations for spending growth over the next 12 months; expectations for economic growth over the next 12 months decreased, while the expected unemployment rate in 12 months’ time increased; expectations for growth in the price of homes over the next 12 months increased, while expectations for mortgage interest rates in 12 months’ time remained unchanged Inflation In September the median rate of perceived inflation over the previous 12 months increased to 3.6% from 3.5% in August. Median expectations for inflation over the next 12 months also increased, to 3.1% from 3.0%. Median expectations for inflation three years ahead and median expectations for inflation five years ahead were unchanged at 2.9% and 2.5% respectively. Uncertainty about expectations for inflation over the next 12 months increased slightly, remaining higher than the level prior to the start of the conflict in the Middle East. Respondents in the bottom income quintile continued to report higher inflation perceptions and expectations, on average, than those in the top quintile. Younger respondents (aged 18-34) continued to report lower inflation perceptions and expectations than older respondents (aged 35-54 and 55-70). Inflation results Income and consumption Consumers’ expectations for nominal income growth over the next 12 months increased to 1.1% in September from 1.0% in August. As in previous months expectations were, on average, higher in the bottom income quintile (1.5%) than in the top quintile (1.2%). Perceived nominal spending growth over the previous 12 months increased to 5.3% from 5.2%, while expected nominal spending growth over the next 12 months increased to 3.7% from 3.6%. Income and consumption results Economic growth and labour market Expectations for economic growth over the next 12 months decreased in September to -1.5%, from -1.2% in August. Expectations for the unemployment rate 12 months ahead increased to 11.3%, from 11.0%. As observed in previous months, households in the bottom income quintile expected the highest unemployment rate 12 months ahead (13.6%), while households in the top income quintile expected the lowest rate (9.7%). Consumers continued to expect the future unemployment rate to be only slightly higher than the perceived current unemployment rate (10.6%), suggesting a broadly stable labour market outlook. Economic growth and labour market results Housing and credit access Consumers expected the price of their home to increase by 3.5% over the next 12 months, higher than in August (3.4%). As in previous months expectations for home price growth over the next 12 months remained, on average, higher in the lowest income quintile (4.0%) than in the highest income quintile (3.2%). Expectations for mortgage interest rates in 12 months’ time remained unchanged from July, at 4.9%. As in previous months, households in the top income quintile expected the lowest mortgage interest rates 12 months ahead (4.4%), while those in the bottom quintile expected the highest rates (5.7%). The net percentage of households reporting a tightening (relative to those reporting an easing) of access to credit over the previous 12 months increased compared with August, as did the net percentage of households expecting tighter credit conditions over the next 12 months (relative to those expecting an easing). Housing and credit access results The microdata underlying the aggregate results are available in the Data and methodological information section of the ECB Consumer Expectations Survey (CES) web page. The release of the CES results for October is scheduled for 27 November 2026. For media queries, please contact: Benoit Deeg , tel.: +49 172 1683704. Notes The fieldwork for the latest CES wave was carried out between 27 August and 28 September 2026. The main aggregate results for individual countries and the euro area are published on the ECB Data Portal and on the ECB’s website every month. Unless otherwise indicated, the statistics presented in this press release refer to the 2% winsorised mean. For further details, see ECB Consumer Expectations Survey – Guide to the computation of aggregate statistics . The CES is a monthly online survey of, currently, around 19,000 adult consumers (i.e. aged 18 or over) from 11 euro area countries: Belgium, Germany, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Austria, Portugal and Finland. The results are used for policy analysis and complement other data sources used by the ECB. Further information about the survey and the data collected is available on the CES web page . Detailed information can also be found in the following two publications: Bańkowska, K. et al., “ ECB Consumer Expectations Survey: an overview and first evaluation ”, Occasional Paper Series , No 287, ECB, Frankfurt am Main, December 2021; and Georgarakos, D. and Kenny, G., “ Household spending and fiscal support during the COVID-19 pandemic: Insights from a new consumer survey ”, Journal of Monetary Economics , Vol. 129, Supplement, July 2022, pp. S1-S14. The survey results do not represent the views of the ECB’s decision-making bodies or staff.
