title: Kazakhstan Expands Compute for Its AI Future
body: Kazakhstan Expands Compute for Its AI Future Jensen Huang’s visit to the nation’s capital, Astana — including a presidential meeting and public fireside chat — coincided with  new AI infrastructure commitments anchored by NVIDIA compute. October 22, 2026 by Rev Lebaredian 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Kazakhstan’s AI ecosystem is moving from infrastructure plans to deployment. The shift is visible across the full AI stack — from infrastructure to models to applications. The announcements below — coinciding with a visit to Astana by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang — point to the nation’s increasing supply of accelerated computing, along with its growing demand for what comes next. On Friday, Oct. 23, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang visited Astana, meeting with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev at the Akorda Presidential Palace and joining Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev — Kazakhstan’s minister of AI and digital development — for a public fireside chat at the Alem.AI program. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Jensen Huang and Kazakhstan’s AI Minister Speak at Alem.AI In their fireside chat at Alem.AI, Kazakhstan’s international center for artificial intelligence, Madiyev and Huang discussed the country’s push to become an AI nation — building the energy and computing infrastructure to support homegrown AI and applying it across the economy. Madiyev said Kazakhstan wants AI that reflects its language and culture. “We want AI that understands and speaks Kazakh and captures cultural contexts and cultural specifics,” he said, describing the country’s work on Kazakh-language models. Huang said Kazakhstan could turn its energy resources into a foundation for AI production — and a new kind of export. “Instead of just exporting energy, in the future, you could transform energy into intelligence and export intelligence,” he said. He also argued that local data is central to that ambition: it embodies a country’s culture, history and values. “Your country’s data is your natural resource. It belongs to you.” The conversation also turned to physical AI. Madiyev pointed to Kazakhstan’s factories, mines, agriculture, transport and logistics as potential areas for development, asking how the country could become a hub for training models for robots and other physical systems. Huang called the idea “fantastic,” saying physical AI could transform industries from mining and mineral processing to agriculture. Huang said AI and robotics can help people do more, but ambition will shape how fully they seize that opportunity. He applied the idea to Kazakhstan, saying AI could help lift the country and its people. “If you have ambition, and I believe you do, AI will lift your nation,” Huang said. “AI will lift your people.” Huang also praised the founders of Higgsfield AI, the Kazakhstan-founded startup, and it was announced NVIDIA is making an investment into the startup during the event. “The first thing and the last thing is you invest in people, not companies,” he said, describing the founders as visionary and pointing to their effort to compete globally. Asked about AI security, Huang said the technology must be developed and deployed responsibly. He described NVIDIA’s OpenShell as a way to contain AI agents by limiting their access to files and tools and monitoring their activity. For young people entering a fast-changing field, Huang recommended learning how AI works — not just how to use it. He said aspiring AI programmers should understand the technology’s principles, strengths and weaknesses, combining technical knowledge with the ability to work effectively with AI. “I envy being 18 years old today… because the world is changing so rapidly, and there’s a complete reset because of technology.” The Infrastructure Layer Is Scaling The visits coincided with a signing ceremony marking Firebird’s investment agreement with the government of Kazakhstan, held at the presidential palace. Building on its first AI factory in Armenia, Firebird is expanding into Kazakhstan, where it has secured a U.S. export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs. The first phase is under construction with Kazakhtelecom at Data Center Valley, targeting commercial launch in the third quarter of 2027. A planned second phase would bring Firebird’s total potential AI infrastructure capacity in Kazakhstan to approximately 500 megawatts. Firebird also plans to establish Firebird Labs Kazakhstan to support local AI startups, research and talent development through funding, access to compute and research partnerships. Firebird cofounder and CEO Razmig Hovaghimian attended the signing ceremony at the Akorda Presidential Palace alongside government officials. “What began as a seed of an idea 180 days ago has grown into a major investment in Kazakhstan’s AI future,” said Razmig Hovaghimian, co-Founder and CEO of Firebird. “President Tokayev’s vision gave us the confidence to think bigger about what we can build together. With Jensen Huang here today, that ambition feels more tangible than ever. We’re building the infrastructure for Kazakhstan’s talent and ideas to reach the world.” Kazakhtelecom , the nation’s largest telecommunications company, has already deployed 400 NVIDIA H200 and 480 NVIDIA B300 GPUs in Astana and Almaty. Next year, the company plans to deploy more than 1,000 GPUs in the Data Center Valley , along with more than 1,000 NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs in the Ekibastuz region, serving diverse workloads with infrastructure that enterprises, developers and institutions can use at scale. An Honorary Black Belt for Huang Later that day, also at the Akorda Presidential Palace, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev presented Huang with an honorary black belt in Judo. The belt, embroidered in gold stitching, was a special thanks from President Tokayev for Huang’s support of Kazakhstan’s AI ambition and for leadership aligned with the spirit and rigor of the martial art. At the end of their meeting President Tokayev had another honor for Huang, presenting him with the Order of Dostyk, First Class, for Huang’s contribution to the development of artificial intelligence in Kazakhstan. Dostyk means friendship and the Order honors peace, friendship and cooperation. AI-Native Companies Scale With Compute And that development is accelerating. The nation’s AI-native companies are also building out their compute capacity — and the applications that run atop them. Higgsfield is expanding its AI infrastructure with NVIDIA Vera Rubin running on cloud service providers, giving the company additional capacity as models, products and customer demand for its generative media applications grow. More local capacity gives developers and companies room to train, fine-tune and serve increasingly capable models. Successful applications, in turn, create demand for more compute. Kazakhstan’s AI opportunity isn’t defined by GPU counts alone. Connecting that infrastructure with developers, universities, startups and industries can turn accelerated computing into useful applications. That was at the core of the discussion the NVIDIA team had with hundreds of developers from across Kazakhstan during a reception later in the evening. The gathering in this self-proclaimed AI nation was inspiring because of the ideas shared, the clear drive to build and a collective ambition to share it with the world. Today’s announcements represent different layers of the AI stack in Kazakhstan— infrastructure deployment, access to compute and AI-native product development — where the AI foundation is reaching new scale. Watch the fireside chat between Jensen Huang and Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev, streamed live from Alem.AI in Astana . title: Treasury Issues Proposed Rule to Implement Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act
body: October 22, 2026 WASHINGTON– The U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) today issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) to propose updates to the Outbound Investment Security Program (OISP) based on direction from Congress in the Comprehensive Outbound Investment Security (COINS) Act, passed as part of the Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act.  The COINS Act codifies the U.S. Government’s approach to regulating certain outbound investments by U.S. persons and builds upon Treasury’s existing OISP. In passing the COINS Act, Congress made clear that restricting certain U.S. outbound investments into dual-use strategic technologies that benefit a foreign adversary’s military modernization efforts, surveillance states, and human rights abuses is necessary to prevent harm to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. President Trump is committed to protecting our national security and the implementation of the COINS Act is consistent with maintaining a strong, open investment environment that benefits our economy and supports our national security interests. The COINS Act directs the Secretary of the Treasury (the Secretary) to issue regulations that (1) require United States persons to provide notification to Treasury regarding certain transactions involving covered foreign persons that are engaged in notifiable technologies, and (2) prohibit United States persons from engaging in certain other transactions involving covered foreign persons that are engaged in prohibited technologies.  The COINS Act authorizes the Secretary to prescribe regulations with technical parameters for “prohibited technology” and “notifiable technology” in five technology sectors: semiconductor technologies and microelectronics; artificial intelligence systems; quantum information technologies; high-performance computing and supercomputing; and hypersonic systems.  The COINS Act also authorizes the Secretary—in consultation with the appropriate congressional committees and subject to notice and comment rulemaking—to add and define technologies beyond those specifically listed in the law that enable the military, intelligence, surveillance, or cyber-enabled capabilities of a country of concern.  Accordingly, the Secretary has added biotechnology to the proposed regulations. “Under President Trump’s leadership, we are committed to putting America’s national security first,” said Secretary Scott Bessent .  “The proposed regulations would strengthen the existing Outbound Investment Security Program to prevent our adversaries from using U.S. investment to develop critical technologies that threaten U.S. national security.  This important step also helps promote our commitment to an open investment environment by providing clarity to U.S. and foreign investors as well as an opportunity for them to provide feedback on the proposed regulations.” “The proposed regulations are designed to address risks that can arise when foreign adversaries try to benefit from U.S. investment in key technology sectors,” said Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for Investment Security Christopher Pilkerton.  Pilkerton added, “It will enhance the Outbound Investment Security Program and our efforts to protect U.S. national security.” The NPRM issued today provides details on key concepts and aspects of the program’s proposed implementation, including: Requirements applicable to a U.S. person (including any controlled foreign entities); Categories of covered national security transactions; Definitions; The scope of covered foreign persons; Excepted transactions; Technical specifications to inform the scope of covered national security transactions based on certain technologies and products in the areas of semiconductor technology and microelectronics, quantum information technologies, super intelligence systems, hypersonic systems, high-performance computing and supercomputing, and biotechnology; Information that a U.S. person is required to provide to Treasury as part of a notification; The process of requesting non-binding feedback and submitting confidential information; The knowledge standard and expectations for a U.S. person to conduct a reasonable and diligent inquiry prior to undertaking a transaction; and Conduct that would be treated as a violation of the proposed rule and applicable penalties for such conduct. Treasury invites comments from a wide range of stakeholders on all aspects of the NPRM including feedback on the scope of a covered national security transaction, definitions of key terms, the notification requirements, and the penalty and enforcement processes for violations, among other aspects.  Treasury will carefully consider this input before issuing the final implementing regulations. Written comments may be submitted by the deadline in the official NPRM, available at https://www.regulations.gov .  The NPRM will be followed at a later date by final implementing regulations, which will set an effective date for the program. The NPRM, fact sheet, and additional information are available at: https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/international/outbound-investment-program .

title: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available
body: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available Today, we’re announcing the general availability of AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities . AWS Continuum is a security service that finds and validates code vulnerabilities, then delivers fixes as patches you can automate or as pull requests in your repositories. AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities confirms which findings are exploitable in your environment, ranks the resulting issues by business impact, and proposes a fix for each one. Every remediation starts in a mode where Continuum proposes the fix and a person approves it before it ships. In the future, you will be able to decide which actions Continuum can take on its own, within the guardrails you define. Using frontier artificial intelligence (AI) models, threat actors can turn a vulnerability disclosure into working exploit code in minutes, and the same tools that speed up development also increase the volume of findings your teams must process. If your organization runs a large application estate, your scanners likely produce thousands of findings a day, and many of them need no action. A finding can be unreachable, unexploitable, or already mitigated by a runtime control. Generic severity scores don’t tell you which resources a threat actor can actually reach, so a critical score on a dev-only utility looks the same as a medium score on a service one step away from a payments database. Previously, confirming whether a finding was exploitable took hours of manual investigation, and shipping a fix with confidence took days of coordination across security, infrastructure, and application teams, because the blast radius of a change is hard to assess without business context. To close that gap, Continuum proves which findings are exploitable and bounds the risk of each fix it proposes. Continuum builds a context graph from two primary sources: your code repositories and your AWS environment. For AWS, you set up a collector in the account and Region where your code runs. The collector gathers resource details such as AWS Config resources and network configuration so Continuum can judge whether a vulnerability is reachable over the network and what a threat actor could reach from it. From this graph, Continuum learns which systems are business-critical, who owns them, how services depend on one another, and which data each one touches. It uses that picture to identify your highest-value systems, such as customer data stores, payment pipelines, and authentication services, and then ranks each resulting issue by how close its attack path runs to those systems. Continuum analyzes each finding against your code and its environment context and assigns an evidence level, such as a verdict proven by static analysis of the vulnerable code path. For findings it can reproduce, Continuum runs the exploit in an isolated sandbox and attaches proof-of-concept code with the reproduction steps. It produces the attack path, the supporting source analysis, and a blast radius assessment instead of a risk score alone. It also evaluates whether your existing defenses would detect and stop the validated path. For each confirmed issue, Continuum generates a fix (a code patch, a dependency upgrade, or a configuration change) and opens it as a pull request in your connected repository, ready to review. Every fix requires human approval: you review and merge the pull request, so the final decision stays with your team. In the future, you will be able to build confidence in specific remediation classes and let Continuum apply those fixes automatically once its confidence gates pass, such as test coverage, scope bounds, and historical success rate. AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities in action To show how this works, I open AWS Continuum in the console and go to Code vulnerabilities . Before I can review issues, I set up an environment. I connect a code source, either a GitHub integration or an Amazon S3 bucket, and then create an environment that scans it on a schedule I choose. An Amazon S3 source has a couple of prerequisites: the bucket sits in the same account and AWS Region where I turn on AWS Continuum, and I grant access through an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role that AWS Continuum assumes. I can optionally add AWS infrastructure context by setting up an AWS Continuum collector in the account and Region where my code runs and authorizing my environment to use it. For the full requirements and steps, see the AWS Continuum User Guide . The Overview page brings these pieces together in one place, showing my Code integrations , the Environments built on them, and the status of any AWS collector that supplies AWS resource context. I open one of my environments. The Issues tab lists validated, prioritized issues rather than raw scanner output, each with a severity, a status, and the time it was created. I choose one of the issues. The Overview rates it High severity, with the status Completed and the remediation already Delivered to GitHub. The Risk assessment explains why. Continuum rates its Exploitability as Exploitable , with an evidence level of Static proven and a validation run status of Completed . Likelihood is High , since the service is reachable from an attacker, requires no authentication, and needs no user interaction. Impact is Moderate , which means an attacker gains the ability to modify business data, with a blast radius reaching other users in the same tenant. A Proof section includes the source analysis behind the verdict. The Remediation section shows a fix already delivered as a pull request in GitHub, changing four files, with 50 lines added and 24 removed across the cart service. Continuum opens the fix as a pull request titled Continuum fix , and I choose View pull request to open it in GitHub. The console is explicit that a generated patch does not mean the issue is fixed. I still review and merge it, which keeps the final decision with my team. A Contributing findings section lists the specific scanner finding this issue was built from. The pull request description carries the same risk assessment, remediation summary, and proof from the console, so whoever reviews it in GitHub sees the evidence without leaving their workflow. The Findings tab lists the raw scanner findings across the environment, the evidence that issues are built from. The Scans tab shows the history of each scan with its status, origin, and request and completion times, and I use Configure scan frequency to change the cadence or Queue scan to run one on demand. The Configuration tab is where I manage the environment: the code and context sources it reads from, its code integrations, environment settings such as whether Continuum creates remediation patches, and the AWS collectors it uses for AWS context. In a single workflow, I work through the validated issues in priority order with each scan, reviewing the evidence and scope behind each one before I approve and merge the fixes I trust. Every fix waits for my approval, so the backlog keeps shrinking while my team keeps control of what ships. Now available AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is available today in US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon) Regions. For pricing, visit the pricing page . To learn more, visit the AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities product page and the User Guide . Give it a try in the AWS Continuum console today, and send us feedback through your usual AWS Support contacts. — Esra

title: Regulators unveil plans to simplify Senior Manager and Certification Regime
body:
Regulators unveil plans to simplify Senior Manager and Certification Regime | Bank of England – the UK's central bank Our use of cookies We use necessary cookies to make our site work. We’d also like to use some non-essential cookies (including third-party cookies) to help us improve the site. Accept recommended cookies Proceed with necessary cookies only Skip to main content Regulators unveil plans to simplify Senior Manager and Certification Regime The number of financial services roles required to face enhanced checks from regulators will fall significantly under proposals that will support growth. Published on  
        22 October 2026 News release The number of financial services roles required to face enhanced checks from regulators will fall significantly under proposals that will support growth. The changes are expected to save firms around £2 billion over a 10-year period. The Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) and Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) have today announced parallel consultations on proposals to significantly streamline the Senior Managers and Certification regime (SM&CR). The SM&CR was introduced 10 years ago to instil a culture of accountability among senior decision-makers in regulated firms. Under the proposals, unnecessary burdens will be removed while high standards of individual accountability and conduct will remain unchanged, including the regulators’ commitment to ensuring that individuals are accountable for misconduct that affects society as well as their employers. The changes will allow firms to focus more resources to ensure good customer and market outcomes, recruit and appoint talent, and prioritise innovation and investment, all supporting UK growth and competitiveness. The key changes to the regime include: Regulator pre-approval will be removed for a range of regulatory functions, including Chief Actuaries and Chairs of Risk and Audit Committees. Firms will instead notify regulators of these appointments directly, gaining speed and flexibility while remaining responsible for ensuring candidates are fit and proper. Removing the Certification Regime and associated administrative requirements for around 139,000 individuals below senior manager level to be subject to annual certification checks and appear on the Financial Services Register. Raising the conduct rule breach reporting threshold for most staff below senior manager level and streamlining Conduct Rule training requirements. This enables firms to better target more serious misconduct. Certain Senior Manager roles, such as CEOs, CFOs and Chairs, will continue to require regulator pre-approval, including fit and proper tests, before appointment. Regulators will also be able to require pre-approval for otherwise notified roles in high-risk cases. Firms will remain responsible for ensuring their employees remain competent, suitable and meet appropriate standards of conduct, and those no longer requiring pre-approval will continue to be held to the same level of accountability as before. Katharine Braddick, Deputy Governor for Prudential Regulation and Chief Executive Officer of the PRA, said: “The Senior Managers Regime is an essential part of the UK’s regulatory framework. These proposals keep checks in place for the most important roles, meaning individuals are accountable for their actions, but reduce the administrative burden where it isn’t needed, giving firms more time to invest in growth-focused activities and greater flexibility in onboarding senior talent.” Sarah Pritchard, Deputy CEO, said: “SM&CR has delivered significant improvements in accountability and governance across financial services. We remain committed to ensuring individual accountability and good standards of behaviour across financial services. But we can achieve the same impact with a more streamlined regime, supporting our aim to be a smarter regulator.” Some of the proposed reforms require legislative change. By consulting now, the FCA and PRA will be ready to implement reforms quickly once legislation is passed. The consultations are now open until 22 January, seeking views on how the regime can be made more proportionate while maintaining high standards of individual accountability and conduct. The consultations invite feedback on all aspects of the proposals with policy expected to follow in 2027. This was announced as part of Mansion House speeches delivered by Katharine Braddick and Nikhil Rathi. In her speech, Katharine unveiled a five-year strategy for the PRA designed to transform the regulator, focusing on the resilience of the financial sector, the regulator’s growth and competitiveness objective, innovating with data and technology and boosting transparency. Notes to editors Read and engage with the PRA’s consultation . Read and respond to the FCA's consultation , and review the accompanying cost-benefit analysis. These consultations are the second and most significant phase of SM&CR reform. They build on changes in April 2026 , including longer timelines for senior manager applications following unexpected or temporary changes, removal of duplicate certification requirements for overlapping functions, and a 30% increase in enhanced firm thresholds for larger firms. The reforms are expected to reduce PRA SM&CR pre-approvals by 43% and halve the overall burden of the PRA regime. For FCA Enhanced solo-regulated firms where fewer SMFs apply, around 15% of applications would move to notification and 2 SMF roles would be removed, saving a further 19%. The PRA’s latest quarterly data shows that 98% of applications were determined within the proposed new two-month statutory deadline, compared with 98.3% in the FCA’s most recent quarterly metrics. The proposals build on wider PRA and FCA initiatives to support growth and competitiveness, including reforms to the ring-fencing regime to enable more flexible sharing of operational resources, proposals to index over 100 PRA thresholds to nominal GDP growth, and FCA reforms to strengthen the attractiveness of UK capital markets and support investment, and joint PRA/FCA initiatives to help innovative firms start up, scale up and compete internationally. title: Minutes of the Securities Lending Committee meeting – September 2026
body:
Minutes of the Securities Lending Committee meeting – September 2026 | Bank of England – the UK's central bank Our use of cookies We use necessary cookies to make our site work. We’d also like to use some non-essential cookies (including third-party cookies) to help us improve the site. By clicking ‘Accept recommended settings’ on this banner, you accept our use of analytics cookies.   For more information on how these cookies work please see our Cookie policy . Accept recommended cookies Proceed with necessary cookies only Skip to main content Minutes of the Securities Lending Committee meeting – September 2026 The Securities Lending Committee is a forum for market participants and authorities to discuss the UK securities lending market. Published on  
        22 October 2026 Date: 15 September 2026 Time: 2.30pm – 4.30pm | Location: Bank of England, 20 Moorgate, London EC2R 6DA Minutes Item 1: Welcome and introductory remarks The Chair opened the meeting and welcomed the members and observers. Item 2: Diversity, Equity & Inclusion The Committee discussed the developing strategies for attracting and retaining early career talent in the securities finance industry. Development and retainment strategies aimed to provide early career staff with opportunities to diversify knowledge and experience across firms. Other initiatives included firm-wide roll out of leadership programmes driving alignment across the workforce. Item 3: SLC Tax & Regs Update The SLC Tax & Regulations sub-committee provided an update noting increased operational challenges created by holding-period rules and record date requirements across national tax regimes. Implementation of T+1 accelerated settlement could amplify existing issues, should firms fail to adapt. The group noted the need for greater tax harmonisation and monitoring tax-related risk across jurisdictions. Item 4: T+1 Update Industry participants are broadly on track for implementation in October 2027 but there are significant differences in readiness between firms. Operational challenges around securities lending recalls, collateral sourcing, funding, settlement timing, partial settlements and agent lender capabilities persist. Future competitiveness may depend on collateral agility, automation, real-time processing and the ability to support same-day operational workflows. The group noted that T+1 readiness extends beyond compliance and requires scalable operating models capable of supporting future market changes. Item 5: Market update The Committee made observations on business growth, capital optimisation and market evolution and discussed increased use of central counterparties, collateral efficiency mechanisms and smart collateral structures. Members highlighted growth opportunities in newer markets and the growing importance of digital asset initiatives, including the rise of tokenisation programmes. Digital collateral discussions centred on how infrastructure projects could eventually reshape financing markets. Upcoming regulatory developments, mandatory clearing requirements and operational changes could affect lenders, borrowers and investment funds over the coming years. Item 6: Changes in the Digital Landscape The group discussed digital assets and market infrastructure noting regulatory developments supporting tokenisation, digital securities, collateral usage, and digital market infrastructure programmes. There are multiple industry working groups examining repo, collateral mobility, payments, legal frameworks and digital securities issuance. Practical use cases remain the critical challenge. The group discussed a legal case involving the potential re-characterisation of a securities financing transaction as a secured loan, where the outcome could have significant implications for repos, securities lending and contractual certainty. Members noted the pace of development in artificial intelligence and characterised current adoption as primarily efficiency-driven rather than fully autonomous decision-making. Use cases have tended to centre on administrative tasks, information retrieval, data aggregation, recall processing and enhanced transparency across funding and collateral books. The group discussed evolution of AI use from individual productivity tools into strategic infrastructure with the potential to influence trading activity, client selection, collateral mobility and decision-making. Concerns remain around use of AI in governance, resilience, vendor oversight and data security, particularly if AI systems gained access to sensitive operational data. Item 7: AOB No further business. Attendees M&G - Chair, Nina Moylett Blackrock - Tim McLeod Clifford Chance - Habib Motani Goldman Sachs - Johanne Armita HSBC - Jamie Anderson ICMA - Godfried de Vidts JP Morgan - Harpreet Bains Morgan Stanley - Krishan Chada MUFG - Tim Smollen M&G Plc - Simon Dunderdale State Street Global Markets - Matt Neville Blackrock - Davina Stickland (Tax & Regulatory sub-committee) Clifford Chance - Caroline Dawson (Tax & Regulatory sub-committee) HSBC - Shikha Kalra (Tax & Regulatory sub-committee) ISLA - Adrian Dale (Tax & Regulatory sub-committee) Norges Bank IM - Christy Stagemeyer (Tax & Regulatory sub-committee) Bank of England - Simon Dolan Bank of England - Trinity Frost Bank of England - Kirstine McMillan Apologies AIMA - Adam Jacobs-Dean Barclays - Devi Aujeet ISLA - Ina Budh-Raja Norges Bank IM - Morten Gevoll Convert this page to PDF Other news News // News release 22 October 2026 Regulators unveil plans to simplify Senior... title: NVIDIA Unveils Minerva to Bring End-to-End Observability for AI Factories
body: NVIDIA Unveils Minerva to Bring End-to-End Observability for AI Factories New AIOps platform connects infrastructure and workload telemetry to help operators increase uptime and maximize AI factory yield. October 22, 2026 by Brian Sparks 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Launched today, NVIDIA Minerva is an AIOps platform built to help teams find problems earlier and keep AI factories productive. It brings together telemetry from infrastructure and AI workloads, then applies purpose-built AI models to turn that data into timely, actionable insight. AI factories are among the most complex operations in the world, with vast numbers of GPUs working across high-speed networks to train models and serve AI applications. At that scale, a single degraded component can slow an entire job. The warning signs may be easy to miss, such as a GPU running hotter than its peers or an NVMe drive losing performance under load. The platform focuses on AI factory yield, a measure of the useful work infrastructure produces through GPU hours, goodput, cluster uptime and token production. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Delivering a Dynamic View of an AI Factory Traditional monitoring tools often divide the data center into separate views. Networking, compute, site reliability and machine learning teams each see a different part of the operation. Minerva connects those signals across NVIDIA GPUs, networking, storage, schedulers and workloads. With these signals, Minerva builds a dynamic knowledge graph that logically maps the infrastructure — GPUs, SuperNICs, switches and cables — and the jobs running on it. This context helps operators trace a slow training job to the component affecting it, even across a factory with hundreds of thousands of GPUs. It analyzes billions of data points per hour using supervised and unsupervised machine learning. It learns normal behavior, detects previously unseen anomalies, predicts emerging failures and correlates related events based on the factory’s topology. Instead of sending every symptom to an operator, it can group an event storm into a focused incident with a likely root cause. Minerva comes with a native AI assistant and connects to external agentic AI tools. This adds a natural-language interface grounded in live telemetry. Operators can investigate cluster health and receive recommended remediation through conversation. Teams can keep a person in the loop to manually implement fixes or connect Minerva to automation through infrastructure application programming interfaces and external systems. Results That Maximize AI Factory Yield The ability to correlate workload and infrastructure issues along with its agentic AI capabilities help simplify AI factory operations. Instead of dealing with a blizzard of alerts, Minerva aggregates related problems into a single actionable item. This allows AIOps teams to move from reactive to proactive maintenance. And all of this helps AI factories maximize GPU uptime. Minerva delivers value for the key metrics AI factories focus on: Longer time between interruptions : Minerva spots trouble before it happens, so jobs run longer without incident. Faster time to repair : When an incident does happen, Minerva pinpoints the problem, leading to a significantly quicker resolution. Greater insight : Modern AI infrastructure generates a flood of data; Minerva filters it out, leaving only the handful of alerts that actually matter. IREN is among the NVIDIA partners using Minerva to optimize its AI factories. “As we scale our AI factories, the key to providing the best service for our customers is maximizing the productivity of our GPUs,” said Denis Skrinnikoff, chief technology officer of IREN. “NVIDIA Minerva gives our operations team one view across the network, the GPUs and the jobs running on them, so we focus more on proactive maintenance rather than troubleshooting. That visibility strengthens our operating model for the infrastructure we’re building next.” Joining IREN , Aolani , Bitdeer AI , IBM , Jio, Lambda , Quake AI and Tesla plan to deploy Minerva. In addition to Dell Technologies , Lenovo and Supermicro will offer Minerva as part of their AI factory operations portfolios. Learn more about NVIDIA Minerva . See notice regarding software product information. title: Cloud Deployment Incoming: ‘Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’ Arrives on GeForce NOW
body: Cloud Deployment Incoming: ‘Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’ Arrives on GeForce NOW Get memberships through Amazon on Fire TV, rally a party in ‘FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE’ and explore Season Two of ‘The Elder Scrolls Online.’ October 22, 2026 by GeForce NOW Community 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Lock in and load out this GFN Thursday. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 arrives on GeForce NOW at launch, bringing a new campaign, multiplayer action and DMZ, high-stakes extraction mode to supported devices . The campaign also gets an enhanced look: GeForce RTX 5080-class performance arrives for Ultimate members, bringing support for ray-tracing features in the cloud. There’s a new way to join the cloud, too: Existing supported Fire TV Stick users can now purchase one-month Performance or Ultimate memberships directly through Amazon, making it easier to sign up and start streaming on the big screen. Plus, Square Enix’s FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE brings cinematic pixel art and strategic battles to the cloud, and The Elder Scrolls Online’s Echoes of Skyrim Season adds the entire Greymoor Chapter free for all ESO Standard Edition owners. It’s all part of six games joining the GeForce NOW library this week. Deployment Without the Downloads Squad up and answer the call on the cloud. Activision and Infinity Ward’s Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches today on GeForce NOW. Members can drop into the trenches in Korea, close-quarter combat in New York, high-octane chases through Paris, night raids in Mumbai and city-wide engagements to reclaim occupied territory. Fight as Private Park, a young South Korean soldier facing live combat for the first time alongside his squad as a routine patrol turns into a desperate fight for survival. Beyond the front lines, operator-turned-outlaw Captain Price is operating outside the system he once served, pursuing revenge through covert missions as the conflict spreads. Multiplayer pairs precise combat with fluid movement, a dozen core 6v6 maps from around the world and battlegrounds that are shaped by the campaign’s global conflict. The DMZ extraction mode sends players into contested territory to recover valuable technology, weigh objectives and decide when to get out. Loot, fight, negotiate, betray and extract — it’s all fair in the cloud and battleground. Ultimate members can now experience the campaign with ray tracing, powered by newly added GeForce RTX 5080-class performance across PCs, Macs, handhelds, mobile devices, browsers, supported TVs and more. With game downloads and installs handled by GeForce NOW, members can spend less time preparing a local rig and more time preparing the next loadout. A New Way to Play A new way to join GeForce NOW on Fire TV. GeForce NOW in-app purchase is rolling out to existing supported Fire TV Stick users, making it possible to purchase a membership directly through Amazon using an existing account. Transactions are processed through Amazon’s billing system, creating a more seamless path from setup to gameplay. GeForce NOW transforms Fire TV into a powerful PC gaming rig in the cloud. Members can stream supported PC games they already own or purchase new titles from digital stores including Steam, Epic Games Store, Ubisoft Connect, Xbox PC Game Pass, GOG and EA. The library includes thousands of ready-to-play games, including many of the world’s most-played titles and more than 100 free-to-play games. No downloads, installs, patches or updates stand between a new game and playtime. An Amazon Fire TV Stick, the GeForce NOW app and an Ultimate membership are all it takes to level up the living room with GeForce RTX 5080-powered gaming. A Pixel-Perfect Fantasy Classic roots. A new adventure. Square Enix’s FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE launches today on GeForce NOW, bringing the series’ classic roots into a cinematic pixel-art world. Travel with companions bound by fate and uncover the truth behind a force threatening to bring everything to ruin. Strengthen the party with Visions of beloved FINAL FANTASY characters, each bringing unique skills and abilities to battle. Dynamic camera angles and pixelized 3D models give familiar fantasy a fresh perspective. title: The Trump Administration is Making Homeownership More Affordable
body: October 22, 2026 Proposed Rules Implement the ROAD to Housing Act and Support Affordable Homeownership in America WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury issued proposed regulations to make homeownership more affordable for hardworking Americans. The proposed regulations implement Section 1001 of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (ROAD to Housing Act), which restricts large institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes, codifying key requirements of President Trump’s Executive Order 14376 , Stopping Wall Street from Competing with Main Street Homebuyers . “Under President Trump, this Administration continues to restore the path to affordable homeownership for millions of young and working families,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent . “Treasury is working to ensure American families and workers have a fair shot at purchasing homes in their communities by increasing housing supply and limiting large institutional investors’ role in the market, while supporting a strong, stable housing market and avoiding unnecessary disruption.” RESTORING THE AMERICAN DREAM OF HOMEOWNERSHIP Beginning on January 7, 2027, a large institutional investor generally may not purchase, or enter into a contract to purchase, a single-family home unless the purchase qualifies as an “excepted purchase” under the ROAD to Housing Act. The ROAD to Housing Act defines a large institutional investor by reference to, among other things, whether an entity is engaged in the business of investing in, owning, renting, managing, or holding single-family homes and has direct or indirect investment control over at least 350 such homes. The ROAD to Housing Act permits several categories of excepted purchases, including purchases made pursuant to build-to-rent programs, renovate-to-rent programs, homeownership programs, and programs to boost homeownership. Today’s NPRM sets forth Treasury’s proposed framework to: Establish standards for purchases made pursuant to build-to-rent programs that promote continued investment in new housing; Provide a safe harbor for purchases made pursuant to renovate-to-rent programs that bring neglected homes back into the housing supply and up to code; Clarify the requirements for homeownership programs and programs to boost homeownership, including providing safe harbors for large institutional investors that provide meaningful financial support towards their renters’ purchase of a home; Clarify that an entity is engaged “in the business of” investing in , owning, renting, managing, or holding single-family homes when it does so for the purpose of receiving income or financial gain, and not incidentally to a different business; Define when an entity may qualify as a passive investor in another entity that owns a home because it does not share directors or officers with the other entity and does not have a property control right over the underlying homes; Clarify certain purchases involving debts previously contracted, loss mitigation, and transfers between large institutional investors that protect the liquidity of the housing market; and Clarify the calculation of the maximum civil penalty where a single prohibited purchase involves more than one large institutional investor. The proposed rule would provide non-exclusive safe harbors for several statutory requirements. These include standards for determining whether a home has been substantially rehabilitated under a renovate-to-rent program, whether a renter has received meaningful financial support under certain homeownership programs, and whether a renter has received a right of first refusal and 30-day first-look period. Treasury’s proposed approach recognizes that housing-market participants use a variety of ownership, investment, construction, servicing, and property-management structures and seeks to provide clarity without unnecessary disruption to housing supply, homebuilding, rehabilitation activity, or capital formation. Members of the public should submit comments in response to the NPRM within 30 days after publication in the Federal Register. The proposed regulations are available here . ###

title: We are working with Voltus to build a 1-gigawatt virtual power plant.
body: We are working with Voltus to build a 1-gigawatt virtual power plant. Oct 22, 2026 Today, Google and Voltus announced an expanded agreement to build a 1-gigawatt (GW) virtual power plant across the PJM grid region, which serves 67 million people across 13 states and Washington, D.C. Voltus aggregates flexible capacity from local businesses and homes — like smart thermostats, batteries, and industrial assets — into a Google-funded virtual power plant. During peak demand, these assets temporarily reduce energy use to support grid reliability. In return, participating customers receive direct economic benefits, including bill savings and cash payments. Building on a 100-megawatt agreement from earlier this year, this 10-fold expansion represents one of the largest known distributed capacity portfolios deployed by a hyperscaler to date. This initiative reflects Google’s commitment to actively bring new capacity to local grids while strengthening regional reliability and affordability.

title: Leading European Financial Services Organizations Embrace Open Models to Build Proprietary Intelligence
body: Leading European Financial Services Organizations Embrace Open Models to Build Proprietary Intelligence From transaction foundation models to sovereign cloud deployments, leading financial institutions across Europe are scaling intelligent technologies with advanced computing. October 21, 2026 by Jason Renders 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! At GTC Berlin, banks, payment companies and financial data providers are showing what production-scale intelligence looks like — built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, powered by open weight models and running on their own infrastructure. Revolut is rebuilding its technology stack on a single foundation model PRAGMA , powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. Using the NVIDIA cuDF toolkit and Dynamo-Triton software on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs , Revolut is scaling PRAGMA in production, servicing an initial 80 million customers and engineered to scale 3x. “Revolut processes billions of transactions — the opportunity was always there, but the question was whether foundation models could operate at that scale and across domains. PRAGMA answers that,” said Pavel Nesterov, head of AI at Revolut. “Built in collaboration with NVIDIA, it’s the clearest proof yet that the gap between a research breakthrough and a production banking system can be closed.” Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Training on Accelerated Infrastructure Starling Bank , the first bank to train an agentic model on U.K. sovereign cloud infrastructure, has developed “Starling Intelligence” — the intelligence layer that underpins its AI capability — on Civo’s U.K. cloud using the bank’s own transaction data. Lloyds Banking Group built ATUM , a transaction foundation model that converts billions of banking transactions into reusable intelligence — accelerated with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and improving efficiency across bank-wide use cases. SBS launched a banking sovereign intelligence platform so banks can run generative and agentic models without their data leaving their own walls. Open Models at a Fraction of the Cost Open weight models give European financial institutions proprietary intelligence built on data they own, at costs they control. NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform is the engine running beneath them. Neobank bunq’s agentic assistant Finn now runs on open weight models. Powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, deploying on Nebius matches the quality of leading closed models at 60% of the cost per answer. NatWest is building technology designed to recognize the full range of British accents, dialects and financial terminology, developed with NVIDIA’s speech models, including Nemotron 3.5 ASR. Modulr is building specialized models for distinct parts of payment operations, based on the NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B open model. Santander is an early adopter of the new NVIDIA Kumo family of open weight foundation models for structured financial data, using them to build specialized intelligence for core banking workloads. Accelerated Computing Transforms Financial Research LSEG is working with NVIDIA to help financial institutions analyze large volumes of historical tick data up to 10x faster with the Polars GPU engine , accelerated by NVIDIA cuDF on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. RavenPack built a dataset generation pipeline on Bigdata.com that takes a plain-language research hypothesis and returns a labeled, backtest-ready dataset — running on a fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron model. Investors can use these datasets to identify, analyze and visualize market trends. Speeding Data Pipelines to Improve Fraud Detection RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs and NVIDIA cuDF help accelerate data processing across multi-terabyte-scale, siloed, regulated sources, compressing the time from data to decision for fraud and other scenarios. HSBC provides near-real-time client insights that support customer processes and on-demand decision-making while minimizing risk and fraud, powered by 5x faster data processing on Starburst Enterprise’s GPU Engine . Stripe , a global provider of programmable financial services, sees 42x faster data pipelines and 92% cost savings for its Stripe Radar fraud-detection platform with NVIDIA GPU-accelerated Ray Data in offline testing. This enables Stripe Radar’s machine learning pipelines to continuously optimize model training and improve fraud detection. Learn more about NVIDIA accelerated computing in financial services . See notice regarding software product information. title: NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models
body: NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models New tools joining NVIDIA Cosmos are helping accelerate data pipelines, train, evaluate and optimize world models more efficiently, and improve accuracy at lower cost. October 21, 2026 by Pranjali Joshi 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! To help developers rapidly build world models , which help physical AI systems understand and simulate the real world, NVIDIA has expanded the Cosmos platform with new training tools, simulation checkpoints and Cosmos Data Factory blueprints. Ranking top five on six different open models leaderboards, the NVIDIA Cosmos platform gives world model builders the frontier open models — as well as data, training and optimization tools and recipes — to scale training data, adapt models, test behavior and optimize for performance before deployment. Build Better Training Data Building world models begins with multimodal, multisensory data. NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory brings together the tools and skills for labeling, curating, augmenting and evaluating data at scale for training physical AI. Cosmos Curator, a GPU-accelerated solution for curating video training datasets, has now added support for multimodal multisensory inputs and processing blocks. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Cosmos Data Factory now offers the following five cloud-native blueprints and is available through GitHub , Microsoft Azure , Nebius and CoreWeave : Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation: Curates and labels driving data, then adds synthetic examples of hard-to-capture scenarios to expand training coverage. Image Attribute Augmentation: Varies object appearance to improve image search. Event Video Generation: Turns still images into synthetic videos of rare or unsafe events. Defect Image Generation: Generates printed circuit board, metal and glass defect images for inspection models. Video Data Augmentation: Changes weather and lighting in existing footage while preserving scene structure. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/CDF-visual-Oct20.mp4 Cosmos Data Factory accelerates data curation, processing and synthetic data generation with agentic skills. Companies are already putting Cosmos Data Factory blueprints to work to speed their physical AI development workflows. Porsche is leading the development of a shared AV data flywheel across Volkswagen Group brands, using Cosmos Data Factory through Voxel51 on Microsoft Azure. This is expected to reduce repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and shorten development cycle times by up to 85%. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Porche-Cosmos-Data-Factory.mp4 Porsche searching and augmenting autonomous vehicle data footage in Voxel51, powered by Cosmos Data Factory. ANYbotics generated over 1,500 synthetic video clips with Cosmos Data Factory blueprints, curating real-world data and validating outputs with Encord’s platform, to train its industrial-inspection robots to recognize liquid spills and other changes between facility visits. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ANYbotics-Cosmos-Data-Factory.mp4 ANYbotic s generating anomaly clips with Encord powered by NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory. Ultralytics , a computer vision company, retrained its YOLO model with real images and targeted synthetic defects generated using Cosmos Data Factory, improving defect localization and recall. Train, Adapt and Optimize Models With training data prepared, developers may train their own architecture or start with a pretrained model. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA extended Cosmos Framework training, optimization and deployment tools and recipes as agent skills to more open models, along with Cosmos 3, giving world model builders a faster path from experimentation to deployment. Developers and agents can now adapt open models like GR00T , Alpamayo , QWEN, Pi0.5 and other compatible Hugging Face models through fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, optimize the model with distillation and quantization, and deploy with high-performing inference. Cosmos Framework is an open, modular framework of model training and optimization tools and skills to accelerate world model development. To develop a world model specialized for egocentric manipulation, robotics research lab MicroAGI post-trained Cosmos 3 on videos of humans manipulating objects and distilled its 32-billion-parameter reasoner down to an 8-billion-parameter Nano model with no loss in accuracy. Developers can label data and post-train Cosmos 3 on Roboflow for their specific environments and tasks, then deploy those models to RoboFlow hosted or on-premises NVIDIA GPUs to bring video reasoning into factories and warehouses. Test Policies and Run Models Faster Alongside these tools, NVIDIA continues advancing foundational technology through its work on Cosmos models. New Cosmos 3 Nano model variants for simulation enable developers to test autonomous policies in repeatable, hard-to-capture, multiview multisensor scenarios. Accompanying code allows developers to adapt the models to train and evaluate their own policies for autonomous vehicles and bimanual robots in interactive simulations before real-world testing. Multiview and multisensory video data generation for evaluating policies in closed loop simulation. Developers can deploy core Cosmos models using updated NVIDIA Cosmos 3 NIM microservices, which deliver up to 2x faster inference with no quality loss in validated configurations, while continuous video analysis enables sub-second alerts. For vision AI developers, the new NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) 3.3 , built on Cosmos NIM microservices, turns one prompt into an efficient video AI application and helps teams monitor 40% more video streams with the same GPU. ADNOC uses Fogsphere’s MistIQ agentic platform , built with Cosmos and the NVIDIA Metropolis VSS Blueprint , to detect safety hazards in real time across 65 sites. For rare events, Fogsphere also uses the Cosmos Data Factory to generate synthetic training data, improving detection without needing to physically stage dangerous situations. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ADNOC-Cosmos.mp4 The Cosmos platform is fully modular and open. Developers can use Cosmos Data Factory to generate training datasets, Cosmos Framework to train and adapt world models, then deploy supported Cosmos models through NIM microservices . title: How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck
body: How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck Companies around the world are using the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run AI factories as one system and unlock infrastructure development. October 21, 2026 by Vladimir Troy 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Companies around the world are building on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run the grid and the AI factory as one system, from the substation to the rack. Their adoption of the platform responds to an acute problem. Power is now the biggest bottleneck in infrastructure. More than $300 billion in equipment is backlogged, and over 200 gigawatts of projects are waiting in U.S. interconnection queues. One root cause of the bottleneck is siloed systems. The grid, the facility and the compute inside have long been designed independently from one another, creating the conditions for delays, risk and stranded capacity. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements To help address this, NVIDIA DSX brings these systems together: NVIDIA DSX Sim and SimReady assets from leading energy manufacturers let engineers simulate the grid, substation and AI factory together, validating generators, switchgear, power systems and cooling before breaking ground. NVIDIA DSX Flex syncs AI factory demand with grid conditions and onsite generation, turning AI factories from static loads into flexible grid assets. NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS and DSX Exchange squeeze more compute from every watt and securely share signals across compute, networking, energy, cooling and operations. GE Vernova is deploying its grid-to-facility and rack power expertise to complement NVIDIA DSX systems, enabling customers to transform power constraints into competitive advantages while maximizing compute and token output, sustainability and grid reliability. Hitachi Energy ’s battery energy storage system has qualified as NVIDIA DSX Ready ,  helping customers identify power infrastructure that meets applicable NVIDIA DSX reference architecture design requirements for resilient, reliable and scalable AI factories. Schneider Electric , together with AVEVA and ETAP, is advancing NVIDIA DSX with validated NVIDIA Vera Rubin power and cooling reference architectures and an NVIDIA Omniverse -powered AI factory digital twin. Combining AVEVA ’s engineering software expertise with NVIDIA SimReady assets, OpenUSD and Omniverse enables connecting simulations, real-time operational data and AI-driven optimization across AVEVA, Schneider Electric and third-party solutions. Together, these capabilities help organizations design, simulate, operate and optimize data centers across their lifecycle, improving energy efficiency and workload performance while accelerating time to token. Siemens Energy is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA by developing a reference design for resilient, scalable and grid-aware power infrastructure across power generation, transmission and distribution. This design is aligned with the requirements of the NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factory design. The company is also exploring usingNVIDIA technologies such as RAPIDS, Metropolis and Isaac Sim for its Noedra digital twin platform, evaluating how the technologies could enhance grid infrastructure monitoring, identify emerging risks and support unplanned outage prevention. Phaidra integrated DSX Flex, DSX Max-Q and DSX Exchange into its self-learning agents, optimizing cooling and power allocation to maximize tokens per watt, improve grid flexibility and deliver about 10% more compute within the same power envelope. Emerald AI integrated its Conductor platform into DSX Flex to help utilities tap underused grid capacity, an approach modeled to unlock up to 100 gigawatts on the existing U.S. grid. Explore the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint and the Vera Rubin DSX AI Factory Reference Design . Learn more from NVIDIA and energy leaders who are accelerating power-flexible AI factories to strengthen the grid at GTC Berlin. Visit Hitachi Energy (booth 7004, hall 7), Schneider Electric (booth 3041, hall 3) and Siemens Energy (booth 3048, hall 3) and tune into sessions with Schneider Electric on Wednesday, Oct. 21: From Grid to AI: Engineering the Future of AI Factories and Energy Intelligence: Powering the AI Era . body: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations October 21, 2026 by Mavi Nafria 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin. Frontier Results With Open Models Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D. Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements On Shopify’s internal benchmark, the post-trained model surpasses a leading frontier model in accuracy while cutting serving costs by 90% and delivering responses 7x faster. Beyond Sidekick, NVIDIA CCluster vLLM inference optimization software helped Shopify achieve 4.5x faster performance and up to 12x lower inference cost across five additional use cases: catalog enrichment, merchant assistant, e-commerce shopping simulation, product taxonomy classification, and merchant and buyer recommendations. Zooplus , Europe’s leading online pet retailer, with Infosys and NVIDIA technologies rebuilt its product discovery stack for the agentic era. A production ready prototype deployed inside Zooplus ’ Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment achieved 86% search accuracy using the NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever library for semantic search and the NVIDIA Blueprint for retail catalog enrichment for generated, search-ready product attributes. Photoroom results from its deployment with Vestiaire Collective , where its Image Editing API now standardizes every primary image,  about 40,000 a day across 70 countries, at the point of listing. Listings processed by Photoroom sold at a 5% higher rate of liquidity, with 3% to 7% more unique views per product page . The pipeline runs on NVIDIA GPUs with TensorRT and Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo Snapshot can help users quickly respond to demand spikes. Omi launched ProductDrop, a workflow that anchors every generated image to an approved digital twin, letting brands scale creative output across entire catalogs without introducing product errors . L’Oréal is using this approach, combining Omi ’s digital twins with generated brand environments within its CreAItech program. Omi runs TRELLIS 3D asset generation on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, speeding up inference by 10x and reducing pipeline latency by 4x. In addition, L’Oréal is accelerating the discovery of the best ingredient combinations, moving from months of experimentation to hours of computational screening, with the integration of NVIDIA ALCHEMI into its research workflow. L’Oréal is also testing this approach with CurieOS, Orbital Industries ‘ operating system for science and engineering, using OrbMol-v2, its open source molecular simulation model. Integrated with the NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit and powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, OrbMol-v2 is five times faster than comparable models and delivers 21% lower error than the next-best model of its kind. This AI-based workflow enables researchers to identify the most promising ingredient combinations for solubilizing UV filters and optimizing performance before committing to laboratory testing. Mirakl , a software company for intelligent commerce, runs open models on NVIDIA GPUs, both on its own infrastructure and through European cloud providers like Scaleway . This keeps its technology sovereign, avoids vendor lock-in and delivers the speed and scale its customers expect . Mirakl ’s Catalog Transformer pairs fine-tuned open models with proprietary services and has onboarded more than 70 million products, turning messy vendor data into accurate, well-organized catalogs. Physical Intelligence Enables Training in Simulation NVIDIA physical AI, digital twins and open models help simulate retail environments, automate warehouse operations and deliver virtual try-on experiences for European retailers and fashion brands. Otto Group advanced its autonomous warehouse under human supervision initiative — built with Reply on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and running on Google Cloud — to the group’s largest fulfillment center in Haldensleben, Germany. New capabilities let logistics teams design, test and optimize warehouse operations entirely in simulation before any physical implementation . ALLSIDES launched its 3D Digital Twin Factory: an automated pipeline that transforms physical objects into SimReady 3D digital twins in minutes, capturing sub-millimeter geometric accuracy, measured physical properties and fully relightable materials that maintain accuracy under any lighting condition. Those digital twins serve as the foundation for simulating entire store layouts in 3D, as well as for tracking products reliably throughout the shopping journey and at checkout regardless of ambient light. Built on NVIDIA CUDA, OptiX and TensorRT, the platform already serves brands including adidas , Amazon , Nike , Zalando and Zara . CATCHES achieved production results from its RealFit deployment with AMIRI of conversion up 55%, add-to-cart up 80% and gross sales up 56% , all after seasonal adjustment against like-for-like styles. The company launched PredictiveFit, extending physics-based virtual try-on to retailers, as well as CASI, a personal fashion agent that shops, styles and sizes for customers over WhatsApp, powered by open weight models including NVIDIA Nemotron 3, built on NVIDIA Omniverse and the Newton Physics Engine. Explore New NVIDIA Retail Blueprints at the Nebius Booth At GTC Berlin, Nebius is showcasing three NVIDIA Blueprints for retail , all available in early access and running on Nebius infrastructure, accelerated by NVIDIA: Agent Harness for Employee Productivity : An agentic assistant that consolidates scheduling, task management, inventory alerts and operational insights for store managers. Inventory Simulation and Optimization: A blueprint that can help retailers reduce overstock and stockouts by modeling demand scenarios, testing replenishment strategies and optimizing stock levels before users need to commit in the real world. Agentic Finetuning Flywheel: A self-improving loop that uses agentic workflows to continuously generate training data, fine-tune open source models and feed real-world performance back into the next training cycle. Request early access to the blueprints and learn more about NVIDIA technologies for retail and consumer packaged goods . See notice regarding software product information. title: Pioneers Across Europe Deploy NVIDIA Earth-2 Open Models to Power Real-World Weather and Climate Prediction
body: Pioneers Across Europe Deploy NVIDIA Earth-2 Open Models to Power Real-World Weather and Climate Prediction October 21, 2026 by Niall Robinson 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Weather forecasts shape more than daily plans; timely weather information is crucial for energy producers, insurers and transport operators to plan around changing conditions. A global forecast can show a storm taking shape, but decisions about solar farms, shipping routes or insured property depend on what happens locally. NVIDIA Earth-2 gives developers and researchers a family of open AI models and tools they can customize with their own data. Running on NVIDIA computing, these technologies support global weather prediction, detailed regional forecasts and environmental research. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements StormScope EU is the latest model to join Earth-2 — a regional version of the StormScope model for short-term forecasting, trained over Europe weather and climate data. It uses EUMETSAT satellite observations to predict evolving cloud conditions across 16 Meteosat channels at 10-minute intervals. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing a live StormScope EU pipeline in an interactive weather demo built in partnership with Earthmover . The demo uses Earth2Studio to run forecasts and Earthmover’s data platform to manage and serve the real-time results, which are updated as soon as new satellite observations come in, every 10 minutes. Earthmover serves these results as map tiles, letting visitors explore predictions across Europe without downloading entire datasets. Developers can combine Earth-2 models in workflows tailored to regional needs, using StormScope for short-term forecasting and CorrDiff to add local detail to coarser weather data. Developers can also pick up these model architectures and train them for new environmental applications such as air-quality modeling. The open source NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo framework provides training and customization tools so teams can build applications that incorporate proprietary data and domain expertise to meet regional needs. Organizations building on Earth-2 capabilities include: AXA is using NVIDIA Earth-2’s FourCastNet 3 to study regional cyclone risk beyond the historical record across more than 1,000 simulated seasons, generating insights that can inform risk assessments and help customers target prevention efforts. Vaisala Xweather is combining Earth-2 with its proprietary observations , lightning data and forecasting expertise to enhance its weather intelligence platforms for government, energy, maritime, transportation and insurance customers. Its work includes adapting StormScope with lightning data to advance short-term forecasting lead time and make these warnings accessible through Vaisala Xweather’s software-as-a-service offerings and AI-assistant integrations. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Vaisala-Xweather-Nvidia-StormScope.mp4 Video courtesy of Vaisala Xweather. University of Manchester researchers adapted the Earth-2 CorrDiff model for U.K. air-quality modeling. It trained the model on the NVIDIA-powered Isambard-AI supercomputer and ran it locally on NVIDIA DGX Spark systems, bringing environmental modeling from a national supercomputer to the desktop. TotalEnergies is exploring NVIDIA Earth-2 for solar-energy forecasting, evaluating StormScope-based solar-radiation nowcasts at two photovoltaic sites and developing models to provide weather information at subhourly intervals. The work explores how more detailed forecasts could help anticipate changes in solar-power generation. Space42 developed SARDiff4Height using CorrDiff and NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo. The research estimates surface heights from a single radar image and produces uncertainty maps, helping analysts understand where estimates need closer scrutiny. Explore NVIDIA Earth-2 open models and tools , and explore with Earth2Studio’s forecasting examples . Read AXA’s hurricane-risk case study and Manchester’s air-quality story to learn how teams are adapting weather AI to specialized challenges.
