title: NVIDIA Open Models Power a New Wave of European Public Sector Projects
body: NVIDIA Open Models Power a New Wave of European Public Sector Projects Across Europe, open models help governments provide essential public services while keeping sensitive data on organizations’ own infrastructure. October 21, 2026 by Eva-Maria Hempe 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Governments need modern solutions to serve the public while keeping sensitive information under their control. Open models provide a path forward, letting governments evaluate them, adapt them to local languages and public services, run them on infrastructure they control, apply their own safeguards and keep sensitive data within controlled environments. Some open models go further, with the datasets they were trained on published so governments can verify if training data was licensed, biased or compliant. NVIDIA partners and European governments are teaming to bring  advanced models to boost the efficiency of public administration while retaining control of data and infrastructure. Several are also building editions of the NVIDIA Nemotron-Personas collection , the partner-grounded datasets behind NeMo User Sim , NVIDIA’s open source library for population-scale user simulation that dynamically evaluates and trains models and agents in local languages. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements European Commission: Scaling Governed AI Applications Berlin-based software company deepset is expanding its Haystack Enterprise Platform , the foundation of AI@EC, the European Commission’s shared platform for building and running AI applications on commission-managed infrastructure. The update connects agent development, execution, optimization and governance for all customers, adding capabilities to compare operating costs, evaluate answer quality and trace problems. NVIDIA Triton Inference Server supports the shared services used to find and rank relevant information. The expansion builds on operating requirements demonstrated by deployments such as AI@EC, where reusable components, role-based access, audit trails and guardrails support applications including document summarization, knowledge management and multilingual policy analysis. Poland: Advanced Computing for Healthcare and Employment Deloitte is helping Poland build agentic systems for healthcare and employment services using open models. Poland’s eHealth Centre is building its Intelligent Services Platform for medical imaging with NVIDIA DGX BasePOD and the MONAI framework. The tool will help physicians analyze X-rays, CT scans and MRI images, detect abnormalities and prioritize urgent cases, reducing the time patients wait for results. With Deloitte’s support, Poland’s Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Policy is developing an agentic factory on NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure. Designed to support more than 400 labor offices, it will run models including PLLuM, GPT OSS and Inkling for document search, summarization and digital assistants, helping staff more efficiently assist job seekers. NVIDIA is also working with SpeakLeash in Poland and the University of Ljubljana in Slovenia on country-specific additions to its synthetic personas program, with localized datasets planned to follow. UK: Data for Locally Relevant Advanced Modeling London-based Locai Labs released Nemotron-Personas-UK , a dataset of 1 million synthetic personas reflecting the U.K.’s demographic and geographic diversity while reducing privacy risk. Potential uses include healthcare evaluation and bias testing across age groups, education levels and rural and urban populations. For developers building public-service models, it offers a way to test whether models work consistently across different communities. Germany: Digital Assistants and AI for Classified Work In Germany, Materna is introducing Sinfonie, an on-premises platform combining generative AI, voice interaction and 3D avatars, with NVIDIA Audio2Face available for animation. Built on a project for a German state administration, it helps employees access institutional knowledge through spoken questions while keeping data on their organization’s infrastructure. For organizations handling classified information, secunet, NVIDIA, Red Hat and deepset are going a step further. The four companies are developing a sovereign cloud offering built on secunet’s proven SINA Cloud foundation, which includes security components that have been authorized for use with classified information. The planned offering combines four components: NVIDIA accelerated computing and NVIDIA Nemotron open models; Red Hat OpenShift AI for deploying and managing AI workloads; deepset’s Haystack AI agent orchestration; and infrastructure operated by secunet in German data centers. To support local development, the Sovereign Open Source Foundation Models research initiative (Soofi) is developing a family of AI models for German industry and the public sector. That includes Nemotron-Personas-Germany, an open dataset of 1 million records, each with six synthetic personas, grounded in the 2022 census across all 16 federal states and 400 districts. Created with NVIDIA NeMo Data Designer without real people’s private data, the dataset helps developers test whether public-service models work consistently across regions, age groups and communities. Like the U.K. edition, it can be used with NeMo User Sim so developers can evaluate and train models against simulated users based on synthetic German personas. France: Advanced Open Models in the Public Sector Workspace CANUT, France’s public purchasing body for digital services, selected LINAGORA and Docaposte to provide a sovereign collaborative workspace built on Twake.ai. More than 2,500 eligible organizations, including municipalities, schools and healthcare institutions, can access the framework without running their own tender. The workspace offers public employees email, document sharing and collaboration tools, with NVIDIA technology supporting speech transcription and infrastructure hosted in France. Région Occitanie is the preferred partner for scaling deployment. Greece: A Local Agentic Ecosystem Greek AI and energy company KIEFER is developing an agentic factory built on NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD with DGX GB200 alongside Sophea open weight models and Greek-language tools for knowledge retrieval, speech and digital assistants. These capabilities stand to make institutional information easier to find and use for Greek-speaking public sector teams, while giving organizations control over where agents run and how data is handled. Codefest: Building the Next Applications In an effort to support public sector organizations in integrating agentic AI in Europe and beyond, NVIDIA Open Models Codefest brings together startups, software providers and labs across the region to turn open models into locally controlled solutions for public sector challenges, including medical reasoning, AI tutoring and model governance. The top five teams are Pleias , Zehnlab.ai , Disseqt , Algoritmica GmbH and ABA Technology . Deutsche Telekom and T-Systems have provided the compute infrastructure for teams to train and deploy large language models. title: October 22, 2026 - FDA Launches New Program to Advance Neuroscience Medical Product Development
body: FDA News Release FDA Launches New Program to Advance Neuroscience Medical Product Development Neuroscience Advancement and Innovation Nexus to coordinate agency action on brain and nervous system conditions, with inaugural focus on Alzheimer's prevention For Immediate Release: October 22, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today announced the launch of the Neuroscience Advancement and Innovation Nexus (NAIN) , a new agency program aligned with the Trump Administration’s efforts to accelerate medical innovation and deliver breakthrough treatments. NAIN is designed to advance the science, tools, and regulatory approaches needed to support the development of medical products for conditions affecting the brain and nervous system. NAIN’s inaugural initiative, the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator , will focus on advancing medical products that help delay or prevent Alzheimer's disease. Both efforts support the National Alzheimer’s Project Act (NAPA), the federal government's comprehensive roadmap for coordinated action on Alzheimer's and related dementias. "The launch of NAIN reflects FDA's commitment — in support of the Trump Administration’s drive to transform health care innovation — to making sure our regulatory science and cross-center collaboration keep pace with the rapid advances happening in neuroscience," said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. "Through NAIN and the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator, we are bringing the full breadth of FDA's expertise to bear on one of the most urgent public health challenges of our time.” Developing medical products for neuroscience indications is associated with complex scientific and clinical challenges, including limited understanding of underlying biology, variable disease presentation, and difficulties in demonstrating meaningful clinical benefit, particularly for conditions that develop over many years. Advances in biomarkers, digital health technologies, and other medical product development tools, however, offer important opportunities to address these challenges. NAIN will bring together scientific and regulatory expertise from the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, and Center for Devices and Radiological Health to address scientific and regulatory questions that benefit from coordinated consideration across drugs, biologics, and devices. NAIN will encompass conditions that affect the brain and nervous system broadly, including neurologic and psychiatric disorders, substance use disorders, and pain. NAIN will also support robust engagement with patients, industry, academia and other stakeholders to advance these efforts. As its first initiative, NAIN is launching the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator . This inaugural initiative will draw on perspectives from across the FDA and engage patients and caregivers, researchers, industry, public-private partnerships and other government agencies. The initiative will explore innovative approaches to advancing clinical trials for Alzheimer’s disease prevention and early-intervention drug development with emphasis on trial populations, stage-appropriate endpoints, and evidentiary approaches for demonstrating prevention or delay of cognitive decline due to Alzheimer’s disease. The FDA has long been committed to supporting the development of safe and effective medical products that address diseases and conditions of the brain and nervous system. Through NAIN and the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator, the agency is taking a proactive, coordinated approach to accelerating progress, bringing together its scientific and regulatory expertise, engaging the broader research and development community, and working in concert with federal partners to meet the scale of this public health challenge. Media: FDA Request for Comment 202-690-6343 Consumer: 888-INFO-FDA The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products. ###

title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iran’s Shadow Fleet Networks
body: October 21, 2026 Law Firms, Shipping Agents, and Vessels Helped Conceal and Transport Iranian Commodities WASHINGTON —Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury sanctioned Panama- and Greece-based law firm Karnakis and Karnakis , which has supported illicit Iranian shipping activity for years, indirectly aiding Tehran’s ability to generate revenue to fund its military, weapons, and nuclear programs.  Throughout Operation Economic Outcast, Treasury has continued to coordinate with counterparts in Europe and around the world to sever the Iranian regime’s remaining economic lifelines. “Whether you are conducting illegal oil transfers at sea or sitting in the corner office of a law firm, if you are supporting the Iranian regime, we will find you and sanction you,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Iran’s facilitators must make a choice: Either you are with us or against us. We know who you are, we know what you’re doing, and we will continue to take action.” Treasury today also sanctioned Singapore- and UAE-based shipping agents that directly aid Iranian shadow fleet operations.  Today’s actions strike not only the legal and maritime facilitators that sustain Iran's sanctions-evasion networks, but also a fleet of cargo vessels that has helped generate substantial revenue for the Iranian regime. The designations imposed today are being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian petroleum and petrochemical sectors, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy. FinCEN is acting in close coordination with European partners, including in Greece, and leveraging existing legal authorities, such as its first issuance of an administrative subpoena pursuant to 31 U.S.C. § 5318(k) of the Bank Secrecy Act, to advance its investigation into a Greek bank’s potential ties to Iran and its proxies. Additionally, FinCEN has issued multiple requests for information concerning banks’ relationships with OFAC-designated Iranian financial institutions. OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST IS ISOLATING THE IRANIAN REGIME Announced by Secretary Bessent on August 24, 2026 and dubbed Economic D-Day, Operation Economic Outcast is severing the remaining economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime. Treasury has mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terror.  Working with partners across the U.S. government, the European Union, United Kingdom, Gulf partners, and others, Treasury is targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue, as well as its sanctions evasion schemes to move funds. Operation Economic Outcast significantly expanded sanctions risk for those who continue to choose to do business with Iran.  Treasury warned that any entity facilitating money laundering or sanctions evasion on behalf of Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system.  Operation Economic Outcast also expanded sanctions exposure for non-U.S. persons who continue doing business with the Iranian regime and will accelerate the pace of U.S. enforcement. More information on Operation Economic Outcast is available here . LAW FIRM ESTABLISHING SHADOW FLEET ARCHITECTURE Through Operation Economic Outcast, Treasury is targeting law firms and corporate service providers that establish shell and front companies for persons trading in sanctioned Iranian products, an essential service needed for any such malign actor to evade sanctions or regulatory compliance.  Panama- and Greece-based law firm Karnakis and Karnakis has for years leveraged its legal practice to register shipping companies that own shadow fleet vessels responsible for shipping hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of Iranian steel, petroleum, and petrochemicals, among other goods.  The firm previously set up the companies Skyros Maritime and Trading S.A. , Corfu Maritime and Trading S.A. , and Elias Shipping and Trading Group S.A. , among others, all of which OFAC has previously designated for their ownership of vessels active in the trade of Iranian petroleum and petroleum products. Elias Shipping and Trading SA, the owner of the RAMONA 1 (IMO: 9233222), served as a front company for the Al-Qatirji Company, a Syrian firm responsible for selling millions of barrels of Iranian oil for the benefit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF) and Houthis.  The Al-Qatirji Company at the time of its designation was one of the main financial channels for the IRGC-QF, enabling the terrorist group to generate and access hundreds of millions of dollars a year in revenue gained from the sale of Iranian oil. Karnakis and Karnakis played a particularly critical role in establishing the corporate architecture for the shipping empire of Iranian liquified petroleum gas (LPG) magnate Seyed Asadoollah Emamjomeh (Emamjomeh), which is collectively responsible for shipping hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of Iranian LPG and crude oil.  Karnakis and Karnakis served as the corporate agent for many of Emamjomeh’s firms, including several that were ultimately designated for their role in shipping Iranian petroleum products. Karnakis and Karnakis was founded, and is currently owned, by dual Panamanian-Greek nationals Sofianos Karnakis Kosmas and Konstantinos Karnakis Kosmas , with Panamanian-Greek national Ioanis Karnakis Kosmas and Panamanian national Pedro Ortega Jones serving as employees of the law firm.  Karnakis and Karnakis employees, including Panamanian national Roberto Ortega Jones , act as directors and officers of many of the companies they register in order to obfuscate the true beneficial owners of these companies. Karnakis and Karnakis is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum and petrochemical sectors of the Iranian economy.  Sofianos Karnakis Kosmas, Konstantinos Karnakis Kosmas, Pedro Ortega Jones, Roberto Ortega Jones, and Ioanis Karnakis Kosmas are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Karnakis and Karnakis. CARGO FLEET VESSELS Iran relies on seemingly legitimate cargo vessels to move Iranian petrochemicals and other products, including steel.  Panama- and Greece-based Roxette Maritime Shipping and Trading S.A. (Roxette), for which Karnakis and Karnakis serves as the corporate agent, is the operator and ship manager of the Panama-flagged vessels ANEMOS (IMO 9205952), GLORIS (IMO 9449510), and PRIDE (IMO 9487407), all of which have shipped various cargos of Iranian-origin goods within the past year, including petrochemicals and steel products.  In addition, Roxette is the ship manager and operator of the Panama-flagged cargo vessels DESTINY (IMO 9385491), FLAMINGO 1 (IMO 9474199), HARMONY (IMO 9449522), and PRINCE (IMO 9548316). Roxette Maritime Shipping and Trading S.A. is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petrochemical sector of the Iranian economy.  ANEMOS, GLORIS, PRIDE, DESTINY, FLAMINGO 1, HARMONY, and PRINCE are being identified pursuant to E.O. 13902 as blocked property in which Roxette Maritime Shipping and Trading S.A. has an interest. SHIPPING AGENTS AIDING SHADOW FLEET Shipping agents play a critical role in shadow fleet operations by aiding the transit of illicit Iranian cargo through ports, including oil, petroleum, and other commodities.  Treasury is taking action against two shipping agents that have helped Iran transport its products to buyers around the world. Amigoz Singapore PTE. Ltd. (Amigoz) is a Singapore-based full-range shipping agency that provides port agency services.  Amigoz acted as the agent for a shipment of light crude oil overseen by Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company, which oversees a network of front companies that supports the allocation of billions of dollars’ worth of commodities to Iranian military entities.  As of 2026, Amigoz has been associated with a range of dark fleet actors, including some affiliated with the shipping empire of Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani , and provided bunkering services to the Iranian shadow fleet vessel ZIXUAN (IMO 9317298). Whales Shipping Line LLC (Whales), a Dubai-based maritime and logistics company, acted as the shipping agent for Sparrow Trading FZE, a sanctioned Dubai-based front company that organized the purchase of tens of millions of dollars’ worth of Iranian petrochemicals in coordination with Persian Gulf Petrochemical Industry Commercial Co.  Whales has also conducted business worth hundreds of thousands of dollars with Amigoz.  Whales is the registered owner of two UAE-flagged small support vessels: WHALES DIAMOND (IMO 9375032) and WHALES PEARL (IMO 9483114). Amigoz Singapore PTE. Ltd. is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum sector of the Iranian economy.  Whales Shipping Line LLC is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Amigoz Singapore PTE. Ltd.  WHALES DIAMOND and WHALES PEARL are being identified as blocked property in which Whales Shipping Line LLC has an interest. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities with designated or otherwise blocked persons. Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions.  OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List . title: October 20, 2026 - FDA Issues Final Guidance on Prescription Drug Apps and Software
body: FDA News Release FDA Issues Final Guidance on Prescription Drug Apps and Software New policy clarifies when app content requires FDA review and how drug-connected software must be described on medication labels For Immediate Release: October 20, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today released final guidance establishing a clear framework for how drug companies can develop, distribute, and label apps used alongside their prescription medicines. The guidance ends longstanding uncertainty by providing recommendations about when app content is subject to FDA submission requirements, when an app should be mentioned on a drug’s official label, and what companies should submit to the agency. “Mobile apps are playing a growing role in how patients manage their medications and health conditions,” said Captain Chris Wheeler, Pharm.D., Director of the Division of Medical Policy Programs within FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “This guidance helps ensure that the information these tools provide is accurate, evidence-based, and clearly communicated to both patients and their providers.” The guidance addresses three key questions for industry: when app content is treated as FDA-required labeling versus promotional labeling, when an app should be referenced in a drug’s official prescribing information, and what companies should submit to FDA when they distribute app content to users. The guidance identifies two categories of companion software: Apps connected to a medical device (such as an app paired with an asthma inhaler) generally should be described on the drug’s official prescribing label, given the central role the software plays in how the medicine is used. Standalone apps (such as symptom trackers, dose reminders, or health coaching tools) should appear on the prescribing label if the company can show the app is essential for safe and effective use or can demonstrate a meaningful clinical benefit. In most cases, content a companion app displays to users will be treated as promotional material, consistent with how the FDA handles other drug advertising. “This guidance reflects FDA’s commitment to responsible, risk-proportionate oversight of digital health, an area that is a key priority for the agency and is evolving rapidly and holds significant promise for improving patient care,” said Michael Davis, M.D., Ph.D., Director of the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “By aligning our approach across drug and device centers, we are giving developers a clear and consistent pathway to bring safe, effective digital health technologies to patients.” “Companion apps are quickly moving beyond simple dose reminders toward tools that adapt to each patient,” said Jared Seehafer, M.S., FDA Deputy Commissioner for Technology . “Finalizing this guidance gives drug companies and their technology partners a stable foundation to build on as these technologies advance and helps ensure patients and providers can trust the information they receive.” This guidance also reflects the FDA’s ongoing commitment to modernizing its regulatory framework to keep pace with rapidly evolving digital health technologies. By providing clear, practical recommendations for both drug-connected software and standalone software, the agency aims to reduce unnecessary uncertainty for developers and manufacturers while preserving the safety and effectiveness standards that patients and healthcare providers rely on. The final guidance is available here . Media: FDA Request for Comment 202-690-6343 Consumer: 888-INFO-FDA ### Boilerplate The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation's food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products.

title: October 20, 2026 - FDA Approves Once-Weekly Generic Hormone Therapy Patch for Women
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves Once-Weekly Generic Hormone Therapy Patch for Women For Immediate Release: October 20, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration yesterday approved the first generic of Climara Pro (estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system, 0.045 mg per day/0.015 mg), a transdermal hormone therapy patch for women with an intact uterus applied once a week. The approval aligns with FDA’s Public Health Pillar : Increasing Access to Affordable Medicines & Medical Products. “Menopause is a universal experience for women, and it can greatly affect a person’s quality of life. This approval makes effective treatment more accessible,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “Approvals like this reflect FDA’s ongoing commitment to expanding American patient access to safe, affordable, high-quality medications.” The generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system is therapeutically equivalent to Climara Pro, which is indicated for use in women with an intact uterus for: Treatment of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause Prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis Climara Pro and the generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system contain both estrogen and progestogen in a single patch; this differs from estrogen-only patches commonly used in menopause treatment. Climara Pro and the generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system are specifically approved for women with an intact uterus, as the progestogen component is included to reduce the risk of endometrial hyperplasia that can occur with estrogen use alone. “Once-weekly dosing can make a real difference in how patients manage their care,” said Michael Davis, M.D., Ph.D., Director of FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “A patch offers a convenient alternative to daily oral medications, which may help patients stay on track with their treatment.” Climara Pro and the generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system are contraindicated in patients with undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding; breast cancer or a history of breast cancer; estrogen-dependent neoplasia; active deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE) or a history of these conditions; active arterial thromboembolic disease or a history of these conditions; known anaphylactic reaction or angioedema or hypersensitivity to estradiol and levonorgestrel; hepatic impairment or disease; and protein C, protein S, or antithrombin deficiency, or other thrombophilic disorders. The most common adverse reactions (greater than or equal to 5%) are: application site reaction, vaginal bleeding, breast pain, upper respiratory infection, back pain, depression, pain, headache and flu syndrome. In the U.S., nine out of 10 prescriptions filled are for generic drugs. Increasing the availability of generic drugs helps to create competition in the marketplace, which then helps to make treatment more affordable and increases access to healthcare for more patients. Learn more about the FDA Drug Competition Action Plan . Climara Pro is a registered trademark of Bayer. The FDA approved Zydus Pharmaceuticals (USA) Inc.’s Estradiol and Levonorgestrel Transdermal System. Please contact the manufacturer for information about the medicine’s availability. title: October 20, 2026 - FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Chronic Hepatitis B Treatment
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Chronic Hepatitis B Treatment New treatment may allow some patients to maintain viral control after stopping all hepatitis B therapy For Immediate Release: October 20, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) injection, in combination with existing antiviral therapy, to treat chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in certain adults without cirrhosis. Hibsago is the first FDA-approved antisense oligonucleotide to treat chronic hepatitis B. Hibsago is approved for certain adults without cirrhosis who have been taking HBV antiviral therapy for at least six months, have suppressed levels of HBV in their blood and have hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) levels of 3,000 IU/mL or less, as determined by an FDA-authorized test. “For many people living with chronic hepatitis B, treatment can mean taking antiviral medication for years to keep the virus suppressed,” said Wendy Carter, DO, Acting Director of the Office of Infectious Diseases in the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “Hibsago provides a new treatment approach that gives some patients the possibility of maintaining control of the virus after all chronic HBV treatment has ended. This approval represents an important advance for people living with this serious disease.” Chronic hepatitis B is a long-term liver infection caused by HBV. Over time, the infection can lead to serious liver disease, including cirrhosis, and increase the risk of liver cancer. Hibsago works by targeting the genetic instructions the virus uses to make copies of itself and viral proteins, helping reduce the amount of virus and hepatitis B surface antigen in the body. The FDA also authorized the Roche Elecsys HBsAg II quant II RxDx assay as a companion diagnostic device to aid in the selection of patients with chronic HBV infection for treatment with antiviral therapy in accordance with the FDA approved drug labeling and to assist in monitoring patients throughout the course of treatment. Researchers studied Hibsago in two clinical trials that compared it with a placebo, an inactive treatment. Hibsago is injected under the skin for up to 24 weeks. Patients take it alongside their existing hepatitis B medicine and continue that medicine for at least 24 weeks after their last Hibsago injection. Some patients may then be able to stop their existing medicine if they meet certain health and lab test requirements. Across the two trials, 24% of patients who received Hibsago met the requirements to stop their existing medicine, compared with none who received placebo. Twenty-four weeks after stopping all hepatitis B treatment, 19% of patients who received Hibsago still had the virus under control, and a protein that signals hepatitis B infection (HBsAg) could not be detected in their blood. Hibsago has a boxed warning for serious liver reactions as well as low platelet counts, which can increase the risk of potentially life-threatening bleeding. Hibsago also has warnings for worsening kidney function, serious inflammatory adverse reactions like vasculitis, and serious risks if the injection is not administered properly. Patients need regular blood tests and follow up with their healthcare provider before and during treatment to monitor these risks. The most common side effects, excluding laboratory abnormalities, are injection site reactions, fever, fatigue and headache. The FDA granted Hibsago Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy designations as well as Priority Review . The approval was granted to GSK plc. title: National Republican Senatorial Committee v. Federal Election Comm’n
U.S. Treasury Identifies $270 Million in Suspicious Activity Linked to Federal Student Aid Fraud
body: October 19, 2026 FinCEN Refers Findings to Federal Investigators to Combat Fraud and Protect Taxpayer Dollars WASHINGTON - The U.S. Department of the Treasury announced today that its Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has identified approximately $270 million in suspicious financial activity potentially linked to fraud against federal student aid programs. FinCEN has referred these findings to federal investigators to pursue potential fraud schemes targeting federal student aid programs and help ensure those responsible are held accountable. These referrals underscore the Trump Administration’s commitment to eliminating fraud, protecting taxpayers, and safeguarding the integrity of federal student aid programs. “Federal student aid is intended to expand educational opportunities, not line the pockets of fraudsters who steal from students pursuing their education and hardworking taxpayers,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent . “The Trump Administration will not tolerate criminals who exploit government programs for personal gain. Treasury is working with financial institutions and law enforcement to identify these fraud schemes, recover stolen funds, and hold those responsible accountable.” “Federal student aid is meant to support students, not fraudsters. That is exactly why we introduced the new FAFSA fraud detection tool earlier this year, which stops fraud at the start of the federal student aid process,” said Education Secretary Linda McMahon. “We are proud to partner with the White House Task Force to combat fraud, waste, and abuse across these critical programs – already saving American taxpayers more than $2 billion in less than 2 years!” In a July 2026 Alert , FinCEN warned financial institutions about student aid fraud and asked them to report suspicious activity. That Alert explained that schools or their payment contractors often send aid refunds by electronic bank transfer and that the payment description often includes the word “refund” along with the school’s name or initials. The Alert also noted that fraudsters often move stolen aid through money mules, shell companies, and fake accounts to hide the source of the money. These red flags help financial institutions spot suspicious payments and report them to FinCEN in suspicious activity reports, as required by the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA). Financial institutions have filed nearly 100 suspicious activity reports since the July Alert. FinCEN’s review of these reports identified more than 20,000 potentially suspicious transactions since February 2026. These reports reflect suspicious activity that has been identified and reported by financial institutions and, therefore, should not be considered a complete representation of the scope of any particular type of suspicious activity.  Accordingly, FinCEN has referred this information to law enforcement as tip-and-lead information for further investigation. Federal student aid fraud schemes often involve fraudulent enrollments designed to divert financial assistance away from legitimate students. In “ghost student” schemes, criminals steal personal information, such as names and Social Security numbers, and use it to enroll fake students in classes under a victim’s identity. Fraudsters may also use super intelligence to produce fake documents that blend stolen information with invented details, which creates what are known as synthetic identities that can pass identity checks. Victims, including minors, often do not know that someone has received student aid in their name. In “straw student” schemes, fraud rings pay real people for their personal information, enroll those people at a school, and then keep the aid refunds issued to them. Corrupt school employees sometimes help these rings by recruiting straw students and altering their school records. Student aid fraud drains taxpayer funds, and in some cases, keeps real students out of classes that fake enrollees have filled. Student aid fraud has real consequences for students and American taxpayers. It drains finite grant resources from deserving students, potentially prevents legitimate students from enrolling in classes occupied by fraudulent enrollees, and can leave identity theft victims responsible for debts they never incurred. As part of the Trump Administration’s efforts to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse across the federal government, Treasury is working with the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, led by Vice President Vance, and encouraging whistleblowers to report credible information involving fraud, money laundering, sanctions violations, and tax-law violations. Whistleblower tips, combined with financial institutions’ reporting under the Bank Secrecy Act, help Treasury and its law enforcement partners uncover criminal networks, recover taxpayer funds, and hold bad actors accountable. Treasury will continue to leverage financial intelligence, strengthen coordination across government, and pursue those who seek to profit by defrauding American taxpayers and harming legitimate students. ###

title: October 19, 2026 - FDA Approves Immunotherapy That May Allow Certain Patients with Rectal Cancer to Avoid Chemotherapy, Radiation and Surgery
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves Immunotherapy That May Allow Certain Patients with Rectal Cancer to Avoid Chemotherapy, Radiation and Surgery For Immediate Release: October 19, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval for a new use of the immunotherapy Jemperli (dostarlimab-gxly) that may allow some patients with locally advanced rectal cancer to avoid common treatments that can have a lasting impact on their daily life. Patients with locally advanced rectal cancer often receive chemotherapy and radiation prior to surgery, which can affect bowel, urinary, and sexual function, as well as fertility. Surgery also carries risks of serious, sometimes life-threatening complications, including poor healing and leaks where the bowel is reconnected, and in some patients, permanent colostomy. “The FDA is committed to closing the gap between scientific progress and patient access, and that commitment has to show up not just in policy, but in the pace of our work,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “American patients deserve timely access to innovative treatments, and the Trump Administration is making that a reality. Completing this review nearly 4 months ahead of schedule means some patients who might otherwise be preparing for surgery, radiation or chemotherapy may now have a different conversation with their doctor.” Today’s approval is for Jemperli used alone in adults with previously untreated stage II or stage III locally advanced rectal cancer. At these stages, the cancer has grown into nearby tissue or reached nearby lymph nodes but has not spread to distant organs. To be eligible, patients’ tumors must be mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) or microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H), as determined by an FDA-authorized test. Published estimates suggest that approximately 3% of locally advanced rectal cancers are dMMR or MSI-H. Both terms describe a defect in the way cancer cells correct errors when copying their DNA. Normally, a built-in repair system catches and fixes these mistakes. When the system does not work properly, errors accumulate and create proteins the immune system can recognize, making these tumors particularly vulnerable to immunotherapy. Jemperli works by blocking a signal that cancer cells use to shield themselves from the immune system. Specifically, it targets a protein called PD-1 on immune cells. “Standard treatment for rectal cancer has major life-changing effects. For certain types of rectal cancer, this approval represents a groundbreaking option that avoids surgery, radiation and chemotherapy. This represents a significant benefit for patients and their families,” said Angelo de Claro, M.D., director of the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence . “The FDA is acting on emerging evidence to bring new approaches to patients sooner, while requiring further studies to confirm that these treatments provide lasting benefits.” The FDA based its decision on interim results from AZUR-1 ( NCT05723562 ), a phase 2 study evaluating Jemperli alone in 154 patients with previously untreated dMMR or MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer. In the study, patients received up to nine doses of Jemperli, given every 3 weeks over 6 months. After a median follow-up of more than 2 years — meaning at least half of patients had been monitored for that long — almost three-fourths of patients had not needed surgery, radiotherapy or chemotherapy. Longer follow-up is needed to understand the duration of response and how often the cancer returns. An earlier study at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center ( NCT04165772 ) evaluated Jemperli alone in 50 patients with previously untreated dMMR or MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer. None of the patients had detectable signs of cancer after Jemperli treatment, and nearly all patients (93%) maintained that cancer-free status for at least 12 months. Of the 27 patients followed for at least 3 years, only one had their cancer return, and it recurred in the same area. Jemperli can cause the immune system to attack healthy organs and tissues. These reactions can be severe or fatal. The most common side effects, reported in at least 15% of patients treated for this type of rectal cancer, were fatigue, rash, diarrhea and itching. The FDA granted Priority Review to the application and Breakthrough Therapy designation to Jemperli for the treatment of dMMR or MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer. This action marks the 11th approval of a drug reviewed under the Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher pilot program , which aims to help accelerate the review of therapies that address national public health priorities. Because this is an accelerated approval based on interim trial results, the sponsor must continue following patients to show these responses create lasting clinical benefit. The approval was granted to GSK. title: Treasury International Capital Data for August 2026
body: October 16, 2026 WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury today released Treasury International Capital (TIC) data for August 2026.  The next release, which will report on data for September 2026, is scheduled for November 18, 2026. The sum total in August of all net foreign acquisitions of long-term securities, short-term U.S. securities, and banking flows was a net TIC inflow of $199.8 billion.  Of this, net foreign private inflows were $178.5 billion, and net foreign official inflows were $21.3 billion. Foreign residents increased their holdings of long-term U.S. securities in August; their net purchases were $300.7 billion.  Net purchases by private foreign investors were $257.8 billion, and net purchases by foreign official institutions were $42.9 billion. U.S. residents increased their holdings of long-term foreign securities, with net purchases of $21.6 billion. After including adjustments, such as estimated foreign portfolio acquisitions of U.S. stocks through stock swaps, overall net foreign purchases of long-term securities are estimated to have been $279.2 billion in August. Foreign residents decreased their holdings of U.S. Treasury bills by $47.8 billion.  Foreign resident holdings of all dollar-denominated short-term U.S. securities and other custody liabilities decreased by $37.8 billion. Banks’ own net dollar-denominated liabilities to foreign residents decreased by $41.6 billion. Complete data are available on the Treasury website here . ### About TIC Data The monthly data on holdings of long-term securities, as well as the monthly table on Major Foreign Holders of Treasury Securities, reflect foreign holdings of U.S. securities collected primarily on the basis of custodial data.  These data help provide a window into foreign ownership of U.S. securities, but they cannot attribute holdings of U.S. securities with complete accuracy.  For example, if a U.S. Treasury security purchased by a foreign resident is held in a custodial account in a third country, the true ownership of the security will not be reflected in the data.  The custodial data will also not properly attribute U.S. Treasury securities managed by foreign private portfolio managers who invest on behalf of residents of other countries.  In addition, foreign countries may hold dollars and other U.S. assets that are not captured in the TIC data.  For these reasons, it is difficult to draw precise conclusions from TIC data about changes in the foreign holdings of U.S. financial assets by individual countries. Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iranian Regime’s Abuse of Religious Charity Networks
body: October 15, 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued an Alert asking financial institutions to report potential Iranian regime abuse of religious charity networks, including diversion of religious tithes, or khums . “Under President Trump’s leadership, Treasury will not allow the Iranian regime to continue its long history of abusing religious institutions to line the pockets of its elites and fund terrorism,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent . “By identifying and reporting this potential abuse, financial institutions can provide law enforcement with critical information to isolate the Iranian regime and its financial enablers.” The Iranian regime has been known to abuse ostensibly religious organizations in Iran and neighboring countries to enrich its elites, fund the repression of the Iranian people, and support terrorism abroad. In addition, the regime co-opts khums payments from the global Shi’a community to further its destabilizing activities*.*  In some cases, organizations that collect these payments do so on behalf of prominent Iranian ayatollahs with ties to the regime. These entities may use informal financial channels like hawalas and cash couriers to remit the funds to Iran or to Iran-linked actors. FinCEN’s Alert includes red flag indicators to aid financial institutions in detecting, preventing, and reporting this illicit activity. Indicators of Potential Iranian Abuse of Religious Charities A charitable organization or nonprofit organization (NPO) solicits donations but does not appear to provide any charitable services, or openly supports the Iranian regime or its terrorist proxies, such as in fundraising appeals or on social media. A charitable organization or NPO receives large donations from an unknown source over a short period of time and then sends significant wire transfers or checks to other charitable organizations or NPOs. A charitable organization or NPO, or the customer’s employee, engages in behavior suggesting efforts to evade certain reporting or recordkeeping requirements. A customer receives transfers from a charitable organization or NPO with which the customer has no clear business relationship, and then the customer proceeds to withdraw the funds in cash or remit them onward. FinCEN recognizes that legitimate charities should have access to financial services and can transmit funds through transparent channels.  FinCEN reminds banks to apply a risk-based approach to customer due diligence requirements when developing the risk profiles of charities and other non-profit customers, as discussed in the Joint Fact Sheet on Bank Secrecy Act Due Diligence Requirements for Charities and Non-Profit Organizations . ###
